7 meters above the water.The abutments use rock on both banks as foundation, built up with dressed stone.

Diagonal timber bracing frames are interlocked to form the arch, with round logs as beams and transverse planks as the deck.

The covered hall has a hip-and-gable roof with four-column nine-purlin beam-lifting timber frame, 11 bays and 48 columns.

A shrine in the central bay worships the Xuan Tian Great Emperor.Guardrails with wind-and-rain shields line both sides.

Tangli Bridge's internal structure is simple, with no bracket sets (dougong); no steles around the bridge, no inscriptions inside — only some slogans.

From the interior alone, signs of recent construction are fairly obvious.The surrounding environment is good, with no major environmental damage, except that a highway is being built across the way.

推荐级别：★★★★

三溪桥

No.36
Sanxi Bridge
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：福州市闽侯县大湖乡坂头村与六锦村之间
类型：桥梁·木拱桥
特征标签 Highlights
木拱桥结构工匠线索桥村关系古道线索廊屋题跋楹联张业阁撰书
中文 Chinese

三溪桥位于闽侯县大湖乡坂头村与六锦村之间，到达坂头村后有路标指示六锦方向10公里，行走大约一半见一水库大坝，向大坝下游即库区相反方向望去，三溪桥在溪底的绿树丛荫中依稀可辨。三溪桥外观略显陈旧，风雨板有缺失，顶部未作任何装饰，外形端庄古朴。三溪桥又称藜峰桥，清道光二十五年（1845年）建。

单孔木拱廊屋桥，跨于雪溪、院里溪和东溪等三溪汇流处，南北走向，长32米，宽5.4米。桥建在悬崖峭壁间，桥堍假以峭壁巨石为基，用花岗岩条石垒砌承架。桥梁拱架用27根粗大杉木均分三组，每组9根并排穿插而成，作拱状。木拱上铺设圆木为梁。

桥面上建木构廊屋，廊屋面阔12间，抬梁式木构架用四柱，悬山顶。桥面横铺木板，两侧置木倚栏，檐下置遮雨板，廊内设长凳，桥头供奉佛像。

三溪桥的特点是廊屋内梁檩之上题跋极多，有关于桥建设的，有参禅敬佛的，有吟咏山水的，还有毛主席语录，各时期内容丰富，足见三溪桥所在之处也是一人文荟萃之地。立柱梁枋均撰书楹联，有"鳌梁高架仿疑虹见空中，鸟路斜临却讶龙邻井上"；"此地疑文王避雨处，前溪忆子路问津时"；"慧眼逢人能效杞桥进履，违心下士曾知渭水推车"；"再行数武算庄村处处家家极乎快极乎快，一望三山遮草木高高下下如此奇如此奇"等。

相传三溪桥上所有楹联均为罗源名秀才张业阁撰书，令人称奇的是时隔这么多年，梁柱上的墨迹依然清晰可辨。与营造最关紧要的，是廊屋脊檩上墨书"大清道光二十五年岁次壬寅蒲月吉旦立，主绳墨罗邑霍口周光连春"。三溪桥周边环境本来上佳，可惜近年于近在咫尺处修建一水库大坝，使三溪桥的景观和安全受到较大影响。

English

Sanxi Bridge stands between Bantou Village and Liujin Village in Dahu Township, Minhou County.

From Bantou Village, a sign indicates 10 kilometers toward Liujin; about halfway, a reservoir dam appears — looking downstream from the dam (opposite the reservoir), Sanxi Bridge is faintly visible among green trees at the stream bottom.

Its appearance is slightly weathered, with missing wind-and-rain boards and no decoration on top, dignified and ancient in form.

Also known as Lifeng Bridge, it was built in 1845 (the 25th year of Daoguang reign, Qing).

A single-span timber-arch covered bridge spanning the confluence of three streams — Xue Stream, Yuanli Stream, and Dong Stream — it runs north-south, 32 meters long and 5.

4 meters wide.Built between sheer cliffs, its abutments use cliff boulders as foundation, with granite dressed stones laid to support the frame.

The arch frame uses 27 large Chinese fir logs divided into three groups of 9, interlocked side by side in arch form.Round logs are laid as beams above the arch.

A timber covered hall stands on the deck, 12 bays wide with four-column beam-lifting frame and overhanging gable roof.

The deck is planked transversely, with wooden leaning rails on both sides, rain boards under the eaves, long benches inside, and Buddha statues at the bridgehead.

Sanxi Bridge's distinctive feature is the abundance of inscriptions on its beams and purlins: about bridge construction, about Zen worship, about landscape poetry, even Chairman Mao quotations — rich content from various periods, showing this was also a culturally vibrant place.

Columns and beams bear couplets, such as "The ao-beam rises high, seemingly a rainbow in the sky; the bird path slants nearby, startling as a dragon beside the well" and "This place seems where King Wen took shelter from rain; the stream ahead recalls when Zilu asked the way.

" Legend says all couplets were composed and written by Zhang Yege, a famous xiucai (provincial graduate) from Luoyuan — remarkably, after so many years, the ink on beams and columns remains clearly legible.

Most importantly for construction, the ridge purlin bears ink inscription: "Erected on an auspicious day in the fifth month of the Renyin year, the 25th year of Daoguang reign of the Great Qing; master carpenter Zhou Guang Lianchun from Huokou, Luoyi.

" The surrounding environment was originally excellent, but unfortunately a reservoir dam built nearby in recent years has significantly affected the bridge's landscape and safety.

推荐级别：★★★★★

雪峰崇圣禅寺

No.37
Chongsheng Zen Temple on Xuefeng Mountain
级别：国家级重点佛教寺院
年代：清
地址：福州市闽侯县大湖乡境内福古线旁雪峰山
类型：宗教建筑·木结构·石作
特征标签 Highlights
早期石作遗迹清末木作南方丛林第一义存祖师塔枯木庵唐刻
中文 Chinese

雪峰崇圣禅寺，位于闽侯县大湖乡境内福古线旁雪峰山，距福州市区76公里，始建于唐咸通十一年（870年），开山祖师是著名高僧义存。1983年被国务院列为全国重点佛教寺院，素有"南方丛林第一"之美誉。宋代时，天下著名禅寺按等级列为"五山十刹"，雪峰寺名列十刹之首。

至明代，四大名山代替五山十刹，雪峰寺仍有广泛影响，清代雪峰寺被列为五大丛林之一，现有的建筑格局多为清光绪年间中兴雪峰寺的达本禅师所定。

雪峰崇圣禅寺现存主要建筑有内外山门、放生池、天王殿、大雄宝殿、法堂、禅堂、藏经楼、伽蓝殿、祖师堂、客堂、钟鼓楼、方丈室、枯木庵、留香堂、尊客堂等，占地面积约73000平方米。第一进院落主要建筑为天王殿（山门），封火山墙，檐下斗拱颇具特色。殿内空间高敞。

殿后有放生池，以桥通大雄宝殿前庭院。第二进院落轴线建筑为大雄宝殿，重檐歇山顶，前廊明间镂雕蟠龙石柱，花窗圆形，嵌各色花牙子，甚为可爱。法堂前西北角有义存祖师塔。

为寺内最古之文物，唐天祐四年（907年）建。高4.1米，底径2.9米，塔亭为后建。寺东南数百米有枯木庵，庵内存枯木一段，内壁有唐天祐年间题刻。"崇圣禅寺"匾额系赵朴初居士题写，楹联也多为名人名家撰书。

寺内至今还保存有经书、法器、彩瓷、书画等文物，其中义存祖师开山玉印、血书、印度梵文《贝叶经》、八千余卷《频迦藏经》、《碛砂全藏》、唐檀木雕观音、清缅甸国王赠送翡翠玉雕佛像等，均为稀世珍宝。雪峰寺外表颇有稚嫩感，但内部构件仍多清代旧作。

寺院香火很旺，很多出家人在此修持。大殿内佛像端然严整，寺院并提供素斋和很多佛学书籍，佛事很盛，确为弘扬佛法的清净之所。

English

Chongsheng Zen Temple on Xuefeng Mountain stands beside the Fugu Road in Dahu Township, Minhou County, 76 kilometers from downtown Fuzhou.

Founded in 870 (the 11th year of Xiantong reign, Tang), its founding patriarch was the renowned monk Yicun.

Listed as a National Key Buddhist Temple by the State Council in 1983, it has long been praised as the "Number One Monastery of the South.

" In the Song Dynasty, when famous Zen temples were ranked as "Five Mountains and Ten Monasteries," Xuefeng Temple ranked first among the ten.

In the Ming, the Four Great Mountains replaced the Five Mountains and Ten Monasteries, but Xuefeng remained influential; in the Qing it was listed as one of the Five Great Monasteries.

Its current layout was largely established by Master Daben, who revived Xuefeng during the Guangxu reign.

Existing buildings include inner and outer gates, a free-life pond, Heavenly King Hall, Mahavira Hall, Dharma Hall, Zen Hall, Scripture Library, Qielan Hall, Patriarch Hall, guest hall, bell and drum towers, abbot's quarters, Kumu Nunnery, Liuxiang Hall, and Zunke Hall, covering about 73,000 square meters.

The first courtyard's main building is the Heavenly King Hall (gate), with fire-sealing gable walls and distinctive eave bracket sets.Its interior is spacious.

Behind it lies the free-life pond, connected by a bridge to the Mahavira Hall courtyard.

The Mahavira Hall has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof; the central bay of its front porch features carved dragon-coiled stone columns, with circular lattice windows inset with colorful floral brackets.

At the northwest corner before the Dharma Hall stands the Patriarch Yicun Pagoda — the temple's oldest relic, built in 907 (the fourth year of Tianyou reign, Tang).It stands 4.

1 meters tall with a base diameter of 2.9 meters; its pavilion is a later addition.

Several hundred meters southeast is Kumu Nunnery, containing a section of dead wood with Tang Dynasty (Tianyou reign) inscriptions on its inner wall.

The "Chongsheng Zen Temple" plaque was written by Zhao Puchu, and many couplets were composed by famous scholars.

The temple preserves scriptures, ritual implements, colored porcelain, calligraphy, and paintings — including Patriarch Yicun's founding jade seal, blood-script sutras, Indian Sanskrit palm-leaf scriptures, over 8,000 volumes of the Pinjia Canon, the Qisha Canon, a Tang sandalwood carving of Guanyin, and a jade Buddha statue presented by the King of Burma in the Qing — all rare treasures.

Though the exterior appears somewhat new, many interior components are still Qing originals.The temple has thriving incense, with many monks practicing here.

The Buddha statues in the Mahavira Hall are solemn and dignified; the temple provides vegetarian meals and many Buddhist books, with active religious ceremonies — truly a pure place for propagating the Dharma.

推荐级别：★★★

远济桥

No.38
Yuanji Bridge
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：福州市闽侯县白沙镇联坑村
类型：桥梁·木拱桥
特征标签 Highlights
木拱桥结构活遗产的作品古道风光郑多金老人重修
中文 Chinese

一路闽江风光，寻找位于闽侯县白沙镇联坑村的远济桥。公路边有一数百米长的青石古道，沿着古道蜿蜒而下，经过一处小庙，远济桥的身影便出现在眼前。远济桥又名壹佰桥。

建于清光绪（1875—1908年）年间，单孔木拱廊桥，南北走向，全长32.4米、宽5米、距溪底20米。桥堍以天然岩石为基，用块石垒砌而成。

用圆木穿插交错成多组拱架，上顺铺圆木为梁，再横铺木板为桥面。廊屋歇山顶，穿斗式木构架，面阔十一间，进深四柱。

原桥东头有清光绪年间（1875—1908年）侯官县进士陈景韶撰写隶书"远济桥"木雕桥匾，并阴刻方寸行书跋文，详细记载建桥历史背景、时间，现已不在桥头，可能被有关部门另外保管。远济桥曾经落架大修，工程总负责是国家级非物质文化遗产木拱桥营造技艺传承人，寿宁县郑多金老人。

远观重修后远济桥桥体工艺严整，桥护板不缺，上部无风雨板，廊屋顶部属新建，装饰带闽地风格。

English

Following the Min River scenery, one seeks Yuanji Bridge in Liankeng Village, Baisha Town, Minhou County.

Beside the road runs a several-hundred-meter-long bluestone ancient path; winding down it past a small temple, Yuanji Bridge comes into view.

Also known as Yibai Bridge (One-Hundred Bridge), it was built during the Guangxu reign of the Qing (1875-1908).

A single-span timber-arch covered bridge running north-south, it is 32.4 meters long, 5 meters wide, and 20 meters above the stream bed.

The abutments use natural rock as foundation, built up with dressed stone.Round logs are interlocked into multiple arch frames, with lengthwise logs as beams and transverse planks as the deck.

The covered hall has a hip-and-gable roof with column-and-tie timber frame, 11 bays wide and 4 columns deep.

Originally at the east end stood a wooden bridge plaque with clerical script "Yuanji Bridge" composed by Chen Jingshao, a jinshi from Houguan County during the Guangxu reign, with intaglio running-script colophons detailing the bridge's historical background and construction date.

It is no longer at the bridgehead, possibly stored elsewhere by authorities.

Yuanji Bridge underwent a major dismantling and restoration, led by Zheng Duojin, an elderly craftsman from Shouning County and national-level intangible cultural heritage inheritor of timber-arch bridge construction.

Viewed from afar, the restored bridge has rigorous craftsmanship, intact side boards, no wind-and-rain boards on the upper part, and a newly built covered hall roof with Min-style decoration.

推荐级别：★★★★

凤凰寺大殿

No.39
Main Hall of Fenghuang Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：福州市永泰县同安镇洋头村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
残留的原始木构做法明万历题记四瓣拼料柱麻绳纹替木
中文 Chinese

不巧，或者是刚巧，走访永泰凤凰寺的时候赶上大修。大修的规模让我心惊。按照大殿题记上的说法，历史上"万历岁次己未（1619年）腊月吉旦，僧惟融重新鼎建"。2013年的大工程距离"重新鼎建"是不远了。大殿坐北朝南，门前院落朝东开小门，门样式颇晚近，疑为后来改造的结果。

大殿单檐歇山顶，面阔七间，进深六间，屋顶坡度较缓和，有早期建筑特征。殿内三世佛座为石构，刻"万历辛丑年（1601）仲夏吉日造"的字样，后人填描了艳丽的红色，不过尚可看出须弥座之莲瓣纹饰颇具本地特色。座上佛像均为晚近新换。

另外还保留着重修碑记两通，一个是明崇祯辛巳岁二月"凤凰寺觉印师功德碑"，另一通是大清乾隆庚寅碑。得以探勘工地现场，了解到柱、椽望、梁架等绝大部分构件已经新换，唯前廊尚存前檐铺作等部分原始构件。前后檐梁架做法不同，前檐较复杂。明间梁架中柱不落地。前廊隔架科与檩之间替木底面刻作麻绳纹，似摹拟凤尾然。

拆换下来的柱子截面可见为四瓣拼料，有四块和八块两种拼法。

English

Unfortunately — or perhaps fortunately — our visit to Yongtai's Fenghuang Temple coincided with a major restoration.The scale of the work was startling.

According to the hall's inscription, historically "in the twelfth month of an auspicious day in the Jiwei year of Wanli (1619), Monk Weirong completely rebuilt it.

" The 2013 major project is not far from a "complete rebuilding" itself.

The main hall faces south, with a small door opening east in the front courtyard; the door style is quite late, likely a later modification.

The hall has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, seven bays wide and six deep, with a relatively gentle roof slope — an early architectural feature.

The three-Buddha throne inside is stone, inscribed "Built on an auspicious day in the fifth month of the Xinchou year of Wanli (1601)," later repainted in vivid red, though the lotus-petal ornamentation of the xumizuo still shows distinctive local character.

The Buddha statues on the throne are all recent replacements.

Two restoration steles survive: one from the second month of the Xinsi year of Chongzhen (1641), "Merit Stele of Master Jueyin of Fenghuang Temple," and another from the Gengyin year of Qianlong in the Qing.

Exploring the construction site revealed that most components — columns, rafters, beams — have been replaced, with only the front porch retaining some original components such as the front-eave bracket sets.

The front and rear eave beam frames differ in method, the front being more complex.The central column of the central bay's beam frame does not reach the ground.

Between the front porch's inter-bay brackets and purlins, the underside of the substitute timber (timu) is carved with hemp-rope patterns, seemingly imitating phoenix tails.

The cross-section of removed columns shows they were assembled from four segments, in both four-piece and eight-piece configurations.

推荐级别：★★

名山室

No.40
Mingshan Stone Chambers
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：北宋
地址：福州市永泰县樟洋镇院里村西南2公里
类型：宗教建筑·木结构·石作
特征标签 Highlights
早期木作石作宋元造像宋代木构祖师殿白莲教七祖图崇宁二年须弥座
中文 Chinese

高盖山，被誉为"永泰第一山"，海拔近千米。山路崎岖，竹林掩映。半山腰上坐落着名山室。名山室的前身叫作高盖名山院，始建于唐文德元年（888年）。五代后唐天成年间（927—930年）闽王王延钧赐额为"名山室"，沿用至今。

宋元经明清至民国间屡有修建和兴废。在这样的地方架木结构，正是因借了山体和山洞。名山室由南向北，在岩洞中建木构建筑，又以岩洞为主要空间，由主体岩洞（观音洞）、东室（灵龟洞）、西室（金水洞又称血盆洞，观音洞）组成。

崖壁见也浸染着人文气息。东室保存有一组石窟像艺术，佛教故事之外，更有一幅七比丘图，被专家疑为宋代的白莲教七祖图。西室的金水洞则为古建筑界大力推崇，那是一座宋代木构。

此建筑名为祖师殿，面阔一间，进深二间，六根檐柱皆石柱，截面八楞状，柱身阳刻出线脚，柱间用石地袱，其余梁架均木构。北宋木构十余年前曾经大修，更换瓦面，此后再无修缮。殿中有石质须弥座，其上立尊二，胁侍二。

须弥座当为宋代遗物，正面束腰有铭文："崇宁二年二月十一日题。"其余三面束腰刻狮子，四角雕力士。正面上枭刻云头纹，其余三面皆莲瓣。须弥座前又有石香炉及石供桌，当为同时期所造。石香炉题刻："县城陈仁长叶室中林四小娘敬造。"无年款。周身雕饰花卉及动物纹。

观音洞内筑小石室，内置石质须弥座，供北宋石雕观音像一尊。今洞内石像为复制品，安全考虑，真品已移至室内保存。不枉攀登的曲折，不枉忍受嘈杂加建的经程，朝圣一般地目睹祖师殿真容的时候，感叹再多等待也是值得的。让我们测绘它吧。

English

Gaogai Mountain, hailed as the "Number One Mountain of Yongtai," stands nearly 1,000 meters above sea level.The mountain path is rugged, shaded by bamboo.

Halfway up sits Mingshan Stone Chambers.

Its predecessor, called Gaogai Mingshan Yuan, was founded in 888 (the first year of Wende reign, Tang).

During the Tiancheng reign of the Later Tang (927-930), King Yanjun of Min bestowed the name "Mingshan Shi" (Mingshan Chambers), which has been used ever since.

From the Song and Yuan through the Ming, Qing, and Republican periods, it was repeatedly built, abandoned, and restored.

Building timber structures in such a place leverages the mountain body and caves.

Mingshan Chambers runs south to north, with timber buildings constructed inside rock caves, using the caves as primary spaces.

It comprises the main cave (Guanyin Cave), East Chamber (Linggui Cave), and West Chamber (Jinshui Cave, also called Xuepen Cave or Guanyin Cave).The cliff walls are imbued with humanistic atmosphere.

The East Chamber preserves a group of cave sculptures: besides Buddhist narratives, there is a depiction of seven bhikkhus, suspected by experts to be the Seven Patriarchs of the White Lotus Sect from the Song Dynasty.

The West Chamber's Jinshui Cave is highly regarded in architectural circles — it contains a Song Dynasty timber structure.

This building, called the Patriarch Hall, is one bay wide and two deep, with six eave columns all of stone, octagonal in section with positive moldings on the shafts; stone ground sills connect the columns, while the remaining beam frames are timber.

The Northern Song timber structure underwent major repairs over a decade ago, with the roof tiles replaced, and has not been repaired since.

Inside the hall stands a stone xumizuo, with two main figures and two attendant figures.

The xumizuo is likely a Song relic: its front waist bears the inscription "Inscribed on the 11th day of the second month of the second year of Chongning (1103).

" The other three sides of the waist are carved with lions, and the four corners with guardian figures.The front upper molding has cloud-head patterns, while the other three sides have lotus petals.

Before the xumizuo stand a stone incense burner and stone offering table, likely from the same period.

The incense burner is inscribed: "Respectfully made by Chen Renchang of the county seat and Lin Siniang of Yeshi." No date.Its body is carved with floral and animal patterns.

Inside the Guanyin Cave, a small stone chamber contains a stone xumizuo with a Northern Song stone-carved Guanyin statue.

The statue in the cave today is a replica; the original has been moved indoors for safety.

Worthy of the winding climb and the noisy additions, when one beholds the Patriarch Hall as if on pilgrimage, one feels any amount of waiting was worthwhile.Let us survey it.

推荐级别：★★★★

嵩口古镇

No.41
Songkou Ancient Town
级别：国家级历史文化名镇
年代：清
地址：福州市永泰县嵩口镇
类型：民居·公共建筑
特征标签 Highlights
夹杂在木建筑中的石作古镇气氛和生活古码头福建第一个乡镇商会
中文 Chinese

嵩口古镇位于戴云山东麓福州市最高峰东湖尖（海拔1682米）脚下，大樟溪、长庆溪的汇流处，经历千年风雨洗礼的嵩口古码头，是闻名遐迩的人流、物流集散地，成就了嵩口三府六县水陆交通中心。

自南宋始，每月初一、十五的赶墟习俗沿续至今；至清末民初蔚为鼎盛，1914年成立了福建省第一个乡镇商会，曾自行发行纸币，自设税卡和鸦片专卖局，俨然一副都市景象。

古镇中有遗留下来的商号林立的老街，也有大大小小的祠堂，里面是族人相聚小憩的场所，更加公共一些的是镇上的妈祖庙（天后宫），装饰得热烈。镇中最常见的还是街头的小店，再有就是大大小小的古宅山庄。徜徉在嵩口的大街小巷，我们从现在留下的嵩口处处人文遗迹，也可以想象嵩口当年的热闹富庶。

透过窗户，看到的是白墙青瓦，很多古迹有幸历经风雨得以存留下来，但处在目前的社会背景下，古建筑的保护面临新的问题，甚至比以前各个时期更为严峻。希望嵩口的古建筑得以更好保存，也使这个时代的发展借鉴古建筑的精髓，中国古代的人文精神得以发扬，从而达到真正的和谐境界。

English

Songkou Ancient Town lies at the eastern foot of the Daiyun Mountains, beneath Donghujian — Fuzhou's highest peak at 1,682 meters above sea level — at the confluence of the Dazhang Stream and Changqing Stream.

The Songkou ancient wharf, weathered by a thousand years of wind and rain, was a renowned hub for people and goods, making Songkou the water-and-land transportation center for three prefectures and six counties.

From the Southern Song onward, the market-day custom on the first and fifteenth of each lunar month has continued to this day.

It reached its peak in the late Qing and early Republican periods; in 1914, Fujian's first township chamber of commerce was established here, which once issued its own paper currency, set up its own tax checkpoints and opium monopoly — resembling a small city.

The ancient town preserves old streets lined with shops, as well as ancestral halls of various sizes where clans gather and rest.

More public is the town's Mazu Temple (Tianhou Palace), decorated vibrantly.

Most common are the small street-side shops, followed by ancient mansions and mountain villas of various sizes.

Wandering Songkou's streets and alleys, the surviving humanistic traces everywhere allow one to imagine the town's former prosperity.

Through windows, one sees white walls and black tiles; many ancient relics have survived the storms, but in today's social context, the protection of ancient buildings faces new challenges — perhaps more severe than in any previous period.

One hopes Songkou's ancient buildings can be better preserved, and that this era's development can draw on the essence of ancient architecture, allowing the humanistic spirit of ancient China to flourish and achieve true harmony.

推荐级别：★★★

嵩口古镇古宅一

No.42
Old House I in Songkou Ancient Town
级别：国家级历史文化名镇
年代：清
地址：福州永泰县嵩口镇
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构贴金窗扇雕饰繁复斗拱
中文 Chinese

流经嵩口镇的大樟溪是安静的。曾经的嵩口是一个繁华的水陆大码头。这里商人云集，聚集了财富便在附近购置房产，并且精心装饰，以至于现在留下的清代大宅星罗棋布分布在嵩口周边各个村庄。根据主人的偏好和当时的条件所限，有的宅院伫立在很醒目的位置，有的却很低调，不大引起人们的注意，然走进里面却是别有洞天。绿树掩映下的古民居，深藏在村落中很不起眼的位置。

安闲的下午，向导随意引领我们推开一座古宅的大门。回头就是村中鹅卵石铺就的古路。庭院深深，大有一眼望不到头的意思。庭院中摆满了农作物加工品，贴金的和雕刻精美的窗扇诉说着往日辉煌，雕饰繁复的斗拱和屋架是昨日标榜的话题。

在嵩口这样的老宅还有很多，看得多了也难免审美疲劳，因为每所宅院的内部构造基本大同小异，不过对于古建筑发烧友来说可以说是一块乐土，尽可以一座一座细细考察品评。另外一个不当说的问题，广泛存在于各个古建筑聚集地，就是镇中心实际上已经新楼林立，村民自家新建的楼也是现代样式居多，那些前人留下的不可复制的宝贵遗产正在受到日益严重的冲击。

English

The Dazhang Stream flowing through Songkou Town is quiet.Songkou was once a bustling water-and-land wharf.

Merchants gathered here, and with accumulated wealth they purchased properties nearby and decorated them meticulously — so much so that surviving Qing Dynasty mansions are scattered like stars across the villages around Songkou.

Depending on the owners' preferences and the conditions of the time, some mansions stand in prominent positions while others remain low-key, barely drawing attention — yet stepping inside reveals a world of its own.

Ancient residences shaded by green trees lie hidden in inconspicuous spots within the villages.On a leisurely afternoon, our guide casually led us to push open the gate of an old mansion.

Behind us lay the village's cobblestone ancient path.The courtyard was deep, seemingly endless.

It was filled with agricultural products; gilded and exquisitely carved window sills spoke of past glory, while ornately carved bracket sets and roof frames were once the talk of the town.

There are many such old houses in Songkou; seeing too many can lead to aesthetic fatigue, as the internal layout of each is largely similar.

Yet for ancient architecture enthusiasts, this is a paradise where one can examine and evaluate each mansion carefully.

Another issue, widespread in every ancient architecture gathering place, is that the town center is now filled with new buildings; villagers' newly constructed houses are mostly modern in style, and the irreplaceable precious heritage left by predecessors is under increasingly severe impact.

推荐级别：★★★

嵩口古镇古宅二

No.43
Old House II in Songkou Ancient Town
级别：国家级历史文化名镇
年代：明
地址：福州永泰县嵩口镇
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构粉墙填充空隙贴近人性融入自然
中文 Chinese

去往嵩口的路上，沿途能看到优美的风景和散落在青山秀水之间的古老民居。偏安于一隅的小村落，不同于名宅大厝，反倒让人觉得这样的民居更加贴近人性，更加融入自然。身在大都市，我们早已不习惯阳光灿烂而了无声息的环境，照片中的男人背着他的小孩在小路上走过，那份安逸平和令人羡慕。立于路边的一处民居，虽然老旧了一些，但看上去还是很有味道。这种把房屋的木架构裸露出来用粉墙填充空隙的做法在欧洲也很常见。

从屋里向外望去，远处的青山依稀可见，只是我们离这样的生活已经很远。遇到房屋的主人一位大姐，问她可不可以拍些照片，她很痛快的答应，并且说房子是祖上留下来的，有一百多年了。问她住在这样的老房子里是不是感觉很好，她说好什么好，住这样的房子，孩子连老婆都讨不到。看来古建筑保护固然很重要，让年轻人都能讨到老婆更重要。或者让那些能供养大家族的忙碌的富豪们来换一种别墅的口味，来这里体味一下农人的闲适？

English

On the way to Songkou, one sees beautiful scenery and ancient residences scattered among green mountains and clear waters.

Small villages tucked away in corners, unlike famous grand mansions, make one feel such dwellings are more human, more integrated with nature.

Living in a big city, we are no longer accustomed to environments of brilliant sunshine and utter silence.

In the photo, a man carries his child along a small path — that peace and contentment is enviable.A residence by the roadside, though somewhat old, still has character.

This method of exposing the timber frame and filling the gaps with whitewashed walls is also common in Europe.

Looking out from inside, distant green mountains are faintly visible — only we are already far from such a life.We met the owner, a middle-aged woman, and asked if we could take photos.

She readily agreed, saying the house was left by her ancestors and is over a hundred years old.Asked if living in such an old house feels good, she replied: "What's good about it?

Living in a house like this, my son can't even find a wife." It seems that while protecting ancient architecture is important, enabling young people to find wives is more so.

Or perhaps busy wealthy families who can support large clans should trade their villa tastes for a taste of rural leisure here?

推荐级别：★★★

嵩口古镇宁远庄

No.44
Ningyuan Village in Songkou Ancient Town
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：福州市永泰县嵩口镇月洲村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构砖石瓦作寨墙防御科举喜报
中文 Chinese

宁远庄是永泰县新发现55座明清风格古建筑之一，在距离嵩口镇5公里的月洲村，路边有张元干故居的指示牌，顺道而进便是。宁远庄有寨墙，寨墙数百米长，6米高，用近一米厚的青石块堆砌而成。

宁远庄始建于清雍正七年（1729年），费时5年才建好。建寨者张谦，生于清康熙年间，曾授文林郎。他从24岁就开始建寨，一生做了很多公益事业。闽地有很多这样的集居住和防御于一体的半封闭式建筑，建在平地的叫作"寨"，建在山上的叫作"庄"。

在进庄的门楼里，贴着近百张小纸片，上面写着某人考中贡生、进士等，落款的年代有清雍正、乾隆、咸丰等。文史专家表示，这就是宁远庄的人在科举考试中举后的京报、院报，都是当时来一张贴上一张，有的已经有几百年历史了。当然，也有一些已经遗失了。由于过去喜报要求使用相同的字体，所以，这些喜报看上去始终是一致的。目前国内还没有其他地方发现保存数量如此多的喜报，非常罕见和珍贵。

一张纸贴在户外也能保存上百年，过去的很多东西令人不解。寨墙上，见到大大小小、排列整齐的圆孔和方洞。村民说，寨墙是中空的，除了放哨眼、射枪孔外，宁远庄还设有通往寨外的地下取水暗管、地下盐仓、粮仓。从庄门向内一眼望去，可以看到正厅。"安宅在仁"的匾额面向主人所在的位置，当身处乱世，居于庄中，也许这样的心理暗示比长枪土炮可以带来更多的安全感。

比起斋墙，一切穿斗架支起的房屋，普通得让人无从追踪任何匠心，这或许就是这里的匠心，把钱花在最需要的地方——防御。不过现在一切都过去了，没有了风声鹤唳，安静平和中宁远庄也渐渐被人遗忘，有些寂寥的样子。

English

Ningyuan Village is one of 55 newly discovered Ming-Qing style ancient buildings in Yongtai County.

Located in Yuezhou Village, 5 kilometers from Songkou Town, a roadside sign for Zhang Yuangan's former residence points the way in.

Ningyuan Village has a stockade wall several hundred meters long and 6 meters high, built with bluestone blocks nearly one meter thick.

Founded in 1729 (the seventh year of Yongzheng reign, Qing), it took 5 years to complete.

The builder, Zhang Qian, was born during the Kangxi reign and was awarded the title of Wenlin Lang.He began building the stockade at age 24 and devoted his life to many public welfare projects.

Fujian has many such semi-enclosed buildings combining residence and defense: those built on flat land are called "zhai" (stockades), those on mountains are called "zhuang" (manors).

In the gate tower, nearly a hundred small paper slips are pasted, recording names of those who passed the provincial or imperial examinations, dated from the Yongzheng, Qianlong, and Xianfeng reigns.

Cultural history experts say these are the capital and provincial examination announcements for Ningyuan Village's successful candidates, pasted one by one as they arrived — some are several hundred years old, though some have been lost.

Because announcements were required to use the same typeface, they all look consistent.

No other place in China has preserved such a large number of examination announcements, making them extremely rare and precious.

A single paper pasted outdoors can survive for over a century — many things from the past are puzzling.On the stockade wall, neatly arranged round and square holes of various sizes are visible.

Villagers say the wall is hollow; besides watch slits and gun ports, Ningyuan Village also has underground water pipes leading outside, underground salt storage, and granaries.

Looking in from the gate, one sees the main hall.

The plaque "An Zhai Zai Ren" (Peaceful Dwelling in Benevolence) faces the master's position — in turbulent times, living in the village, perhaps such psychological suggestion brought more security than spears and cannons.

Compared with the stockade wall, the column-and-tie framed houses are so ordinary that one cannot trace any artistry — perhaps that is the artistry here: spending money where it was most needed — defense.

But now it's all over; without the fear of attack, in quiet peace Ningyuan Village is gradually forgotten, looking somewhat desolate.

推荐级别：★★★

嵩口古镇用坦厝

No.45
Yongtan House in Songkou Ancient Town
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：福州永泰县嵩口镇下坂村（月洲村）
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构砖石瓦作十二扇屏三进大八扇厝燕尾脊
中文 Chinese

距离嵩口镇1公里的月阙村，半高处的坪台上安静地坐落着一所大宅，俯瞰院前的田地。这就是用坦厝。用坦厝的名字有些奇怪，实际上这是以当初主人的名字命名的宅院。

因位于嵩口镇下坂村，用坦厝又称下坂厝，始建于清乾隆年间（1752年），历时27年，父建子续，先后建成，距今有257年，建筑面积5080平方米。大门之内，200多个房间，建有大厅、下落厅、横厅、书斋、内外埕、雨水井、后花园等。

它沿袭中原古民居建筑的风格特征：建筑结构以木材与土石混合为主；建筑风格，三进大八扇厝，每扇夹墙有风火墙相隔，中间大厅两侧小厅厢房对称，以一至二层楼为主，气派宏伟；屋顶斜面皆成凹曲线，两端为燕尾脊；牌楼、木雕、石雕、泥塑、彩画等装饰小品，花样繁多，以木雕为主。

曾经的繁华热闹现在已归于寂寞，宅子里已经没有什么人。遇到以前的住户也是家族的后人陈先生在院中劳作。他虽已七十多岁，但身形还是很硬朗。他说以前这里住着几十户人家，都是陈氏的后人，现在都搬出去了，他自己是因为东西没地方放，才每天来这里干活。提到大宅的兴衰，不免一番感慨，说"文革"时多亏前面挂毛主席像，后面藏传家宝，很多有价值的东西才得以保存。

提到现在文物被盗，他大声地指给我看，哪些是被盗的东西，哪些是后加的防护措施，但似乎就是在说这件事情，并无太多的切肤之痛的样子。镇宅之宝十二扇屏，央视曾经做过专访。不过现在媒体追逐的目标似乎就是什么东西值多少钱，什么东西最值钱，所有的东西都有个标价。对外介绍用坦厝就是以此物为号召，不过防盗措施更为严密，早已秘不示人了。

English

In Yueque Village, 1 kilometer from Songkou Town, a grand mansion sits quietly on a half-height terrace, overlooking the fields before it.This is Yongtan House.

Its name is somewhat odd — in fact, it was named after its original owner.Because it is located in Xiaban Village, Songkou Town, Yongtan House is also called Xiaban House.

Founded in 1752 (during the Qianlong reign of the Qing), it took 27 years to complete, with the father starting and the son continuing — now 257 years old, with a building area of 5,080 square meters.

Inside the gate, over 200 rooms include a main hall, lower hall, transverse hall, study, inner and outer courtyards, rainwater wells, and a back garden.

It follows the style characteristics of Central Plains ancient residences: structure mainly combining timber with earth and stone; architectural style of three-courtyard eight-wing mansion, each wing separated by fire-sealing walls, with side halls and wing rooms symmetrically flanking the central main hall, mainly one to two stories, imposing and grand; roof slopes are all concave curves, with swallow-tail ridges at both ends; decorative elements such as archways, wood carvings, stone carvings, clay sculptures, and colored paintings are varied, with wood carvings predominant.

The former bustle has now given way to loneliness; few people remain in the mansion.We met Mr.Chen, a descendant of the family and former resident, working in the courtyard.

Though over seventy, he is still hale.

He said dozens of families, all Chen descendants, once lived here, but now all have moved out; he comes daily only because he has nowhere else to store his things.

Speaking of the mansion's rise and decline, he reflected that during the Cultural Revolution, thanks to hanging Chairman Mao's portrait in front and hiding family heirlooms behind, many valuable items were preserved.

Regarding current theft of cultural relics, he loudly pointed out which items were stolen and which protective measures were added later — but he seemed to be merely stating facts, without much personal pain.

The town's treasure, twelve folding screens, was once featured in a CCTV special.But now the media seems to chase only how much things are worth, what is most valuable — everything has a price tag.

Introducing Yongtan House to outsiders uses this object as its calling card, though anti-theft measures are stricter, and it has long been kept from public view.

推荐级别：★★★

合龙桥

No.46
Helong Bridge
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：民国
地址：福州市闽清县省璜乡省璜村
类型：桥梁·木拱桥
特征标签 Highlights
木拱桥营造史和当代古旧工艺桥村关系古道线索船型桥墩双数木拱
中文 Chinese

地方上对廊桥或称木拱桥的关注还是始于大约十年前中央台的《探索》栏目的一档节目，追溯《清明上河图》上最引人瞩目的、众人接踵的虹桥。东京汴梁的繁华，显要地反映出那座木制拱桥不是寻常的结构，反以木苗编制，互相咬合，远远超出西方现代结构计算的法则。

因为现代中国这种木制结构的拱桥已经罕见，所以有些学者认为这种桥已经绝迹了，甚至怀疑这种桥是否真的存在过，或是出自画师的凭空臆造。

后来学者在闽浙交界一带发现了大量的这种形制的木拱桥，桥的基础架构和《清明上河图》上描画的如出一辙，甚至结构上比画上的还要有所发展，功能上也有所不同：闽浙一带发现的木拱桥在桥面上还建有长长的走廊，以供过往行人避雨休息之用，人们根据其外形亲切地称这种桥为廊桥、亭桥、厝（屋）桥。先前的怀疑才不攻自破。

但惊喜之余新的争论又产生了：为什么全国那么大的范围内只在闽浙一带发现了这种木拱桥，曾经出现在首都都市的造桥工艺应该遍地开花才是。

于是又出现两种论点："中央派"认为这是随着金人的入侵北宋的瓦解，汴梁的高级技师作为难民逃到闽浙一带，把这种工艺带到了那个地方；另一派"地方派"认为没有那么神秘，因为廊桥在当地实在算不得稀奇，不但数量多，掌握这门手艺的工匠民间也有不少，而且至今他们还在修桥、造桥，因而这种造桥工艺应该是当地土产。

我自己的看法倾向前者，但是也以为，这种桥的结构不利于抵抗侧推力，因此也只能生存在深涧深谷的环境中，中原之地不是它们的老家。合龙桥位于福州市闽清县省璜乡省璜村，就在村口，步行数十米便到。古桥气势宏大，周身涂红，已经略显暗淡，顶部装饰别致，具有地方特色，但平实不过分。

桥中间有一船型桥墩，两边分别架以木拱结构，按这一点说似乎与典型的木拱桥略有出入，可能是受限于材料或工艺，这大概也是"合龙桥"名字的来历，是两条龙合二为一。

据查合龙桥始建于宋代乾道间，元代延佑年间毁，明代万历年间重建，清代甲寅之变耿精忠反，遭火焚，康熙三十八年（1699年）重建，后经重建和维修至今。

合龙桥长32.35米，宽4.35米，桥屋四柱九檩抬梁式木架构，两边桥头未用木柱而用檩条寄墙，12间，44柱，上覆硬山顶。登桥而上，桥内装饰略显近代气息，可能和重修有关。

廊屋两侧设有风雨板，成一定角度撑起，这样既能遮风挡雨又使桥内采光良好，足见匠人苦心。另外，合龙桥还极具个性之桥，除了中间有一桥墩显得与众不同，桥墩两侧的木拱结构竟不完全一致，跨度也不等（一边12.5米，另一边14.7米）。另外支撑桥的大木根数是8根，采用双数而非中间取中两边对称的单数，在闽浙木拱桥中也较少见。

据说造桥的工匠师傅来自两百里外的古田，姓名已无考。因为在村口最热闹的地方，合龙桥周围新建筑林立，与当初营造时的景观设计已经不同。在正对合龙桥的小卖部休息，正午的阳光照耀在合龙桥上，桥周边的老人、小孩怡然自得，路边有很多五行八作的铺户，依然构成一幅很安详的图景。

English

Local interest in covered bridges, or timber-arch bridges, began about a decade ago with a CCTV "Exploration" program tracing the famous Rainbow Bridge in "Along the River During the Qingming Festival.

" The prosperity of Bianjing (Kaifeng) prominently showed that this timber arch bridge was no ordinary structure — woven from timber saplings, interlocked, far exceeding Western modern structural calculation principles.

Because such timber-arch bridges are rare in modern China, some scholars thought they had become extinct, even doubting whether they had ever truly existed or were merely the painter's invention.

Later, scholars discovered numerous such timber-arch bridges in the Fujian-Zhejiang border region; their basic structure is identical to that depicted in the painting, even more developed structurally, and different in function: the bridges found in Fujian-Zhejiang have long corridors on the deck for travelers to shelter from rain and rest.

People affectionately call them covered bridges, pavilion bridges, or house bridges based on their appearance.The earlier doubts were thus dispelled.

But amid the delight, new debate arose: why, across such a vast country, were such bridges found only in Fujian-Zhejiang?

Bridge-building technology that once appeared in the capital should have spread everywhere.

Two theories emerged: the "Central School" argues that with the Jin invasion and the collapse of the Northern Song, Bianjing's master craftsmen fled as refugees to Fujian-Zhejiang, bringing the craft there; the "Local School" argues it is not so mysterious — covered bridges are common locally, numerous in quantity, with many folk craftsmen still repairing and building them today, so the craft should be indigenous.

My own view leans toward the former, but I also believe this bridge structure is poor at resisting lateral thrust, so it could only survive in deep ravines and valleys — the Central Plains was not its homeland.

Helong Bridge stands in Shenghuang Village, Shenghuang Township, Minqing County, Fuzhou, right at the village entrance, a few dozen meters' walk away.

The ancient bridge is imposing, painted red throughout (now slightly faded), with distinctive local-style top decoration, plain and unexaggerated.

In the middle is a boat-shaped pier, with timber-arch structures on both sides — this differs slightly from typical timber-arch bridges, perhaps limited by materials or craft; this is likely the origin of the name "Helong" (Joining Dragons), two dragons joined as one.

Records show Helong Bridge was first built during the Qiandao reign of the Song, destroyed during the Yanyou reign of the Yuan, rebuilt during the Wanli reign of the Ming, burned during the 1674 rebellion of Geng Jingzhong in the Qing, rebuilt in 1699 (the 38th year of Kangxi), and subsequently rebuilt and maintained to the present.

Helong Bridge is 32.35 meters long and 4.35 meters wide.

The bridge house has a four-column nine-purlin beam-lifting timber frame; both bridgeheads use purlins resting on walls rather than timber columns, with 12 bays and 44 columns, covered by a gable roof.

Climbing onto the bridge, the interior decoration shows somewhat modern traces, possibly related to restoration.

Wind-and-rain boards on both sides of the covered hall are angled outward, providing shelter while allowing good lighting inside — evidence of the craftsman's care.

Moreover, Helong Bridge is highly individual: besides the distinctive central pier, the timber-arch structures on both sides of the pier are not entirely identical, with unequal spans (12.

5 meters on one side, 14.7 meters on the other).

Additionally, the number of large timbers supporting the bridge is 8 — an even number rather than the odd number with central symmetry — which is also rare among Fujian-Zhejiang timber-arch bridges.

The bridge-building craftsman reportedly came from Gutian, two hundred li away; his name is lost.

Because it sits at the busiest spot in the village entrance, Helong Bridge is surrounded by new buildings, unlike its original landscape design.

Resting at the small shop facing Helong Bridge, with midday sun shining on it, the elderly and children around the bridge are content, and various roadside shops still form a peaceful scene.

推荐级别：★★★★

宏琳厝

No.47
Honglin House
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：福州市闽清县坂东镇新壶村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构中国最大古民居666间住房雕梁画栋
中文 Chinese

我们面对的不是一面镜子，而是宏林厝中轴线上一开到底的几进院落。宏琳厝坐落于福建省闽清县坂东镇新壶村，距闽清县城25公里。

占地面积17000多平方米，使用木材7000多根，全厝大小厅堂35间，花圃25个，天井30个，风火墙36堵，水井4口，大门13个，住房666间，是一座结构精巧的民居建筑。由虎头门直入三进，各进之间隔一横街。由过雨亭相连。内厝均为木结构，八堵夹火墙都以九根立柱用横枋贯串组成。

中间正厅，两边各建一、二、三官房和火墙弄。左右书院各三间，中为书院厅，两旁为书房。回照三进不同，首尾进两边没有开间，二进回照左右各分二间。正厅、书院、回照围为天井。正厅与后厅以屏风相隔。

第三进正厅设祭祖神龛，足以说明是一次性设计而成。二、三进后厅隔后天井为厨房。正中为厨房厅，左右各建厨房四间。火墙外左右两旁隔沟建筑横厝，朝向与正厝成九十度，横厝两端正反方向各开横厝厅一间，两厅之间平排建横厝八间。横厝之外又建外横厝，平面布局各设两间下马间，东北角和西南角建兔耳各一间。

宏琳厝现已号称中国最大的古民居，里面雕梁画栋，翚飞鸟革，穿门过弄，大有可观。只可惜也有旅游地常见的一幕，讲解者绘声绘色，听者睡意正浓，所谓各行其道。

English

What we face is not a mirror, but several courtyards running straight along the central axis of Honglin House.

Honglin House is located in Xinhu Village, Bandong Town, Minqing County, Fujian Province, 25 kilometers from Minqing county seat.

It covers over 17,000 square meters, using more than 7,000 timber logs.

The entire mansion has 35 halls of various sizes, 25 flower gardens, 30 courtyards, 36 fire-sealing walls, 4 wells, 13 gates, and 666 residential rooms — a residential building of exquisite structure.

Entering through the Tiger Head Gate, one proceeds through three courtyards, each separated by a horizontal street and connected by rain shelters.

The inner mansion is entirely timber structure; the eight fire-sealing walls are each composed of nine columns connected by horizontal beams.

The central main hall is flanked by first, second, and third official rooms and fire-wall alleys on both sides.

The left and right study compounds each have three rooms: a study hall in the center and study rooms on both sides.

The return galleries differ across the three courtyards: the first and last have no side bays, while the second's return galleries are divided into two bays each.

The main hall, study, and return galleries enclose a courtyard.The main hall and rear hall are separated by a screen.

The third courtyard's main hall has an ancestral shrine, indicating the entire complex was designed at once.

The rear halls of the second and third courtyards are separated by a rear courtyard for kitchens: a kitchen hall in the center with four kitchen rooms on each side.

Outside the fire walls, on both sides and separated by drainage ditches, stand transverse wings oriented at 90 degrees to the main mansion; each end of the transverse wings has a transverse hall in opposite directions, with eight transverse rooms between the two halls.

Beyond the transverse wings stand outer transverse wings, with two dismounting rooms each in the plan, and rabbit-ear rooms at the northeast and southwest corners.

Honglin House is now claimed to be China's largest ancient residence, with carved beams and painted rafters, elegant rooflines, and winding passages — much to see.

Unfortunately, it also has the common scene of tourist sites: the guide narrates vividly while the listeners grow drowsy — each following their own path.

推荐级别：★★★

宝林禅寺

No.48
Baolin Zen Temple
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：唐—清
地址：福州市连江县丹阳镇
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
残留的早期石构做法明万历敕建碑文斗拱跳上长长伸出支撑遮檐板
中文 Chinese

从国道通往宝林寺是一段不宽的水泥路，有几公里长，两边都是青山和一块块良田。时值北方的冬令而这里还是满眼绿色，闽地风光着实养眼。宝林寺说是唐代建筑，但几座大殿与传说相比都是新修的，或者系清代以降的作品。只有殿前的几根石柱或池塘边的小桥还保留着几分唐代遗韵。

顺着大殿边的小路拾级而上，第三级的禅室是清代旧物。禅室的东跨院还保留着明万历年间敕建禅寺的碑文。值得注意的是柱头之上层层出挑的斗拱跳上长长伸出，支撑遮檐板，这种做法也有同源变化，在福州地区不时可以见到。这里都是女住持，在忙着劳作，显得平实清净。

有一位出家人很和善地给我们指点游观之所，听说我们是北京来的，很认真地提醒我们注意保暖，"我们这里很冷的"，听上去真是有几分禅意了。宝林禅寺的香火较盛，还见到虔诚的女居士三步一拜地执敬礼佛。

English

From the national highway to Baolin Temple runs a narrow concrete road several kilometers long, flanked by green mountains and patches of fertile fields.

Though it is winter in the north, here everything is still green — the Min landscape is truly easy on the eyes.

Baolin Temple is said to be a Tang Dynasty building, but compared with the legend, several main halls are newly restored or date from the Qing onward.

Only a few stone columns before the halls or the small bridge by the pond retain some Tang Dynasty charm.

Following the path beside the main hall up the steps, the third-level meditation room is a Qing Dynasty relic.

The east annex of the meditation room preserves an inscription from the Wanli reign of the Ming, recording the imperial construction of the temple.

Notably, the bracket sets (dougong) above the column capitals project outward in layers, extending far to support the eave boards — this method has related variations and can occasionally be seen in the Fuzhou area.

The temple is run by female abbots, busy with labor, appearing plain and pure.

One nun kindly showed us around; hearing we were from Beijing, she earnestly reminded us to keep warm: "It's very cold here" — sounding truly Zen-like.

Baolin Temple has thriving incense, and we saw devout female lay Buddhists prostrating every three steps in worship.

推荐级别：★★

含光塔

No.49
Hanguang Pagoda
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：福州连江县城东
类型：宗教建筑·砖石结构
特征标签 Highlights
砖石塔形制工艺比例尺度楼阁式红砖砌造古塔全国仅存二座
中文 Chinese

含光塔距县城三华里，耸立于县城东斗门山上，眺望风邑，为连江县治标志。塔下含光寺，远近景观一良一莠。含光塔呈八角七层楼阁式，塔建于明万历十六年（1588年）。塔高25.2米，第一层高4米，往上逐层缩减。塔内花岗石三角形石阶，绕塔轴中心盘旋而上，各层设门槛。

含光塔除基座、翘角用花岗石外，佛龛、塔檐出拱均以红砖砌造。只是今天古塔通身抹灰，难以看到红砖的本来面目。据统计，楼阁式红砖砌造的古塔，在全国现仅存二座，对研究古塔建筑艺术富有价值。"橹声过寺潮初上，塔影横江月正来。"塔影横斜，橹声咿哑，不过是那时光景。古塔依旧，塔下的世界早已是换了一番境界。

English

Hanguang Pagoda stands three li from the county seat, atop Doumen Mountain east of the city, overlooking the region — a landmark of Lianjiang County.

Below it is Hanguang Temple, with nearby scenery varying in quality.

Hanguang Pagoda is an octagonal seven-story pavilion-style pagoda, built in 1588 (the 16th year of Wanli reign, Ming).It stands 25.

2 meters tall, with the first story 4 meters high, tapering upward.Inside, granite triangular stone steps spiral around the central axis, with thresholds at each level.

Except for the base and upturned corners made of granite, the niches and eave brackets are all built of red brick.

Today, however, the ancient pagoda is entirely plastered, making it difficult to see the red brick's original appearance.

According to statistics, only two pavilion-style ancient pagodas built of red brick survive in China, making this valuable for the study of ancient pagoda architectural art.

"The sound of oars passes the temple as the tide rises; the pagoda's shadow stretches across the river as the moon arrives." The pagoda shadow slanting, the oars creaking — that was the scene of old.

The ancient pagoda remains, but the world below has long since changed.

推荐级别：★★★

护国天王寺塔

No.50
Dhrtarastra Temple Pagoda
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：唐
地址：福州连江县凤城镇仙塔街
类型：宗教建筑·砖石结构
特征标签 Highlights
砖石塔形制工艺比例尺度福建省仅存唐代大型石塔大乘妙法莲华经刻字
中文 Chinese

老者和古塔，最是懂得无言的含义。塔建造未成，寺毁而止，塔脚淹没，身处市井……再多的不幸也丝毫无法减弱给我的震撼。护国天王寺塔位于连江县凤城镇仙塔街，俗称仙塔，又称无尾塔，建于唐大中三年（849年）。塔体花岗石砌造，仿木楼阁式结构，八角，中有石阶上下。

塔仅二层，略有收分，现高9.2米，须弥座高1.2米。塔身每边宽约3米，一层高4.15米，各角出双华拱双昂，正面开门，门楣左右饰龙首，余七面凹入长方形龛，龛上方浮雕小佛像。

二层入口有浮雕人物一对，出口（通一楼）有阴刻文字，左右分别为"大乘妙法莲华经"与"大方广佛华严经"，层高4米，设二门六龛。

这座福建省仅存的唐代大型石塔，形制上与本地宋、元、明石塔之间存在明显的基因联系。

1961年公布为县级文物保护单位。

English

The elderly and the ancient pagoda best understand the meaning of silence.

The pagoda was never completed, the temple was destroyed, the pagoda's base was submerged, and it stands in the midst of the city...no amount of misfortune can diminish the shock it gives me.

Dhrtarastra Temple Pagoda is located on Xian Tower Street, Fengcheng Town, Lianjiang County, commonly known as Xian Pagoda or Tailless Pagoda, built in 849 (the third year of Dazhong reign, Tang).

The pagoda body is built of granite, imitating a timber pavilion-style structure, octagonal, with stone steps inside.It has only two stories, with slight tapering, now 9.

2 meters high, with a 1.2-meter xumizuo base.Each side of the body is about 3 meters wide; the first story is 4.15 meters high, with double hua-gong and double ang at each corner.

The front has a door with dragon-head ornaments on both sides of the lintel; the other seven sides have recessed rectangular niches with small relief Buddha images above.

The second-story entrance has a pair of relief figures; the exit (to the first floor) has intaglio inscriptions reading "Miaofa Lianhua Sutra" (Lotus Sutra) and "Dafangguang Fo Huayan Sutra" (Avatamsaka Sutra) on left and right.

The second story is 4 meters high, with two doors and six niches.

This is the only surviving large Tang Dynasty stone pagoda in Fujian Province, with clear genetic links in form to local Song, Yuan, and Ming stone pagodas.

It was designated a county-level cultural heritage site in 1961.

推荐级别：★★★

普光塔

No.51
Puguang Pagoda
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：元
地址：福州连江县东云居山上
类型：宗教建筑·石结构
特征标签 Highlights
石塔形制工艺比例尺度元代武士雕像螺旋台阶卷头造斗拱
中文 Chinese

普光塔坐落在连州东部紧邻海边的山上，云居古刹的墙外，搜地图的时候找"云居寺"会比较好找。去往云居寺的山路上很少有车，而且一路上风光优美，空气新鲜。不断地向当地人问路，虽然语言沟通不甚顺畅，但他们解答得都很详细。可以看出这一地区的人们比较富足，可能是沿海地区物产丰富，再加上善于经营的原因，山中沿途有很多当地人集资兴建的寺院，规模都很大。

普光塔建于元至正十年（1350年），平面八边形，为花岗岩仿木构八角楼阁式石构，仅存两层，残高9米有余。一层四边开门，四扇石门上的匾额分镌"寂照"、"光明"、"无碍"、"融圆"字样。

正门朝西，每两道门之间都有一座服饰装束明显带有元代风格的武士雕像。雕像形态各异，颇为传神。平面中心有一柱，绕柱有螺旋台阶可上人。第一层塔檐八个角均向上翘起，角柱雕以卷头造斗拱、转角由昂等石构件，转角、补间铺作俱全。二层四面设有佛龛。

二层正门上方，向下倾斜地悬挂着一块青石雕刻的石碑，是塔铭碑，上方为二龙戏珠的浮雕图案，两边衬托着透雕的波浪纹，下方刻有四个小方格，里面图案已模糊不清，依然看得出雕刻之精美程度。碑铭正中竖行阳刻"普光塔"三字。

English

Puguang Pagoda sits on a mountain near the sea in eastern Lianjiang, outside the walls of the ancient Yunju Temple — searching "Yunju Temple" on maps makes it easier to find.

The mountain road to Yunju Temple has little traffic, with beautiful scenery and fresh air along the way.

We repeatedly asked locals for directions; though communication was not entirely smooth, they answered in detail.

It is evident that people in this region are relatively prosperous — perhaps due to the coastal area's abundant products and business acumen — and many temples funded by locals line the mountain route, all large in scale.

Puguang Pagoda was built in 1350 (the 10th year of Zhizheng reign, Yuan).

It has an octagonal plan, a granite imitation-timber octagonal pavilion-style stone structure, with only two stories surviving, over 9 meters in remaining height.

The first story has doors on four sides; the stone door plaques are inscribed "Jizhao" (Silent Illumination), "Guangming" (Bright Light), "Wu'ai" (Unobstructed), and "Rongyuan" (Harmonious Completeness).

The main door faces west; between every two doors stands a warrior statue with clearly Yuan-style attire.The statues vary in form and are quite expressive.

At the center of the plan stands a column, with spiral steps winding around it for access.

The eight corners of the first-story eave all turn upward; the corner columns are carved with stone components such as rolling-head bracket sets and corner ang, with both corner and inter-column bracket sets complete.

The second story has niches on four sides.

Above the second-story main door, a slanting stone stele hangs — the pagoda inscription stele, with a relief of two dragons playing with a pearl at the top, openwork wave patterns on both sides, and four small squares below whose patterns are now blurred but still show the exquisite carving.

In the center of the inscription, three characters "Puguang Ta" (Puguang Pagoda) are carved in vertical relief.

推荐级别：★★★★★

郑氏三落厝

No.52
Three Quadrangle Dwellings of Zheng's Family
级别：区级文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：福州市连江县丹阳镇坂顶村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构横向展开院落日式风格趋同上下水系统
中文 Chinese

在一片青山环抱、绿草荫荫的农田边上，坐落着一组建筑，外观看上去那么的疏朗，与周围的环境那么的和谐，谦逊中又不失鲜明的个性。当我们得知这就是我们寻找中的明代建筑郑氏三落厝，难掩心中的惊喜。与那些偏居于闹市中的老建筑不同，这一片建筑是有自己的领地的，周围是青山和农田，绝少视觉污染，越发忠实再现了几百年前建筑的总体原貌。

造访中幸遇房屋的原住族人郑老伯，他热情地带我们参观。他对自己祖上的历史典故，房屋的一梁一栋都是如数家珍。此地的最早原住是唐代的张姓，官至礼部尚书，后来获罪抄家了。现今的主人郑氏于明代中叶迁居于此，兴建了这座大宅供族人居住。

另一个与其他古建筑不同的是，三落厝不是向纵深发展而是横向展开的，堂屋高大轩敞，与堂屋并排是起居劳作的建筑，然后又是堂屋和另外一组起居劳作之所，实际上是把城市中常见的"几进"的院落横向造成，这也许更符合乡间占地广阔，周围没有邻居的实情。院落的内部会客、起居、劳作的功能区错落有致，有二层的小楼，石磨、米房、水槽等生产用具随处可见。

整座大院还有完备的上下水系统，屋后引来清澈的山泉通过院内的石砌的水道流到各处。三落厝最大的特点，是整所建筑里里外外看上去好似大家熟知的日式风格——确切地说应当是相反的流传顺序：福建沿海地区与台湾、琉球乃至日本南部诸岛有着相似的地理环境，也有着密切的文化往来。或许，大家都是海洋性气候，房屋建筑都需要防风、防雨、防高温，另外人口相对集中居住内部的庭院需要小巧紧凑。

一方水土养一方人，跨越海峡阻隔的趋同现象也是可能的。三落厝以外的其他老建筑也大概都是这个样子的。在三落厝盘桓了许久，和郑老伯分手还有些不舍。最后他感叹道：我活了76岁，经历了好多事，战乱、运动，人生真的是沧海桑田啊！

English

Beside farmland surrounded by green mountains and lush grass, sits a group of buildings whose appearance is so open, so harmonious with the surroundings, modest yet with distinct character.

When we learned this was the Ming Dynasty Zheng Family Three Dwellings we sought, we could hardly conceal our delight.

Unlike old buildings tucked away in busy cities, this complex has its own territory, surrounded by mountains and farmland, with almost no visual pollution — faithfully reproducing the overall original appearance of the building from centuries ago.

During our visit, we were fortunate to meet Mr.Zheng, an original clan resident, who warmly showed us around.

He knew the historical anecdotes of his ancestors and every beam and pillar of the house by heart.

The earliest inhabitants here were the Zhang family of the Tang Dynasty, whose head served as Minister of Rites before being convicted and having his property confiscated.

The current Zheng family moved here in the mid-Ming and built this grand mansion for clan residence.

Another difference from other ancient buildings: the Three Dwellings do not develop in depth but expand horizontally.

The main halls are tall and spacious; beside each main hall stand buildings for daily living and labor, then another main hall and another group of living-and-labor spaces — essentially turning the city's common "several-courtyard" layout into a horizontal arrangement, perhaps more suited to the countryside's vast land and absence of neighboring houses.

Inside, the functional areas for receiving guests, daily living, and labor are well arranged; there are two-story buildings, with stone mills, rice rooms, water troughs, and other production tools everywhere.

The entire compound has a complete water supply and drainage system, with clear mountain spring water from behind the house flowing through stone channels in the courtyard to all parts.

The greatest feature of the Three Dwellings is that the entire building, inside and out, looks like the well-known Japanese style — more precisely, the transmission order should be reversed: the Fujian coastal region, Taiwan, Ryukyu, and even the southern islands of Japan share similar geographical environments and close cultural exchanges.

Perhaps, all having maritime climates, buildings need wind protection, rain protection, and heat resistance; additionally, with relatively concentrated populations, internal courtyards need to be small and compact.

Each place nurtures its own people; convergence across the strait barrier is also possible.Other old buildings beyond the Three Dwellings are probably much the same.

We lingered at the Three Dwellings for a long time, reluctant to part with Mr.Zheng.Finally he sighed: I've lived 76 years, experienced so much — wars, movements — life is truly a sea of change!

推荐级别：★★★★★

陈太尉宫

No.53
Shrine for Grand Commandant Chen
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：宋—清
地址：罗源县中房镇以南乾溪村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构·石作
特征标签 Highlights
早期木作石作历代更改痕迹江南仅存融宋明清三朝风格木结构建筑群南宋正殿梭形柱
中文 Chinese

闯过危险的采石路段，终于进入了风景优美的山间公路，陈太尉宫以极其华丽的姿态，雍容地出现在一片田地里。陈太尉宫坐西向东，偏南十度，由正殿、南北配殿、戏台、门楼等组成，占地面积1155平方米，宫外建筑物有大道、门亭、旗碣、宫埕等1800平方米，合计占地面积3000多平方米。

陈太尉宫始建于五代后梁开平三年（909年），南宋嘉定二年（1209年）扩建，后来又经多次重修扩建。

现存南宋时正殿、明清南北配殿、清代戏台等，是江南仅存完好的、融宋、明、清三朝风格于一体的木结构古建筑群。

前殿由门楼、戏台组成。

大门结构独特，面阔五间，据记载是清咸丰年间所建，正间为门廊，廊左右砌八字屏墙，门廊上方由斗拱组成藻井，廊前檐下为七层如意斗拱连叠，上承歇山顶屋盖，翼角翚飞，古朴大方。

门两侧石柱上嵌着一副对联："神殿重修永镇河川崇祀典，虬松倒插长标斗里显威灵。"戏台为单檐歇山顶，与门楼连为一体，飞翼高翘，上有八角形藻井，沿口嵌着花鸟等图案的雕板。戏台中间平时是过道，演戏时将木板铺设过道之上。戏台两侧有包厢，与南北配殿相连。当地人言三十多年前尚有戏班演出闽剧。

南北配殿均面阔三间，进深六间，单檐歇山顶，由20根梭形柱支撑抬梁式梁架，明间上方六角形藻井以斗拱装饰，雀替刻卷草云纹。

其中南配殿瓜柱、斗拱等处雕刻的花纹更为精细繁缛。正殿重檐歇山顶，举折甚缓。殿坐西朝东，面阔三间，进深五间，木构架尚存早期特征。

原进深八椽，南宋时将后金柱位置后移，改为十椽，清时又于殿前加建轩廊一间。柱头不施普柏枋，斗拱用七铺作双杪双下昂。木构表面无涂层，斗拱个别部位及月梁尚余彩画痕迹。

金柱旁有较细木柱加固支撑，内柱上下端均做梭形卷杀，下端置石础上。柱子侧脚明显。因陈太尉宫是削坡而建，出了大门登坡而上，眼前是一片良田，当地人种植着粮食蔬菜，而宫殿华美的屋顶近在咫尺。徜徉于楼阁殿宇之间，整个建筑中没有其他游人，那种静静地沉浸在美的包围中的感觉不由得使人凝神屏气，只有照相机的快门在不断作响。

English

After navigating the dangerous quarry road section, we finally entered the scenic mountain highway, and the Shrine for Grand Commandant Chen appeared in its magnificent splendor, gracefully set amid fields.

The shrine faces east, ten degrees south of due east, comprising the main hall, north and south auxiliary halls, a stage, and a gate tower, covering 1,155 square meters.

Outside buildings include a main road, gate pavilion, flag steles, and a courtyard totaling 1,800 square meters, for a combined area of over 3,000 square meters.

Founded in 909 (the third year of Kaiping reign, Later Liang, Five Dynasties), expanded in 1209 (the second year of Jiading reign, Southern Song), and repeatedly restored and expanded thereafter.

The surviving Southern Song main hall, Ming-Qing north and south auxiliary halls, and Qing stage form the only well-preserved timber ancient building complex in Jiangnan integrating Song, Ming, and Qing styles.

The front hall consists of the gate tower and stage.The gate has a unique structure, five bays wide, reportedly built during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing.

The central bay is a gate porch with splayed screen walls on both sides; above the porch, bracket sets form a caisson ceiling; under the front eave, seven layers of ruyi bracket sets are stacked, supporting a hip-and-gable roof with soaring wing corners — simple and elegant.

Stone columns on both sides of the gate bear a couplet: "The divine temple rebuilt forever guards rivers and mountains in reverent sacrifice; the twisted pine planted upside down long marks its power in the Big Dipper.

" The stage has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, integrated with the gate tower, with soaring wings and an octagonal caisson ceiling, its rim inlaid with carved panels of birds and flowers.

The middle of the stage is normally a passageway; during performances, wooden planks are laid over it.Boxes on both sides of the stage connect to the north and south auxiliary halls.

Locals say opera troupes performed Min opera here over thirty years ago.

The north and south auxiliary halls are each three bays wide and six deep, with single-eave hip-and-gable roofs, supported by 20 spindle-shaped columns on beam-lifting frames; above the central bay, a hexagonal caisson is decorated with bracket sets, and spandrel brackets are carved with scrolling grass and cloud patterns.

The south auxiliary hall's carvings on melon columns and bracket sets are particularly fine and elaborate.

The main hall has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof with a very gentle roof curve.

Facing east, it is three bays wide and five deep, with timber frame retaining early features.

Originally eight rafters deep, the rear gold columns were moved back in the Southern Song to make it ten rafters; in the Qing, a front porch was added.

Column capitals lack pubai fang (epistyle blocks); bracket sets use seven-puzuo with double tiao and double xia'ang.

The timber surface has no coating; some bracket set parts and moon beams still retain traces of colored painting.

Beside the gold columns, thinner timber columns provide reinforcement; inner columns are spindle-shaped (suoxing) at both ends, resting on stone plinths.Column inclination (cejiao) is evident.

Because the shrine was built by cutting into a slope, stepping out the gate and climbing up reveals fertile fields where locals grow grain and vegetables, while the palace's ornate roof is close at hand.

Wandering among the pavilions and halls, with no other visitors, the feeling of being quietly immersed in beauty makes one hold one's breath — only the camera shutter keeps clicking.

推荐级别：★★★★★

圣水寺栖云洞造像

No.54
Statues in Qiyun Cave of Shengshui Temple
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：宋—当代
地址：罗源县县城
类型：宗教建筑·石造像
特征标签 Highlights
造像18罗汉青石像宋淳祐八年造像朱熹手书南石古道
中文 Chinese

圣水寺坐落在罗源县城内，那座700多年的参天古樟树笼罩下的就是了。寺门前一条现代、拥挤，但还算安静的小街，人们在做着各样的生意。圣水寺始建于宋绍圣三年（1096年），后几经修葺，近来踵事增华，现在留下来的房子最早也要晚于明万历年间。第二进为"大雄宝殿"。

殿前两侧钟楼和鼓楼左右对峙。旁边有客堂。宋代理学大儒朱熹曾客居传学，手书"南石古道"至今仍在。出客堂过拱形小石桥，见一洞口被建了一座金属铁笼牢牢锁住，便是著名的"栖云洞"，里面有18罗汉青石像。

造像是宋淳祐八年的（1248年），为全国重点文物保护单位。据说该洞内雕像竟几次被盗，我们想进入一览几经交涉终未果，虽然有些遗憾，但守洞居士的认真也实在令人钦佩，就不打搅了。在寺的高处，罗源县城一览无余，有些嘈杂的县城也显得安静了不少。原本一片青山秀水的安逸之地，现在的经济发展主业竟为开山采石。

希望浮躁的人心早日得以安宁，以恢复往昔的一方净土。

English

Shengshui Temple sits in the city of Luoyuan, beneath a towering 700-year-old camphor tree.

Before the temple runs a modern, crowded, yet relatively quiet street where people conduct various businesses.

Shengshui Temple was founded in 1096 (the third year of Shaosheng reign, Song), restored several times, and recently embellished; the oldest surviving buildings date no earlier than the Wanli reign of the Ming.

The second courtyard is the "Mahavira Hall." Before it, bell and drum towers face each other on both sides.Beside it is a guest hall.

The great Song Neo-Confucian Zhu Xi once stayed here to teach, and his handwritten "Nanshi Ancient Road" still remains.

Leaving the guest hall and crossing a small arched stone bridge, one sees a cave entrance firmly locked with a metal cage — the famous "Qiyun Cave," containing 18 blue-stone arhat statues.

The statues date from 1248 (the eighth year of Chunyou reign, Song) and are a National Key Cultural Heritage Site.

It is said the statues in the cave have been stolen several times; we tried to enter for a look but after repeated negotiations were unsuccessful.

Though somewhat regretful, the dedication of the lay guardian is truly admirable, so we did not disturb further.

From the high part of the temple, the city of Luoyuan is fully visible, and the somewhat noisy city appears much quieter.

Originally a peaceful place of green mountains and clear waters, its main economic development is now quarrying stone from mountains.

One hopes the restless hearts will soon find peace, restoring the pure land of old.

推荐级别：★★

宁德市 Ningde

54 处

华藏寺

No.55
Huacang Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明—近代
地址：宁德市蕉城区霍童村东南支提山
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
早期遗址历代更改痕迹佛教名山支提山明万历御赐铜铸鎏金毗卢佛明正统北藏经
中文 Chinese

从屏南到宁德的公路可称地质公园，一路上奇山怪石，虽然有些险峻，但风景绝好，一路上还有符号指引。只有如此灵秀的山水，才能孕育出这么多好的建筑，反之只有好的建筑，掩映在这般山水之间，两者才算相得，或许这也是中国古典建筑的营造理念。支提寺最早官称华严寺，支提寺是俗称，坐落在宁德市蕉城区东南的支提山上，寺因山而得名，为宋开宝四年（971年）吴越王钱俶创建。

宋雍熙二年（985年）赐名雍熙寺。现寺系明永乐五年（1407年）重修，赐名华藏寺。永乐以后寺庙几经毁坏和重修，现在的殿宇多是民国36年以后重建的。建筑的规制宏大，颇有千年古刹的遗韵。

因《华严经》中有"不到支提枉为僧"的说法，支提山与山西五台山、四川峨嵋山、浙江普陀山、安徽九华山并称佛教名山。

大雄宝殿为重檐歇山顶，抬梁式木构架，面阔、进深各5间，设有回廊。

吊顶之上绘满多幅佛教故事的彩绘，画法颇为生动，与其他寺院中所常见者不同，给人印象深刻。

华藏寺内供奉有大量珍贵文物，如明万历二十五年（1597年）御赐铜铸鎏金大毗卢佛像一尊，绕座千圣天冠铁佛900多尊，此外还保存明正统四年（1439年）内府刊本《北藏经》6441册，五爪金龙紫衣袈裟一件等。

寺外有元第三、九、二十二代禅师塔、明中兴大行国师塔。华藏寺由于地处深山，游人似乎不多，但寺中的僧人的修行非常严谨，按时打点诵经等功课不辍，另外还发放弘扬佛法，劝人向善的书籍刊物。

English

The highway from Pingnan to Ningde could be called a geological park, with strange mountains and rocks along the way; though somewhat precipitous, the scenery is superb, with symbolic markers guiding the route.

Only such elegant landscapes can nurture so many fine buildings; conversely, only fine buildings, nestled in such landscapes, make the two complement each other — perhaps this is also the design philosophy of classical Chinese architecture.

Zhiti Temple, officially first called Huayan Temple (Zhiti Temple is the common name), sits on Zhiti Mountain southeast of Jiaocheng District, Ningde.

Named after the mountain, it was founded in 971 (the fourth year of Kaibao reign, Song) by Qian Chu, King of Wuyue.

In 985 (the second year of Yongxi reign, Song), it was bestowed the name Yongxi Temple.

The current temple was restored in 1407 (the fifth year of Yongle reign, Ming) and named Huacang Temple.

After Yongle, the temple was repeatedly destroyed and restored; most current halls were rebuilt after the 36th year of the Republic.

The building's scale is grand, with the lingering charm of a thousand-year-old monastery.

Because the Avatamsaka Sutra states "not reaching Zhiti makes a monk's life in vain," Zhiti Mountain is ranked alongside Wutai Mountain (Shanxi), Emei Mountain (Sichuan), Putuo Mountain (Zhejiang), and Jiuhua Mountain (Anhui) as a famous Buddhist mountain.

The Mahavira Hall has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof with beam-lifting timber frame, five bays wide and five deep, with surrounding corridors.

Above the ceiling, numerous paintings of Buddhist stories are vividly rendered, different from those commonly seen in other temples, leaving a deep impression.

Huacang Temple houses many precious relics, including a gilded bronze Vairocana Buddha bestowed by the emperor in 1597 (the 25th year of Wanli reign), over 900 iron statues of Thousand-Sages Crown-Buddhas surrounding the seat, 6,441 volumes of the Northern Canon printed by the imperial palace in 1439 (the fourth year of Zhengtong reign), and a five-clawed golden dragon purple robe.

Outside the temple stand the pagodas of the 3rd, 9th, and 22nd generation Chan masters of the Yuan, and the pagoda of Grand National Preceptor Daxing of the Ming.

Because Huacang Temple is deep in the mountains, there seem to be few visitors, but the monks' practice is rigorous, with regular chanting and other duties unceasing; they also distribute books and publications promoting the Dharma and encouraging goodness.

推荐级别：★★★

廉村

No.56
Liancun Village
级别：国家级历史文化名村
年代：清
地址：宁德福安市溪潭镇廉村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构开闽进士第一村明代古堡鹅卵石官道一门五进士
中文 Chinese

廉村位于福建宁德福安市溪潭镇。廉村原名石矶津，是唐朝福建第一个进士薛令之的故乡。廉村被喻为开闽进士第一村，位于福安市溪潭镇穆阳溪中游西岸，旧名富溪津、石矶津，因里人薛令之是福建第一位进士（唐神龙二年即706年中进士），且为官清廉，被御赐"廉村"、"廉水"、"廉岭"之名。

南宋以后，因水陆交通便捷，出现经济繁荣、文化发达的景象。明嘉靖三十九年（1560年），筑城墙以御倭寇，称廉村堡。

云雾后边就是廉村，村堡平面略呈椭圆形，周长1258米（现存850米）。墙面用鹅卵石垒砌，中为泥土夯筑。墙基厚4米。东、西尚存三个城门，用花岗岩条石叠砌。城墙上生长的大树已经与墙共生，或许就是庇佑古村的树神。城堡内面积达10万平方米。

有明代官道，中用鹅卵石拼花、纵向平铺三条条石，长500米，横贯城堡东西。官道两侧尚存大型明、清时期民居26座，清代祠庙4座。

不少家庭大厅迄今仍完好地摆放着当时造型古朴、雕镂精致的大型木屏风。城东有明代古码头2座，用鹅卵石铺砌，宽约3.5米，曾是通往大海的内河港口，也是沟通闽东北和浙南的水陆枢纽和物资集散地。沿溪是用鹅卵石铺就的古道，路旁并立几方石碑。

廉村历代人才辈出，自唐至清，获取各种功名者共50多人，宋大观三年（1109年）到南宋宝祐三年（1255年），146年间，有进士23人，出现（陈雄）一门五进士的奇迹。

宋代大儒朱熹也曾经到廉村讲学。徜徉于村中，到处是古老的街道和建筑，不时地传来鸡鸣狗吠和鸟儿飞动时拍打翅膀的声音，偶尔也有人们的说话声，仿佛回到了过去。满眼青翠的绿色，清澈的空气，让人沉醉于这一切所构成的梦境之中，乐而忘返。

English

Liancun Village is located in Xitan Town, Fu'an City, Ningde, Fujian.

Originally named Shijijin, it was the hometown of Xue Lingzhi, Fujian's first jinshi (imperial examination graduate) of the Tang Dynasty.

Hailed as the Number One Village for Jinshi in Fujian, it lies on the west bank of the middle reaches of Muyang Stream in Xitan Town, formerly known as Fuxijin and Shijijin.

Because villager Xue Lingzhi was Fujian's first jinshi (passing in 706, the second year of Shenlong reign, Tang) and was an honest official, the emperor bestowed the names "Lian Village" (Honest Village), "Lian Stream" (Honest Stream), and "Lian Ridge" (Honest Ridge).

After the Southern Song, convenient water-and-land transportation brought economic prosperity and cultural development.

In 1560 (the 39th year of Jiajing reign, Ming), a city wall was built to defend against Japanese pirates, called Liancun Fort.

Behind the clouds lies Liancun; the fort is slightly oval in plan, with a perimeter of 1,258 meters (850 meters surviving).

The wall is built of cobblestones with rammed earth inside, and the wall base is 4 meters thick.Three city gates survive on the east and west, built of granite dressed stones.

Large trees growing on the wall have become symbiotic with it — perhaps the tree spirits protecting the ancient village.The fort covers 100,000 square meters.

It has a Ming Dynasty official road, 500 meters long, running east-west, with cobblestone patterns in the center and three longitudinal dressed stones.

On both sides of the official road, 26 large Ming-Qing residences and 4 Qing ancestral halls survive.

Many family halls still display large, simply shaped and exquisitely carved wooden screens from the period.

East of the village are 2 Ming Dynasty ancient wharves, paved with cobblestones, about 3.

5 meters wide — once inland ports to the sea and water-and-land hubs connecting northeast Fujian with southern Zhejiang.

Along the stream runs a cobblestone ancient path with several steles beside it.

Liancun has produced talents throughout history: from Tang to Qing, over 50 people obtained various academic degrees.

From 1109 (the third year of Daguan reign) to 1255 (the third year of Baoyou reign, Southern Song), in 146 years there were 23 jinshi, including the miracle of five jinshi from one family (Chen Xiong's).

The great Song Neo-Confucian Zhu Xi once lectured in Liancun.

Wandering the village, ancient streets and buildings are everywhere; the sounds of roosters crowing, dogs barking, birds flapping wings, and occasional human voices seem to transport one to the past.

Verdant green everywhere and clear air make one intoxicated by this dreamlike scene, reluctant to leave.

推荐级别：★★★★

楼下村

No.57
Louxia Village
级别：福建省历史文化名村
年代：清
地址：宁德福安市溪柄镇楼下村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构三十二幢大宅观音兜虾蛄墙陈志华调研著书
中文 Chinese

楼下村，一个位于宁德福安市溪柄镇柏柱洋南面的神秘村落，青山掩映之下，距离千年古刹狮峰寺仅不到一公里。三十二幢形制规整的大宅院中，最早的建于清嘉庆十三年（1808年），其形制阔大壮观，建筑特色别具一格。我的老师陈志华先生两次在此调研，并著书《楼下村》，令我当年好生疑惑他是怎样找到这个地方的。

清嘉庆年间，刘氏先祖刘向荣建了村里第一栋大宅，称作"垟中厝"。随后他的后代在邻近位置，陆续建了形制相近的大宅院。大宅院集中分布于村中三条横向主干道的中段上。

从清嘉庆十三年（1808年）至咸丰三年（1853年）间，共有三十多幢传统民居大宅院在此拔地而起，连成蔚为壮观的住宅群。步入楼下村，如同翻开一幅古朴悠然的乡村画卷，错落有致的大宅院蛰居在群山之间。沿约两米宽的石板路穿梭，左右是土黄色的夯土院墙。置身其中，感受出一种浓重的历史沧桑感。

古村的布局严整，村中原先都是铺的石头的古道。各幢大宅四周夯土墙之上，被金黄色和白壁烘托着，四个尖角刺向天空的"观音兜"和高低起伏的"虾蛄墙"最具特色。

English

Louxia Village is a mysterious village south of Baizhuyang in Xibing Town, Fu'an City, Ningde, nestled among green mountains, less than one kilometer from the thousand-year-old Shifeng Temple.

Among its 32 well-proportioned grand mansions, the earliest was built in 1808 (the 13th year of Jiaqing reign, Qing), with grand scale and distinctive architectural character.

My teacher, Mr.Chen Zhihua, conducted field research here twice and wrote a book titled "Louxia Village," which made me wonder how he found this place.

During the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, Liu Xiangrong, the ancestor of the Liu family, built the village's first grand mansion, called "Yangzhong Cuo.

" His descendants subsequently built similar grand mansions nearby.The mansions are concentrated along the middle sections of three transverse main roads in the village.

From 1808 to 1853 (the third year of Xianfeng reign), over 30 traditional residential grand mansions rose here, forming a spectacular residential cluster.

Entering Louxia Village is like opening a simple, leisurely rural painting scroll, with well-arranged grand mansions nestled among mountains.

Walking along the two-meter-wide stone paths, earthen-yellow rammed-earth courtyard walls line both sides.Immersed in it, one feels a strong sense of historical vicissitude.

The ancient village's layout is rigorous, originally with stone-paved ancient paths throughout.

Above the rammed-earth walls surrounding each mansion, set off by golden-yellow and white walls, the "Guanyin Dou" (Guanyin hoods) with four sharp corners pointing to the sky and the undulating "Xiagu Qiang" (mantis shrimp walls) are most distinctive.

推荐级别：★★★★

狮峰寺

No.58
Shifeng Temple
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：唐—清
地址：宁德福安市柏柱洋狮峰山
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
早期遗址斗拱历代更改痕迹闽东佛教历史最早规模最大寺院24根方形石柱六铺作偷心造
中文 Chinese

"影动方池鱼惊客，声来半岭竹引风。"狮峰寺又称狮峰广化禅寺，始建于唐景福元年（892年），原在山顶，明永乐年间（1403—1424年）移建于此，清嘉庆年间（1796—1820年）重修。

寺院占地1.3万平方米。坐西朝东，傍山而立，建筑雄伟，古貌尚存，为闽东佛教历史最早、规模最大的寺院之一。狮峰寺由天王殿、大雄宝殿、法堂和观音阁四个主体建筑组成，布局错落有致，建筑风格古朴。大殿建筑风格独特，历史价值极高，属国内罕见。

大雄宝殿进深13米余，宽10米余，高14米。有24根方形石柱，其中8根柱围达2.2米，高5米以上，支撑着木结构的屋顶梁椽，柱高显著大于间广。

大殿外围尚有石柱16根，支托着飞檐翘角。大殿用重檐歇山顶，檐下斗拱构件形式接近福州华林寺大殿，而用六铺作偷心造，加昂形耍头。大殿四周的窗梁板墙，精雕细刻着各种图案。室内斗拱交迭、藻井高举，风采依旧。

English

"Shadows move in the square pond, fish startled by guests; sounds come from the half-ridge, bamboo drawing the wind.

" Shifeng Temple, also called Shifeng Guanghua Chan Temple, was founded in 892 (the first year of Jingfu reign, Tang), originally on the mountaintop.

It was moved to its current location during the Yongle reign of the Ming (1403-1424) and restored during the Jiaqing reign of the Qing (1796-1820).

The temple covers 13,000 square meters.

Facing east and built against the mountain, it is majestic with its ancient appearance preserved — one of the earliest and largest Buddhist temples in eastern Fujian.

Shifeng Temple consists of four main buildings: the Heavenly King Hall, Mahavira Hall, Dharma Hall, and Guanyin Pavilion, with a well-arranged layout and simple architectural style.

The main hall's unique architectural style and high historical value are rare in China.The Mahavira Hall is over 13 meters deep, over 10 meters wide, and 14 meters high.

It has 24 square stone columns, 8 of which have a circumference of 2.

2 meters and height over 5 meters, supporting the timber roof beams and rafters — the column height is significantly greater than the bay width.

Sixteen additional stone columns around the hall's perimeter support the flying eaves and upturned corners.

The hall has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof; the eave bracket set components are similar in form to those of Fuzhou's Hualin Temple main hall, but use six-puzuo touxin zao (hidden-heart construction) with ang-shaped shuatou.

The window panels and walls around the hall are exquisitely carved with various patterns.

Inside, overlapping bracket sets and a raised caisson ceiling retain their former elegance.

推荐级别：★★★★★

太后公厅

No.59
Empress Dowager Hall
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：宋—清
地址：宁德福安市晓阳镇晓阳村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
斗拱拆换下来的老构件太后牌坊谢氏众厅戏台与观戏楼不加油漆粉饰
中文 Chinese

太后公厅亦称皇后坊，坐落于周宁福安晓阳村内。到达晓阳村口，在当地人的指点下从一个不起眼的小巷拐入村子，两边都是此地常见的夯土墙黑瓦的房屋，走不远便进入到一座外面看起来普通、里面建制宏大的建筑，就是这里了。

太后公厅始建于宋代端平元年（1234年），重建于明弘治八年（1493年），由太后牌坊和谢氏众厅组成，坐北朝南偏东15度，占地430平方米。

牌坊面阔三间，进深三柱，重檐，上檐歇山顶，下檐悬山顶，正面有抱鼓石一对。众厅面阔五间带左右梯道，进深四柱，中间为戏台，后面带鼓乐间，两边为观戏楼。

梁架结构为穿斗式木架构，屋面为重檐悬山顶，两山加双重雨披。厚重的用料，精巧的拼接，整个宏大的建筑内完全是木材构建，而且不加任何油漆粉饰，给人感觉古老而清新。

福建当地似乎有个特点就是像太后公厅这样比较郑重的祭拜的场所总是与娱乐密不可分，旁边大多建有戏台，所谓寓教于乐，这样既不会太过严肃枯燥，也不会单纯耽于游乐，可谓两全其美。太后公厅历经数百年保存尚好，并未被束之高阁，而是就溶于村民们的生活中，这也许就是建筑的生命力了。小男孩儿走过公厅，突然用普通话大叫：谁在那里装神弄鬼？

English

Empress Dowager Hall, also called Empress Archway, sits in Xiaoyang Village, Fu'an (near Zhouning).

Arriving at the village entrance, guided by locals, one turns into the village through an inconspicuous alley, flanked by the common rammed-earth walls and black-tiled houses of the region.

Not far in, one enters a building ordinary from outside but grand inside — this is it.

Empress Dowager Hall was founded in 1234 (the first year of Duanping reign, Song) and rebuilt in 1493 (the eighth year of Hongzhi reign, Ming).

It consists of the Empress Dowager Archway and the Xie Clan Assembly Hall, facing south 15 degrees east, covering 430 square meters.

The archway is three bays wide and three columns deep, with double eaves: the upper eave has a hip-and-gable roof, the lower eave an overhanging gable roof, with a pair of drum-holding stones at the front.

The assembly hall is five bays wide with left and right stairways, four columns deep, with a stage in the center, a music room behind, and viewing galleries on both sides.

The beam frame is column-and-tie timber construction; the roof is double-eave overhanging gable with double rain aprons on both gable ends.

Heavy materials and exquisite joinery — the entire grand building is constructed entirely of timber without any paint or decoration, giving a feeling both ancient and fresh.

Fujian seems to have a characteristic: solemn worship places like Empress Dowager Hall are always inseparable from entertainment, with stages usually built nearby — so-called "education through entertainment," neither too serious and dull nor merely indulgent in amusement, achieving the best of both.

Empress Dowager Hall has survived centuries in good condition, not put on a shelf but integrated into villagers' lives — perhaps this is the vitality of architecture.

A little boy walked past the hall and suddenly shouted in Mandarin: "Who's playing tricks over there?"

推荐级别：★★★★

翠郊古宅

No.60
Old House in Cuijiao
级别：福建省历史文化名村
年代：清
地址：宁德福鼎县白琳镇翠郊村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木结构江南第一大古民居360根木柱24个院子双层排水系统
中文 Chinese

在福鼎西南部白琳镇的群山环抱之中，坐落着一座巨大精美的古宅，他的存在为这个名为"翠郊"的名不见经传的小村增色不少。翠郊古宅是吴氏家族的私家宅院。始建于清乾隆十年（1745年），距今已有250多年的历史。仍保存基本完好。

宅院主体建筑规模宏大，占地面积5000平方米：由360根木柱支撑而起，共围出24个院子，6个大厅、12个小厅，共有房192间，总占地面积为13980平方米（20亩），可谓江南第一大古民居。

整体平面图上格局巧妙，且脉络分明，纵横交错又横纵相连，有如一个古老的围棋大棋盘，摆设于幽谷之中。宅院中特殊的双层排水系统，使整个宅院中的水相通，又汇集一处，有聚财的寓意。古宅的建筑风格虚实结合，刚柔并济。严实的合院间以廊屋花墙相连，窗开借景，晦明之趣盎然。墙外花草忽隐忽现又盈溢出含蓄之美，凝重不失轻巧，端庄又不失灵气。

English

Nestled among the mountains of Bailin Town in southwestern Fuding, stands a huge and exquisite ancient mansion, whose presence adds much to this obscure little village called "Cuijiao.

" Cuijiao Old House is the private residence of the Wu family.Founded in 1745 (the 10th year of Qianlong reign, Qing), it has a history of over 250 years and remains basically intact.

The main building is grand in scale, covering 5,000 square meters: supported by 360 timber columns, enclosing 24 courtyards, 6 large halls, 12 small halls, with 192 rooms in total, and a total area of 13,980 square meters (20 mu) — arguably the largest ancient residence in Jiangnan.

The overall plan is ingenious, with clear脉络, crisscrossing and interconnected, like an ancient Go board set in a secluded valley.

The special double-layer drainage system in the mansion connects all water throughout and gathers it in one place, symbolizing the accumulation of wealth.

The architectural style combines void and solid, hardness and softness.

The enclosed courtyards are connected by corridor houses and flower walls, with windows framing views, full of the charm of light and shadow.

Flowers and plants outside the walls appear and disappear, overflowing with restrained beauty — dignified yet light, elegant yet spirited.

推荐级别：★★★★★

老人桥

No.61
Old Man Bridge
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：宁德福鼎市管阳镇西阳村
类型：桥梁·木拱桥
特征标签 Highlights
木拱桥结构桥村关系古道线索福鼎现存唯一木构虹梁式廊屋桥窗棂装饰
中文 Chinese

西昆村附近是大山。西昆村是省级历史文化名村。正值元宵佳节，村里康安寺内香火极盛，拥满前来祈福的人们，但人群中似乎没谁想起这座家庙，这里厚重精美的雕饰不输于翠郊大宅。老人桥，在不远的西阳村。桥建于明正德年间（1506—1521年），是十七都民众为纪念邱阜老人而建的。

清康熙、同治年间重修，桥上建长廊式桥屋，系福鼎市现存唯一的木构虹梁式廊屋桥。

老人桥体量中等，为东西走向，长30.4米，宽4.8米，高8.0米，孔跨25.2米，共13开间，上覆双坡顶，两边檐下有1~4层挡风板。

顶部有装饰，桥架编木起拱，桥屋内专门做了窗棂，在木拱廊桥中比较少见。桥边留有长长的石头铺就的古道，这里曾经是福鼎到宁德的必经之路。桥外青山翠竹或许是当地人看了几百年的。

English

Near Xikun Village are great mountains.Xikun Village is a provincial-level historical and cultural village.

On the Lantern Festival, the Kang'an Temple in the village was bustling with incense, crowded with people praying for blessings, but no one in the crowd seemed to remember this family temple — its heavy and exquisite carvings are no less than those of the Cuijiao mansion.

Old Man Bridge is in nearby Xiyang Village.Built during the Zhengde reign of the Ming (1506-1521), it was constructed by the people of the 17th district to commemorate Old Man Qiu Fu.

Restored during the Kangxi and Tongzhi reigns of the Qing, a long corridor-style bridge house was built on it — the only surviving timber rainbow-beam covered bridge in Fuding City.

Old Man Bridge is medium-sized, running east-west, 30.4 meters long, 4.8 meters wide, 8.0 meters high, with a span of 25.

2 meters, 13 bays, covered by a double-slope roof, with 1-4 layers of wind boards under the eaves on both sides.

The top has decoration; the bridge frame uses woven timber to form the arch, and window lattices were specially made inside the bridge house — relatively rare among timber-arch covered bridges.

Beside the bridge remains a long stone-paved ancient path, once the only route from Fuding to Ningde.The green mountains and bamboo outside the bridge may have been watched by locals for centuries.

推荐级别：★★★★

三福寺双塔

No.62
Double Pagodas in Sanfu Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：宁德福鼎县白琳镇柘里村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
砖塔形制比例尺度仿木构件做法六角七层塔刹出土秦半两汉五铢南宋铜钱
中文 Chinese

赶往双塔的一路是没有边际的采石场，外带加工运输，其环境之不堪，与古人的精美艺术杰作相对照，真是莫大的讽刺。抛开古建筑的保护不言，开山采石以卖钱本身就是野蛮和短视的，如果这也叫发展经济，那割肉卖眼也可以称为发家致富了。余本知老百姓需要穿衣吃饭，需要娶妻生子，像余这种游手好闲之人本不该说三道四，无奈看着着实心痛！现在似乎有一怪圈：环境越好的地区，经济越不发达，若想搞活经济，唯一的办法：破坏环境。

所谓靠山吃山，似乎也不是这么个吃法。

眺望远远的江色，惭愧当初无力学得一身惠民之术，几乎没有心情再重复马英杰先生提供的信息：三福寺双塔位于福鼎县白琳镇柘里村，三福寺建于宋代，双塔始建于南宋时期，另据《裘氏族谱》载，现存双塔为明代永乐九年（1411年）建造。

现寺院为近代重建。双塔形式与大小完全相同，砖砌楼阁式，六角，七层，高7.8米。塔身仿木结构，转角处立柱，施四铺作，不用耍头，每层屋面层层叠涩而上覆筒板瓦，顶刹作葫芦形。

1986年维修双塔时，曾从塔刹中出土大量铜钱，包括了秦半两钱、汉五铢钱和南宋铜钱，同时出土的还有银制立像等物品，银制立像上刻有某某娘舍等，这些都说明了该塔始建于宋朝。

English

The road to the double pagodas passes through endless quarries, with processing and transport — the deplorable environment, contrasted with the exquisite artistic masterpieces of the ancients, is truly a great irony.

Setting aside the protection of ancient buildings, quarrying mountains for money is itself barbaric and short-sighted; if this is called economic development, then cutting flesh and selling eyes could also be called getting rich.

I know ordinary people need food and clothing, need to marry and have children — an idle person like me shouldn't criticize, but I can't help feeling heartbroken!

There seems to be a vicious cycle: the better the environment, the less developed the economy; to revitalize the economy, the only way is to destroy the environment.

The so-called "living off the mountain" doesn't seem to mean this.

Gazing at the distant river, ashamed of my inability to learn skills to benefit the people, I have little mood to repeat the information provided by Mr.

Ma Yingjie: the Double Pagodas of Sanfu Temple are located in Zheli Village, Bailin Town, Fuding County.

Sanfu Temple was built in the Song Dynasty; the double pagodas were first built in the Southern Song.

According to the Qiu Family Genealogy, the existing pagodas were built in 1411 (the ninth year of Yongle reign, Ming).The current temple was rebuilt in modern times.

The two pagodas are identical in form and size: brick pavilion-style, hexagonal, seven stories, 7.8 meters high.

The body imitates timber structure, with columns at corners, four-puzuo bracket sets without shuatou; each story's roof is built up with corbelled courses, covered with cylindrical and flat tiles, with a gourd-shaped finial.

During maintenance in 1986, many copper coins were unearthed from the finial, including Qin Banliang coins, Han Wuzhu coins, and Southern Song copper coins; also unearthed were silver standing figures inscribed with "donated by so-and-so," all indicating the pagoda was first built in the Song Dynasty.

推荐级别：★★★★

仙蒲村

No.63
Xianpu Village
级别：省级历史文化名村
年代：清
地址：宁德福鼎县磻溪镇
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
村落格局木结构通体黑色建筑望族合院住宅林氏宗祠古戏台
中文 Chinese

从翠郊到仙蒲有30多公里的山路，都是新铺的水泥路，但有的路段比较狭窄，加上山路蜿蜒起伏，对自驾是个考验。不过游走于大山之中，周围人迹罕至，有如仙境一般。一路之上穿越了无数的竹林和茶园，这一地区盛产"福建白茶"，想起晚清人士李慈铭讽刺御史宝廷的诗句"曾因义女弹乌柏，妄逐京倡食白茶"，不禁笑出声来。当然，此白茶非彼白茶。

终于到了，驻车于村口的河边，望着对岸成片的黑色大宅，确切的说是大寨子，难免有些发愣。正发愁附近静得出奇，想找个人打听一下，不想竟有人敲车窗：师傅您今天回去吗，能不能带我出去？仙蒲在山的那一边，信步走过石桥，穿过那条称作"仙蒲溪"的大溪，进入了那些黑色大型建筑错落的仙蒲村。大屋鳞次栉比，规模大小参差，静卧于山水田地之间。屋宇之间相隔不远，又保有独立的空间，一派和谐景象。

给人印象最深的，除建筑的精巧外，就是通体的黑色，与周围满山的绿色形成鲜明的令人愉悦的反差。现存有清代以来的古民居数十座，保存完好的依次有外泮林氏民居、外头林氏民居、中头林氏民居、内头林氏民居、桥头林氏民居、大厝里林氏民居、花门楼林氏民居，另外还有林氏宗祠。

仙蒲民居建筑典型者为望族合院住宅，两侧厢房对称布置。结构式样基本采用重檐歇山顶，穿斗式木构架。民居两侧均有阁楼式翘檐，面阔多在8至11间，进深7至12柱之间，规模不小。

独自在村中穿行游荡，偶尔有热情的大姐介绍去参观某某院落。民居庭前都设四角庭院，大门进入后是条石夹锭的通道，直到前面的大厅。通道砌石阶二至三级，以青石打造的石鼓分布通道两侧。庭院坪铺以青石子，光亮而整洁；有的是夯平泥地，平实而整饬。四周以条石为框架，落落大方。厅堂是古民居最为精心装点之处，木雕装饰繁多。

古祠、古庙、古井构成村落三大元素。村落中心处的林氏宗祠为清代建筑，祠堂前立有棋杆夹，铺以青石坪，场地开阔。祠内古戏台、天井及藻井手绘人物故事。

宗祠的形制代表着外来的中原文化，是我们一眼能够辨识得出的，又似乎与当地的特色建筑关系不大。就要离开了，来时想要搭车的年轻人小林过来，听说我是来探访古村的，又热情地拉我去多看几处，他们家就住在一处很大的古宅中，不过是在河的这一边。由于对当地的建筑风格和文化源流心存疑惑，我特意问他祖上是汉族的还是畲族？他很确切地说是汉族，"祖上是从中原举家迁来的"。

回去的路上有小林做伴就不寂寞了。到了附近的镇上，小林还执意请我去吃当地的一家面馆，"很有名气的，来了总归要尝一尝"，虽然门面有些简陋，但味道确实好，食客都是当地人。小林还特意请来自己的小学老师，着实令人感动。仙蒲不负其名，乃喜欢摄影和古建筑的朋友不可错过之地，当然同行之人中最好再有一喜欢自驾的挑战一战。

如果你是三种爱好集大成者，那就独自前往领略一下那一路的气息，毕竟很多东西只有独自品味方能体会其中的妙处。

English

From Cuijiao to Xianpu is over 30 kilometers of mountain road, all newly paved concrete, but some sections are narrow, and with the winding, undulating mountain road, it is a test for self-driving.

Yet wandering in the great mountains, with few people around, feels like a fairyland.

Along the way, one passes through countless bamboo groves and tea gardens — this region produces "Fujian White Tea.

" Recalling the late Qing poem by Li Ciming mocking censor Bao Ting — "Once denounced a righteous daughter for the tallow tree, recklessly followed Beijing courtesans eating white tea" — I couldn't help laughing.

Of course, this white tea is not that white tea.

Finally arriving, I parked by the river at the village entrance, gazing at the clusters of black grand mansions across the river — or rather, large stockaded villages — and couldn't help being stunned.

Worrying that it was eerily quiet nearby and wanting to ask someone, unexpectedly someone knocked on the car window: "Master, are you going back today?Can you take me out?

" Xianpu is on the other side of the mountain.Walking across the stone bridge, crossing the wide stream called "Xianpu Stream," I entered Xianpu Village with its scattered large black buildings.

The grand houses stand in rows, varying in size, quietly nestled among mountains, waters, and fields.The buildings are not far apart yet retain independent space — a scene of harmony.

What impresses most, besides the exquisite architecture, is the uniform black color, forming a striking and pleasant contrast with the surrounding green mountains.
