The ground in front of the academy still preserves meaningful cobblestone paving.Nearby there are even older relics: the ancient Min-Yue State site of the Han Dynasty.

The protection of the Min-Yue King City site is done very carefully; some artificial things made to protect the relics also try to maintain the original style, making one somewhat unable to distinguish true from false.

Though only the foundation remains of this royal city, it shows a distinctive ancient royal aura.It reminds one of the ancient city of Sukhothai in Thailand.

A so-called prosperous place, viewed longitudinally on the time axis and horizontally in culture and commerce, is often prosperous.

In short, people's social creation and development cannot be separated from the natural environment that nurtures them; everything that happens here ultimately depends on the environment here — in China this is called "fengshui," in the West called "geographical history.

" Whether Eastern or Western, after digging mountains and selling stones, hometown becomes a quarry, and humanity becomes a tombstone.

推荐级别：★★★★

东岳庙

No.115
Dongyue Temple
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：南平建瓯市东门
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
寺庙格局木结构东晋建武元年始建圣帝殿福建仅见十一檩抬梁式屋架夔龙纹象鼻下昂
中文 Chinese

建瓯市东门一里地外的白鹤山南麓，坐落着占地四十余亩的大庙建瓯东岳庙，又称东岳行宫。此庙不仅是目前福建省也是华东六省为数不多的古代道教建筑之一；而其主殿"圣帝殿"，则规模、形制为福建仅见。庙始建年代可上溯到东晋元帝建武元年（317年）。

明《建宁府志》卷三《山川》白鹤山条下记载："（山）在府城东，晋时望气者言，山有异气，命工凿之，朝凿暮合，有鹤翔其上，因名，山之麓有东岳行宫。"而最早的古迹，是正殿旁的一口井，名"天涌泉"，是宋熙宁三年（1070年）所凿。东岳庙依山面溪，历史上多有重建和修缮。

据《八闽通志》记载："真如寺，在光禄坊白鹤山之麓，元为天堂庵，洪武十二年（1379年）大殿宇，廿四年（1391年）改今额。"所以今天看到的东岳庙是一组明清以来的建筑。

大门又叫"金刚殿"；入门后上二十余级，便是前殿"东岳宫"，内供十殿阎王，殿后门额上横书"岱宗隆祀"四字，其内还有一座长16米、高10米的木结构戏台，是明代遗留建筑；戏台前有一大空坪，沿空坪再上三级石阶，便是正殿"圣帝殿"。

"圣帝殿"是东岳庙主体建筑，重檐歇山顶，副阶周匝，下层面阔七间，进深八间。上层檐则只有三间，十一檩抬梁式屋架。

大殿用斗拱的手法非常独特，下层斗拱均用翘头，上层平身科也如此，只是达到十一踩的规模，但在柱头科、角科，则用了三只夔龙纹象鼻下昂。殿内砌上明造，施藻井，四面承托以如意斗拱，驼峰雕工精细，有鹿、羊等造型。

金柱、中柱柱础造型介乎覆盆、鼓镜式之间，有些古意。主殿之后是"娘娘殿"，宽16米，高10米，分九开间，建筑与前殿相似。每年农历三月二十七日为东岳庙会，是为庆贺次日东岳帝诞辰而办，已有数百年历史。过去，东岳庙的最大文化特色是庙会集商业、游乐活动于一体。

庙会期间活动，一是由地方最高官员亲自主持，选定地方绅士具体负责；二是政府允许，各县公认，可以向闽北各县题疏筹款；三是会期活动明显带有大规模的城乡物质交流性质；四是庙会期间，殿前空坪上少不了舞狮、伞技、挑幡和民间剧表演。

民国后由东门、察院前、高门头、横街及其附近住户组成福禄寿喜财五班福首轮流值年，正月入庙议事、维修殿宇、题疏筹款、安排活动。当时或许是信仰大于生意。即使地方官不很相信，伙同着或虔诚或有要事相求的老百姓，他们定也煞有介事地把庙会当作官员的"正差"了。

English

At the southern foot of Baihe Mountain, one li outside the East Gate of Jian'ou City, stands the large Jian'ou Dongyue Temple, also called Dongyue Xinggong, covering over 40 mu.

This temple is not only one of the few ancient Taoist buildings in present-day Fujian Province but also in the six provinces of East China; and its main hall, "Shengdi Hall" (Holy Emperor Hall), has a scale and form unique to Fujian.

The temple's founding date can be traced back to 317 (the first year of Jianwu reign, Eastern Jin Emperor Yuan).

Ming's "Jianning Prefecture Annals" Volume 3 "Mountains and Rivers" under the Baihe Mountain entry records: "(The mountain) is east of the prefectural city; in the Jin, a qi-watcher said the mountain had unusual qi, so workers were ordered to chisel it, but it closed by evening after being chiseled in the morning, with cranes soaring above it — hence the name; at the foot of the mountain there is Dongyue Xinggong.

" The earliest relic is a well beside the main hall, named "Tianyong Spring," chiseled in 1070 (the third year of Xining reign, Song).

Dongyue Temple, built against the mountain and facing the stream, has been rebuilt and restored many times in history.

According to the "Bamin Tongzhi": "Zhenru Temple, at the foot of Baihe Mountain in Guanglu Fang, was Tiantang Nunnery in the Yuan; in 1379 (the 12th year of Hongwu) the main hall was built, and in 1391 (the 24th year) it was renamed to its current title.

" So the Dongyue Temple seen today is a group of buildings from the Ming-Qing period onward.

The main gate is also called "Jingang Hall" (Vajra Hall); after entering and climbing over twenty steps, one reaches the front hall "Dongyue Palace," enshrining the Ten Kings of Hell; on the rear door lintel of the hall are written horizontally the four characters "Daizong Longsi" (Grand Sacrifice to Daizong); inside there is also a 16-meter-long, 10-meter-high timber stage, a remaining Ming building; in front of the stage is a large open courtyard, and climbing three more stone steps along the courtyard leads to the main hall "Shengdi Hall.

" "Shengdi Hall" is the main building of Dongyue Temple, with double-eave hip-and-gable roof, surrounding secondary eaves, lower level seven bays wide and eight deep.

The upper eave has only three bays, with an eleven-purlin beam-lifting roof frame.

The hall's use of bracket sets is very unique: lower bracket sets all use qiaotou (upward-curving ends), and the upper pingjianke (intermediate bracket sets) are the same, only reaching the scale of eleven cai (tiers); but at the column-head and corner bracket sets, three kui-dragon-pattern elephant-nose downward ang (xiangbi xia'ang) are used.

Inside the hall, the ceiling is exposed (qishang mingzao), with a caisson ceiling, supported on all sides by ruyi bracket sets; the camel hump (tuofeng) carvings are exquisite, with deer, sheep, and other forms.

The column bases of the golden and central columns are shaped between the inverted-basin and drum-mirror styles, with some ancient feel.

Behind the main hall is the "Niangniang Hall" (Empress Hall), 16 meters wide and 10 meters high, divided into nine bays, with architecture similar to the front hall.

Every year on the 27th day of the third lunar month is the Dongyue Temple Fair, held to celebrate the next day's birthday of the Dongyue Emperor, with a history of several hundred years.

In the past, the greatest cultural feature of Dongyue Temple was that the temple fair integrated commerce and entertainment.

Activities during the fair: first, presided over personally by the highest local official, with local gentry selected for specific responsibility; second, government-permitted and recognized by all counties, allowing fundraising through petitions to all counties in northern Fujian; third, the fair-period activities clearly had the nature of large-scale urban-rural material exchange; fourth, during the fair, the open courtyard in front of the hall inevitably had lion dances, umbrella skills, flag-carrying, and folk drama performances.

After the Republic, five groups of fortune leaders — Fulu, Shouxi, and Cai — formed by residents of East Gate, Chayuanqian, Gaomentou, Heng Street, and nearby households, took turns serving yearly; in the first lunar month they entered the temple to discuss matters, repair halls, raise funds through petitions, and arrange activities.

At that time, perhaps faith outweighed business.

Even if local officials did not quite believe, joining with the common people — whether devout or with important matters to seek — they would certainly treat the temple fair solemnly as an official's "regular duty.

"

推荐级别：★★★

文庙

No.116
Temple of Confucius
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：南平建瓯市仓长路163号
类型：礼制建筑
特征标签 Highlights
寺庙格局木结构明永乐年间始建清同治年间重修同治中兴重檐歇山顶副阶周匝
中文 Chinese

文庙始建于明永乐年间，明清经多次重修，规模宏大，蔚为壮观。题记证明，现状的样子主要确定于清同治年间的那次重修。

其实同治是一个很有意思的时期，主政的既非慈禧太后也非同治皇帝，而是咸丰皇帝的弟弟恭亲王。当时大乱初平，百废待兴，同时朝野上下也开始重新审视自身和西洋文明并尝试早期的洋务运动，衰落中的大清王朝开始有了一些蓬勃之气，史上号称同治中兴。反映在建筑上也可以看到一些与以往不同的东西，虽然在卫道之士看来也许有些许浮躁，毕竟带来一股新鲜气息。

广场前众多烘托文庙的遗迹已经无存，只有经过改造的门廊。门口造型奇特的石狮子，面部有点像泰国的那种鸟神。这文庙不管经过多少朝代的修复，这对石狮神韵依在。再就是门内的石碑。石头不语，文字有声。可以看到今天笔手画脚识字的孩子，可以想象昔日的门庭若市，可以体会古人苦口婆心的劝谏。景象和思绪瞬间掠过，捕捉到什么，都凭个人造诣了。

绿树掩映下气度雍容的大成殿是文庙的主角。大殿重檐歇山顶，副阶周匝，下层面阔五间，上层檐则只有三间。

大殿用斗拱的手法与东岳庙大殿非常类似，上层平身科十一踩，但柱头科、角科和明间当心二攒平身科则用了三只夔龙纹象鼻下昂。殿内逐间用藻井，四面承托以斗拱，彩画遍布，色彩颇有古意。

书院安静的氛围被学龄前儿童打破，这里是他们的乐园，似正是文庙的本意。很奇怪这里的长辈和他们的小孩交流一律用普通话，大概这也是当地文化的一部分——我家的孩子已经上幼儿园了，也要算半个官人了。

建瓯是个很特别的城市，规模不大，名不见经传，但有超出想象的东岳庙，有超出想象的文庙，老城内还有保存完好的部分城墙和城楼。颇有旅行阅历的我也因此不凡而疑惑了一阵子。细思从北面武夷山地区发现汉代闽越王城遗址，到建阳附近的古瓷窑、朱子故里，再延伸到这里，可以发现，也许这一自北而南的地带是这一地区古代经济文化发展的主脉。

有这样悠久的历史和深厚的文化底蕴，建瓯一定能创造新的令人刮目的文明成果。

English

The Temple of Confucius was first built during the Yongle reign of the Ming, and underwent multiple restorations in the Ming and Qing, with a grand and magnificent scale.

Inscriptions prove that its current appearance was mainly determined by the restoration during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing.

Actually, Tongzhi was a very interesting period; the ruler was neither Empress Dowager Cixi nor Emperor Tongzhi, but Prince Gong, the younger brother of Emperor Xianfeng.

At that time, the great chaos had just subsided, everything was waiting to be restored, and at the same time the court and country began to re-examine themselves and Western civilization, attempting the early Self-Strengthening Movement; the declining Great Qing Dynasty began to show some vitality, historically known as the Tongzhi Restoration.

Reflected in architecture, one can also see some things different from before — though in the eyes of moral guardians perhaps somewhat frivolous, after all it brought a fresh breath.

Many relics in front of the square that set off the Temple of Confucius no longer exist, only the modified gate porch remains.

The strangely shaped stone lions at the entrance have faces somewhat like the bird gods of Thailand.

No matter how many dynasties' restorations this Temple of Confucius has undergone, the charm of this pair of stone lions remains.Then there are the stone steles inside the gate.

Stones do not speak, but文字 have voice.One can see today's children gesturing and learning characters, can imagine the bustling crowds of former days, can体会 the ancients' earnest exhortations.

Scenes and thoughts pass in an instant; what one captures depends on personal attainment.

The dignified Dacheng Hall (Hall of Great Achievement), shaded by green trees, is the protagonist of the Temple of Confucius.

The main hall has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof with surrounding secondary eaves; the lower level is five bays wide, while the upper eave has only three bays.

The hall's use of bracket sets is very similar to that of Dongyue Temple's main hall: the upper intermediate bracket sets are eleven-tier, but the column-head, corner, and the two central intermediate bracket sets in the main bay use three kui-dragon-pattern elephant-nose downward ang.

Inside the hall, each bay has a caisson ceiling, supported on all sides by bracket sets, with colored paintings everywhere, the colors quite ancient in feel.

The quiet atmosphere of the academy is broken by preschool children; here is their playground, which seems to be exactly the original intention of the Temple of Confucius.

It is strange that the elders here communicate with their children entirely in Mandarin — perhaps this is also part of the local culture: my child is already in kindergarten, so should count as half an official.

Jian'ou is a very special city, not large in scale and little-known, but with an unexpectedly grand Dongyue Temple, an unexpectedly grand Temple of Confucius, and well-preserved sections of city walls and towers in the old city.

Having considerable travel experience, I was puzzled for a while by this extraordinariness.

Thinking carefully: from the Han Min-Yue King City site discovered in the northern Wuyi Mountain area, to the ancient porcelain kilns and Zhu Xi's hometown near Jianyang, and extending here, one can find that perhaps this north-south belt was the main artery of ancient economic and cultural development in this region.

With such a long history and profound cultural heritage, Jian'ou will surely create new and impressive civilization achievements.

推荐级别：★★★

大觉寺

No.117
Dajue Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：南平建阳市吉水镇山中
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
环境和布局石构造和晚期木结构宋代始建大觉智妙寺大觉禅院日本天皇太子修行传说石矶祠三侯庙
中文 Chinese

来到位于武夷山南麓的建阳，先考察的就是辖区内的石矶祠和大觉寺。顾名思义，石矶祠是个祠堂，供奉蒋源，人称石矶爷，是唐末抗击黄巢义军有功的正统先生，"蒋氏兄弟……使庶民免遭涂炭，于朝廷有功而封侯"。宋初改为"三侯庙"（俗称大庙），清代重建，扩大规模，全庙占地近万平方米。

祠堂广阔，不似地方或家族小祠堂，内设三殿：正殿供蒋公；西配殿供广惠侯，俗名林必兴，以舍生取义得赐；东配殿供昭卫侯，俗名张暹，以正直无私，济民利物而封侯，俗称阎王。虽然建筑大红油饰已经遮盖了一切我对木结构和彩画作的好奇，只是希望堆砌的石构件也许就是唐宋遗物。相传八月十一日为封侯立庙日。是日，方圆十一坊群众杀猪宰羊到庙祭祀，仪式隆重。

气候已经开始转凉，活动一下筋骨，整理一下心情正是时候。最吸引人的还是参加祭祀的人们事后要分散到各设供户家中就餐；另外还从外地请来剧团，从初十夜开台演戏至二十日。位于吉水镇周边山中的大觉寺始建于宋代，又名大觉智妙寺、大觉禅院，据说日本天皇的太子曾来此修行。群山环抱之中，自然少不了幽深的气氛和辛苦的攀登。

周边环境十分幽静，作为古刹整体气韵古意尚存，山中溪水潺潺而下，应有许多景致值得探访，其清幽雅致非普通闹市中寺院可比，朝山礼佛之外也是休闲玩乐的好去处。寺院内部紧凑小巧，已经完全没有大寺的味道，甚至不如石矶祠。对照着光绪年重建寺院碑，大殿的建筑特征便比较了然了。

English

Arriving in Jianyang, located at the southern foot of Wuyi Mountain, the first things examined were the Shiji Ancestral Hall and Dajue Temple within its jurisdiction.

As the name suggests, Shiji Ancestral Hall is an ancestral hall enshrining Jiang Yuan, known as Lord Shiji, an orthodox gentleman who meritoriously resisted Huang Chao's rebel army in the late Tang — "the Jiang brothers.

..spared the common people from disaster, and were enfeoffed as marquises for merit to the court.

" In the early Song it was renamed "San Hou Temple" (commonly called Great Temple), rebuilt in the Qing with expanded scale, the entire temple covering nearly 10,000 square meters.

The hall is vast, unlike a small local or clan ancestral hall, with three halls inside: the main hall enshrines Lord Jiang; the west auxiliary hall enshrines Marquis Guanghui, commonly named Lin Bixing, enfeoffed for sacrificing his life for righteousness; the east auxiliary hall enshrines Marquis Zhaowei, commonly named Zhang Xian, enfeoffed for uprightness and selflessness, benefiting the people and things — commonly called the King of Hell.

Although the building's bright red oil paint has covered all my curiosity about timber structure and painted decoration, one can only hope that the piled stone components may be Tang-Song relics.

According to legend, the 11th day of the eighth lunar month is the day of enfeoffment and temple establishment.

On that day, people from the surrounding eleven neighborhoods kill pigs and sheep to sacrifice at the temple, with a grand ceremony.

The climate has already started to turn cool; it is just the time to stretch one's muscles and整理 one's mood.

The most attractive thing is that people participating in the sacrifice afterwards disperse to dine at the homes of each offering household; additionally, a troupe is invited from elsewhere, performing from the night of the 10th to the 20th.

Dajue Temple, located in the mountains around Jishui Town, was first built in the Song Dynasty, also called Dajue Zhimiao Temple or Dajue Chan Monastery; it is said that the crown prince of the Japanese emperor once came here to practice.

Surrounded by mountains, there is naturally no lack of a deep atmosphere and arduous climbing.

The surrounding environment is very quiet; as an ancient temple, its overall aura retains ancient charm, with mountain streams gurgling down, and there should be many scenery worth exploring — its seclusion and elegance cannot be compared with ordinary city-center temples, and besides pilgrimage to worship Buddha, it is also a good place for leisure and play.

The temple interior is compact and small, completely lacking the feel of a great temple, even less than Shiji Ancestral Hall.

Comparing with the Guangxu-era temple reconstruction stele, the architectural features of the main hall become relatively clear.

推荐级别：★★

拿坑石桥

No.118
Nakeng Stone Bridge
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：南平建阳市书坊乡饶坝村拿坑村
类型：桥梁
特征标签 Highlights
密集的石桥群石构造古道与采石场明嘉靖十七年至万历元年建成清乾隆十五年加造石栏杆13座现存8座
中文 Chinese

说多了木拱桥，并不意味着福建的石桥有些许逊色。木拱桥一般藏在山里，探访起来很是颠簸并快乐着。石桥往往坐落在宽大的江面上，更是今人生活的组成部分。书坊乡拿坑村的石桥群则不然，沿着溪流而建，一公里多长的范围内，居然建了一连串的石拱桥，并保留至今。桥侧每每发现明、清石刻题记记述该桥兴建始末，但是考证起来不是一天半天的事情。

有一本郑顺莲主编的《书坊乡志》，整理建阳史料颇丰，说拿坑村这些石砌单拱桥于明嘉靖十七年（1538年）至万历元年（1572年）期间相继建成，清乾隆十五年（1750年）加造石栏杆。

老人们说共有13座，现存8座。从南平建阳市区前往书坊乡饶坝村拿坑自然村，距离不远，可山路颠簸，要两个多小时的路程，所幸溪水相伴，农人自耕，风景自在。再向邵武方向走，就是拿口村，一坑一口，共享一座山。拿坑村分布在涧溪的两畔，村中就有三座颓石桥，彼此挨得很近，模样非常相似，摆出一副完全不满足于一桥沟通的样子。

可惜保存状况不佳，栏杆破败得几近垮塌，桥身也有砌块走闪的现象。村口和村外的石桥状况更加令人担忧，藤蔓杂草丛生，甚至还有小树。当地人说溪水上的众多桥梁就是算盘的档，史料反映拿坑是古代建阳至邵武古道的必经之地，还有报道说距离拿坑村不远处有一个叫"打石坑"的地方，发现是规模巨大的古采石场，这里很可能是石匠的聚集地。这里的算盘档是不是石匠们施展手艺的试验场，或是"样板间"呢？

English

Talking much about timber-arch bridges does not mean that Fujian's stone bridges are in any way inferior.

Timber-arch bridges are generally hidden in the mountains, and visiting them is quite bumpy yet joyful.Stone bridges often sit on broad rivers, and are even more a part of modern people's lives.

The stone bridge group at Nakeng Village in Shufang Township is different: built along the stream, within a range of over one kilometer, a whole series of stone arch bridges was actually built and preserved to this day.

On the sides of the bridges, Ming and Qing stone inscriptions are often found recording the bridge's construction history, but researching them is not a matter of a day or two.

There is a book "Shufang Township Annals" edited by Zheng Shunlian, which整理 quite a lot of Jianyang historical materials, saying that these stone single-arch bridges in Nakeng Village were successively built between 1538 (the 17th year of Jiajing reign, Ming) and 1572 (the first year of Wanli reign), with stone railings added in 1750 (the 15th year of Qianlong reign, Qing).

Elders say there were 13 in total, 8 surviving now.

From Jianyang urban area of Nanping to Nakeng Natural Village, Raoba Village, Shufang Township, the distance is not far, but the mountain road is bumpy, taking over two hours; fortunately, accompanied by streams, farmers tilling their own fields, and free scenery.

Going further toward Shaowu, there is Nakou Village — one keng (ravine) and one kou (mouth), sharing one mountain.

Nakeng Village is distributed on both banks of the mountain stream; within the village there are three dilapidated stone bridges, close to each other, very similar in appearance, posing as if completely unsatisfied with just one bridge for communication.

Unfortunately, the preservation condition is poor: railings are dilapidated nearly to collapse, and the bridge bodies also have displaced masonry blocks.

The stone bridges at the village entrance and outside the village are in even more worrying condition, overgrown with vines and weeds, even small trees.

Locals say the many bridges over the stream are like the rods of an abacus; historical materials reflect that Nakeng was a必经 place on the ancient road from Jianyang to Shaowu, and there are reports that not far from Nakeng Village there is a place called "Dashi Keng" (Stone-Chiseling Ravine), discovered to be a large-scale ancient quarry — this was likely a gathering place for stone masons.

Are these abacus rods here the testing ground for stone masons to display their craft, or perhaps "showrooms"?

推荐级别：★★★

朱熹墓

No.119
Tomb of Zhu Xi
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：南平建阳市黄坑镇大林谷
类型：陵寝建筑
特征标签 Highlights
凭吊朱熹及夫人刘氏合葬淳熙四年葬刘氏庆元六年归葬九峰山屏障穹隆圆形墓堆鹅卵石砌
中文 Chinese

建阳、邵武、武夷山三市交界的地方有黄坑镇，史称唐石里、嘉禾里，宋先贤朱熹及夫人刘氏合葬陵墓就坐落在后塘村的大林谷。这里曾经是一片葱郁的森林，现在看上去植被也很茂盛。树林之后遥对的是九峰山，作为大林谷的屏障。

淳熙三年（1176年）十一月，先是朱熹的夫人刘氏病逝，次年二月，朱熹葬刘氏夫人于此，显然是他亲自选好的地方。

多年后，朱熹于南宋庆元六年（1200年）在考亭之沧州精舍——就是后来的考亭书院去世，十一月归葬，与夫人永久居此了。

朱熹墓规模不大，质朴无华，但选址上佳，位于高爽之处，视野开阔。

墓园占地面积200平方米，墓园共分三层，顶层为墓室，中间为穹隆圆形墓堆，周围用小鹅卵石砌成，清代康熙五十六年（1717年）立墓碑一块于墓后，高约2米，宽0.8米，上书"宋先贤朱子，夫人刘氏墓"。

墓前有石香炉、石供桌及石华表一对，均为明代所置。历代以来，朱子墓屡经修葺。墓园早年还建有顺宁庵和翠如亭，山下还有宰木亭；入清后康熙、乾隆、嘉庆等朝均有重修，并在山下建朱子祠，后失修倾圮。墓园内现存一块长方形草坪，就是原来的顺宁庵的遗址。近年来，国内外朱子后裔经常前来祭祀，并捐资建起"思源亭"。

English

At the junction of Jianyang, Shaowu, and Wuyishan three cities there is Huangkeng Town, historically called Tangshili or Jiaheli; the joint tomb of Song sage Zhu Xi and his wife Lady Liu is located in Dalin Valley of Houtang Village.

This was once a lush forest, and now the vegetation still looks luxuriant.Behind the woods, facing in the distance, is Jiufeng Mountain (Nine Peaks Mountain), serving as a barrier for Dalin Valley.

In the eleventh month of the third year of Chunxi (1176), first Zhu Xi's wife Lady Liu died of illness; in the second month of the following year, Zhu Xi buried Lady Liu here — obviously a place he personally chose.

Years later, Zhu Xi died in the sixth year of Qingyuan (1200) of the Southern Song at Cangzhou Jingshe in Kaoting — later Kaoting Academy — and was buried here in the eleventh month, permanently residing with his wife.

Zhu Xi's tomb is not large in scale, plain and unadorned, but excellently located, in a high and dry place with open views.

The tomb garden covers 200 square meters, divided into three levels: the top level is the tomb chamber, the middle is a dome-shaped circular tomb mound, surrounded by small cobblestones; in 1717 (the 56th year of Kangxi reign, Qing), a tombstone was erected behind the tomb, about 2 meters high and 0.

8 meters wide, inscribed with "Tomb of Song Sage Zhu Zi and Lady Liu.

" In front of the tomb are a stone incense burner, stone offering table, and a pair of stone ornamental columns (huabiao), all placed in the Ming.

Through successive dynasties, Zhu Xi's tomb has been repeatedly restored.

In the early years, the tomb garden also had Shuning Nunnery and Cuiru Pavilion, and at the foot of the mountain there was Zaimu Pavilion; after entering the Qing, the Kangxi, Qianlong, and Jiaqing reigns all carried out restorations, and built a Zhu Xi Shrine at the foot of the mountain, which later fell into disrepair and collapsed.

A rectangular lawn now existing in the tomb garden is the site of the original Shuning Nunnery.

In recent years, Zhu Xi's descendants at home and abroad often come to worship, and donated to build the "Siyuan Pavilion" (Pavilion of Thinking of the Source).

推荐级别：★★★

宝峰寺

No.120
Baofeng Temple
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：元
地址：南平顺昌县大干镇上湖村
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
石结构与构造环境和布局全石仿木构造元至正二十三年始建明万历四十二年重修肥梁胖柱
中文 Chinese

宝山位于福建省顺昌县城西北部，北靠武夷山，东邻南平茫荡山，西与泰宁金湖、将乐玉华洞毗邻。宝山真的是珍稀植物的宝山，森林覆盖率95.9%以上，让人大开眼界。不去记忆什么宝山的"五绝"或是"三宝"，只是钻进参天的巨木，瞥见云雾中怒放的山花，听着成群山猴的啼鸣，便已不虚此行了。不过真正的主角还在一个大门的后边，还要走过漫长的古道。宝山寺就在这里了，云雾中好像能隐隐地听闻风铃的声音。

寺的原名是宝灵庵、宝山庙，始建于元至正二十三年（1363年），明万历四十二年（1614年）重修。

寺院由元代建的大殿和清代重建的山门、前殿、厢房、凉亭等建筑组成，令人称奇的是整座寺院从台基、地板、梁柱、屋顶到片瓦全部以石代木、仿木构造，连屋面望板也是岩石制作。

大殿为仿木构建筑，坐东南朝西北，面阔五间、进深四间，檐悬山顶。原构当为面阔三间、进深四间，明代重修时将东、西、北三面扩展，形成现有规模。

殿内砌上明造，石柱密集，当时的匠人或许对结构安全存有疑虑。梁架用巨石凿成月梁与梭柱，除两扇大门是木作外，柱、栱、斗拱、榑、屋面、瓦件、脊饰、吻等均以花岗岩石为料，构件断面皆较粗大、敦厚，颇有"肥梁胖柱"的特征。

平梁两端，异形拱、雀替等处都阴刻有纹饰，细腻精美。次间绝大部分采取压地隐起手法雕刻月梁和劄牵及两端收分的榑，梢间穿斗不用穿插枋而砌以隔墙，墙体厚逾七十公分。座斗、雀替、替木等多与梁枋石件相连雕刻成形，椽瓦以巴掌榫左右上下相合。

柱础有双层素面、单层覆盆式和八瓣覆莲式三种，并与柱顶石连为一体。屋脊两端各置石雕鱼形鸱吻，正脊中置石雕宝葫芦。

考其年代，脊樽下有"维大元至正二十三年癸卯岁七月廿八乙未日已卯时募众鼎建上祝"铭文，以及在柱、栱、斗拱、榑、屋面、瓦件上阴刻有十几段元、明、清捐舍维修题记，与明正德版的《顺昌邑志》中"宝山在娄山都，峭拔秀丽，群峰次第而列。

正峰绝顶一庵，梁柱椽瓦之类，皆断石为之"相符。这样的遗存，真是极其罕见，无疑能够拿来当作"标准样本"。同样罕见的还有大殿外石香炉上的一列对联，口气之大——"纳九州贡，化万民愆"，是谁写下的？

English

Baoshan (Precious Mountain) is located in the northwestern part of Shunchang County, Fujian Province, backed by Wuyi Mountain to the north, adjacent to Mangdang Mountain of Nanping to the east, and bordering Taining Jinhu and Jiangle Yuhua Cave to the west.

Baoshan is truly a treasure mountain of rare plants, with forest coverage over 95.9%, an eye-opener.

Without memorizing Baoshan's "Five Wonders" or "Three Treasures," just plunging into the towering giant trees, glimpsing mountain flowers blooming in the mist, and listening to the cries of troops of mountain monkeys already makes the trip worthwhile.

But the real protagonist is still behind a large gate, requiring walking a long ancient path.Baofeng Temple is here; in the mist one seems to faintly hear the sound of wind chimes.

The temple's original names were Baoling Nunnery and Baoshan Temple, first built in 1363 (the 23rd year of Zhizheng reign, Yuan) and restored in 1614 (the 42nd year of Wanli reign, Ming).

The temple consists of the Yuan-era main hall and Qing-rebuilt mountain gate, front hall, side rooms, pavilion, and other buildings.

What is amazing is that the entire temple — from platform base, floor, beams and columns, roof to individual tiles — all uses stone instead of wood, imitating timber construction; even the roof sheathing is made of rock.

The main hall is an imitation-timber building, facing northwest from the southeast, five bays wide and four deep, with an overhanging gable roof.

The original structure should have been three bays wide and four deep; during the Ming restoration, the east, west, and north sides were expanded to form the current scale.

Inside the hall, the ceiling is exposed (qishang mingzao), with dense stone columns — perhaps the craftsmen of the time had doubts about structural safety.

The beam frame uses giant stones chiseled into crescent beams (yueliang) and tapered columns (suozhu); except for the two main doors which are wooden, columns, bracket arms, bracket sets, purlins, roof, tile components, ridge ornaments, and chiwen are all made of granite, with component cross-sections all relatively large and sturdy, quite characteristic of "fat beams and plump columns.

" At both ends of the flat beams, and at special bracket sets and spandrel brackets (queti), there are intaglio-carved patterns, delicate and exquisite.

Most of the secondary bays use the relief technique of "pressing ground to conceal rise" to carve crescent beams, tie beams, and purlins with tapered ends; the end bays use column-and-tie construction without through-tie beams, instead building partition walls over 70 cm thick.

Seat brackets, spandrel brackets, and substitute brackets are mostly carved integrally with the beam and lintel stone pieces; rafters and tiles join with palm-sized tenons left-right and up-down.

Column bases come in three types: double-layer plain, single-layer inverted-basin, and eight-petal inverted-lotus, and are integrated with the column-top stones.

At both ends of the roof ridge are stone-carved fish-shaped chiwen, and in the center of the main ridge is a stone-carved precious gourd.

Examining its date, under the ridge purlin there is an inscription: "Built in the Jimao hour on the Yiwei day, the 28th of the seventh month, the Guimao year, the 23rd year of Zhizheng of the Great Yuan, through public fundraising, praying for the emperor's longevity"; and on columns, bracket arms, bracket sets, purlins, roof, and tile components, there are over a dozen intaglio inscriptions of donations and repairs from the Yuan, Ming, and Qing — matching the Ming Zhengde edition of "Shunchang County Annals": "Baoshan is in Loushan Du, steep and beautiful, with peaks arranged in order.

At the summit of the main peak is a nunnery; beams, columns, rafters, tiles and the like are all made of cut stone.

" Such a relic is truly extremely rare, and can undoubtedly be used as a "standard sample.

" Equally rare is a couplet on the stone incense burner outside the main hall, with such grandeur — "Receiving tributes from nine provinces, transforming the faults of ten thousand people" — who wrote it?

推荐级别：★★★★★

云峰寺

No.121
Yunfeng Temple
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：南平浦城县水北街镇曹村
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
木结构与构造环境和布局唐贞观年间始建唐太宗御封安禅奉佛祝圣道场明成化十八年大殿重檐歇山顶
中文 Chinese

云峰寺在曹村北面约两公里的山坳中，四周群山环抱，风景秀丽。一路走去，默默祷告寺院也如这株古树一般，没有人凭着自己的意愿"拯救"它。走在平直的古道上直奔寺院而去，感觉古道的下面有淙淙溪水流过。莫非有桥？下去一看，竟然是一座保存完好的石拱桥。桥正面的大明成化年的字迹历历在目，没想到还没进云峰寺就有此惊喜。

此桥的制式与松溪县中峰寺前面那座宋代的古桥是完全一样的，只不过那座桥完全被草木所覆盖，无法照个全景。此桥则不同，有心人特意在河堤上铺了泥土台阶以便下去参观。云峰寺始建于唐贞观年间，当年被唐太宗御封为"安禅奉佛祝圣道场"。

宋、明、清历代均有重修。现存大殿建筑重修于明成化十八年（1482年），完整保存了明代建筑原构，是寺内文物价值最高的建筑。

大殿坐南朝北，重檐歇山顶。面阔三间9.89米，进深四间。下层廊深二间，殿身部分分心槽，其上如意斗拱"编制"出来的藻井美得让人窒息。

殿内柱网排列规整，柱础为复盆式莲瓣纹，镌刻"明成化拾捌"、"单消除"、"寿炎"等字样，殿内还存放的明正德年间经住持僧认可或代写的祈福砖刻。回到室外，端详檐下斗拱，则出跳繁多，上下层分别达到九踩和七踩之多，转角处做象鼻夔龙下昂，角科之外均做翘头。真正是个宝贝啊！

无奈岁月和遗忘。为什么不能马上搭个脚手架就开始保护工作呢！忽然意识到这里空无一人，四顾之余，发现过分专注于大殿的缘故，竟然忘记细看金刚造像了。踏着精心铺设的石子走来走去，穿行于寺院之中，慢慢回复到屏声静气的心态。无论怎样的宝贝，逝去总有逝去的道理。

English

Yunfeng Temple is in a mountain hollow about two kilometers north of Cao Village, surrounded by mountains on all sides, with beautiful scenery.

Walking along, I silently prayed that the temple, like this ancient tree, would not be "saved" by anyone according to their own will.

Walking on the straight ancient path straight toward the temple, I felt a gurgling stream flowing beneath the ancient path.Could there be a bridge?

Going down to look, it turned out to be a well-preserved stone arch bridge.

The characters of the Daming Chenghua year on the front of the bridge are clearly visible — I didn't expect such a surprise before even entering Yunfeng Temple.

This bridge's form is exactly the same as the ancient Song bridge in front of Zhongfeng Temple in Songxi County, except that bridge is completely covered by vegetation, making it impossible to photograph a full view.

This bridge is different; someone with a heart specially laid mud steps on the riverbank to facilitate going down to visit.

Yunfeng Temple was first built during the Zhenguan reign of the Tang, and was imperially conferred by Emperor Taizong of Tang as the "Dojo for Peaceful Meditation, Buddha Worship, and Praying for the Sage.

" It was restored in the Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties.

The existing main hall building was restored in 1482 (the 18th year of Chenghua reign, Ming), completely preserving the original Ming Dynasty structure, and is the building with the highest cultural relic value in the temple.

The main hall faces north from the south, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof.It is three bays wide (9.

89 meters) and four bays deep.

The lower corridor is two bays deep; the hall body uses a central-column bay (fenxin cao), and the caisson ceiling "woven" by ruyi bracket sets above it is breathtakingly beautiful.

Inside the hall, the column grid is regularly arranged; the column bases are inverted-basin style with lotus-petal patterns, engraved with characters such as "Ming Chenghua 18," "Shan Xiaochu," and "Shou Yan"; the hall also stores prayer brick carvings from the Zhengde reign of Ming, approved or ghostwritten by the abbot.

Returning outside, examining the bracket sets under the eaves, there are numerous bracket projections — the upper and lower layers reaching nine-tier and seven-tier respectively; at the corners are elephant-nose kui-dragon downward ang (xiangbi kuilong xia'ang), and outside the corner bracket sets are all upward-curving ends (qiaotou).

Truly a treasure!But helplessly, time and forgetfulness.Why can't we immediately erect scaffolding and start protection work!

Suddenly realizing there was no one here, looking around, I found that due to excessive focus on the main hall, I had forgotten to examine the Vajra (Jingang) statues carefully.

Walking back and forth on the carefully laid pebbles, threading through the temple, I slowly returned to a calm and breath-holding state of mind.

No matter what kind of treasure, what passes away always has its reason for passing.

推荐级别：★★★★★

华严寺

No.122
Huayan Temple
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：唐—清
地址：南平松溪县旧县乡李墩村
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
晚期木结构与早期石构件环境和布局唐咸通八年始建明成化年间重建重檐歇山顶穿斗屋架唐代石狮子头
中文 Chinese

李墩村的华严寺处地幽静，景色宜人，香火颇盛，还流传着唐代皇族殒命于此的故事。寺院始建于唐咸通八年（867年），明代成化年间重建，清修复。坐北朝南，依次为山门、天王殿、放生池、大雄宝殿、观音殿，两侧为僧舍、香积厨等。

大殿本身就是重檐歇山顶，穿斗屋架，下层副阶深两间，加上后院的廊庑，局部形成三层屋檐，刹有气势。从室内看去，大殿上层檐宽一间、深二间，用中柱高高举起，重檐之间光线洒进来，香烟飘出去，环顾虽是香客，抬头便是清净。绕到偏院，新刷的白粉墙也烘托这样的气氛。

正值开饭的时间，寺院中素斋香气扑鼻，还有宋代淳熙已酉年福州石匠凿制的石水槽在厨房中忠于职守呢。拜访这种名声不显，于乡民意义更甚的庙宇时，躲避杂物和电线的同时，自己的关注主要在于发现一些早期的痕迹和瞥见一些意外的风景。寺内留存有石狮子头，据说是唐代的；另一尊也是唐代的吗？

鼻子很像八戒，他和狮子本应不是一对，比狮子小很多，现在两人做伴了。庙后不远山上有一座宋代建造的六角形三米高的"舍利藏"石塔，看上去如此简约现代，原有一对，其中一座在20世纪60年代被雷击倒，石构件被村民用于修复河坝，可惜也没有哪个哪怕小一点的陪伴者。

不寂寞的是青山、翠竹，人在，寺院就在，虽然千年来变换了好多模样。

English

Huayan Temple in Lidun Village is located in a quiet place with pleasant scenery and strong incense, and also circulates stories of Tang Dynasty royal family members dying here.

The temple was first built in 867 (the eighth year of Xiantong reign, Tang), rebuilt during the Chenghua reign of the Ming, and restored in the Qing.

Facing south from the north, it依次 has the mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, Free Life Pond, Mahavira Hall, and Guanyin Hall, with monk's quarters and incense kitchens on both sides.

The main hall itself has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof with a column-and-tie roof frame; the lower secondary eaves are two bays deep, and加上 the rear courtyard's corridors, locally forming three layers of eaves, quite imposing.

Looking from inside, the upper eave of the main hall is one bay wide and two deep, held high by central columns; light spills in between the double eaves, and incense smoke drifts out — looking around though there are pilgrims, looking up is purity.

Walking around to the side courtyard, the newly whitewashed walls also set off this atmosphere.

It was mealtime, and the aroma of vegetarian food in the temple was inviting; there was also a stone water trough chiseled by Fuzhou stone masons in the Jiyou year of Chunxi (Southern Song) faithfully performing its duty in the kitchen.

When visiting such temples with little fame but greater significance to villagers, while dodging clutter and wires, one's attention mainly lies in discovering some early traces and glimpsing some unexpected scenery.

Inside the temple there remains a stone lion head, said to be from the Tang; is the other one also Tang?

Its nose looks much like Bajie (Zhu Bajie); it and the lion should not be a pair, being much smaller than the lion, but now the two keep each other company.

Not far behind the temple on the mountain there is a hexagonal three-meter-high "Relic Repository" stone pagoda built in the Song, looking so minimalist and modern; originally there was a pair, one of which was struck down by lightning in the 1960s, and its stone components were used by villagers to repair the river dam — unfortunately there is not even a smaller companion.

What is not lonely is the green mountains and green bamboo; where there are people, the temple is there, though over a thousand years it has changed many forms.

推荐级别：★★

罗汉寺

No.123
Arhat Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：南平松溪县河东乡大布村
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
木结构斗拱环境和布局五代始建千年古刹康熙年重建大雄宝殿下层五踩上层七踩真昂
中文 Chinese

罗汉寺所在的大布村是一个规模很大的村落。村子傍大溪而建，村中又有小河流淌。以江氏祠堂为核心，村边还有古码头和城楼。这里的老建筑还是以山区多见的夯土为主。但大布村似乎特别注重防火墙的营造，而且形状与我们常见的马鞍墙不同，是这种阶梯形的，上面覆盖黑瓦，看上去多了几分庄重。罗汉寺位于松溪县河东乡大布村村头约200米处，寺前樱花盛开。

这是一座始建于五代时期的千年古刹，门前滚礅上的图案精美古朴，手法不像明清时期风格。寺院内第一进大殿为近代重建，第二进大雄宝殿为康熙年重建。

其外观及其引人注目的斗拱的做法与福安狮峰寺的如出一辙，下层五踩，上层七踩，下昂用的是真昂，没有用繁复的雕镂和纤细的象鼻昂。这种做法节省木料却颇费算计。斗拱之下柱枋也颇硕壮。殿内的屋架结构带有显著的历代改造痕迹，是抬梁与穿斗的结合。大雄宝殿内还是民间信仰的聚会之所。

佛像三尊、千手观音、妈祖造像不是晚近的作品，倒也相映成趣。回想起来，罗汉寺第三进院中盛开的山茶的样子挥之不去。山茶不是为植物学家而绽放，甚至不是为了担水施肥的寺院主人，她回应的只是四季。此行的目的本来很是功利，唯有自己的心绪，和着一切凡尘而必然的界定，使得写下的东西和网上的东西有所不同。

English

Dabu Village, where Arhat Temple is located, is a very large village.The village is built by a large stream, and a small river flows through the village.

With the Jiang Clan Ancestral Hall as the core, there are also ancient docks and city towers at the village edge.The old buildings here are still mainly rammed earth, common in mountainous areas.

But Dabu Village seems to pay special attention to the construction of fire walls, and their shape is different from the common saddle walls we see — they are this stepped shape, covered with black tiles on top, looking somewhat more solemn.

Arhat Temple is located about 200 meters from the head of Dabu Village, Hedong Township, Songxi County, with cherry blossoms blooming in front of the temple.

This is a thousand-year-old ancient temple first built in the Five Dynasties period; the patterns on the stone drums (gundun) in front of the gate are exquisite and ancient, with a technique unlike the Ming-Qing style.

The first hall in the temple courtyard is a modern reconstruction, and the second hall, the Mahavira Hall, was rebuilt during the Kangxi reign.

Its appearance and the striking bracket-set construction are identical to those of Shifeng Temple in Fu'an: lower layer five-tier, upper layer seven-tier, the downward ang (xia'ang) uses true ang (zhen'ang), without using intricate carving and slender elephant-nose ang.

This method saves timber but requires considerable calculation.The columns and lintels under the bracket sets are also quite sturdy.

The roof frame structure inside the hall shows significant traces of successive modifications, being a combination of beam-lifting (tailiang) and column-and-tie (chuandou).

The Mahavira Hall is also a gathering place for folk beliefs.

The three Buddha statues, Thousand-Hand Guanyin, and Mazu statues are not recent works, but rather complement each other interestingly.

In retrospect, the appearance of the blooming camellia in the third courtyard of Arhat Temple lingers.

The camellia does not bloom for botanists, nor even for the temple master who carries water and fertilizes; she responds only to the four seasons.

The purpose of this trip was originally quite utilitarian; only my own state of mind, along with all the mundane and inevitable definitions, makes what is written different from what is online.

推荐级别：★★★★

清凉寺

No.124
Qingliang Temple
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：明—清
地址：南平松溪县茶坪乡吴山头村
类型：宗教建筑
特征标签 Highlights
湛卢景色晚期木结构环境和布局唐神龙元年湛卢庵欧冶子铸剑之地明崇祯元年重建
中文 Chinese

《三国演义》里面长坂坡一段描写的曹操本有一把欧冶子铸造的宝剑，叫湛卢，特派一位背剑官夏侯先生掌管，结果被子龙夺去。欧冶子乃春秋吴国人，受越王允常之请，铸名剑五口，叫湛卢、鱼肠、磐郢、巨阙、纯钩。湛卢山便曾经是欧冶子铸剑之地。登山为的是拜访清凉寺，登山就要路过这样的小村庄——吴山头。雨中，五彩的石头路有些湿滑，雾中的古树暗示你已经走进了湛卢的云海。

古道，连绵不断，只有没完没了的雨和风景，很想把此书变成画册。既无导游也无指示牌，好处正在没人打扰，也没有日头提醒时间。终于到了。清凉寺虽踞山巅，而背后有湛云峰可倚，周围翠色四顾、群山若拱。据史料记载，清凉寺原为湛卢庵，始建于唐神龙元年（705年），后毁。

宋元符二年（1099年）为纪念县令周才在山上祈雨，在旧址建祠，后又毁建多次。

明崇祯元年（1628年）重建，改名为湛卢禅院，清末宣统二年（1910年）经过大修，改名为清凉寺。崇祯、宣统，两个都是末世，但毕竟是王朝。

据寺里一块明代碑记载，这里气候清凉，"暑月寒衣"，想必寺名当取是意。山顶的庙宇不像一般寺院宽敞平铺的格局，外面看起来更像一座民居，里面则别有洞天。院中天井的营造使寺院的格局和采光都很有特色，殿内也是开若干天窗采光。院中如果不是完全漆成红色和过多的杂物，还是很古朴的，柱子的石墩都是很老的。

也许是此山太高，上来一次不容易，所以寺院反而保存得比较完好，所以后来的加固和新装置不会太讲究。虽然山中空无一人，寺庙里还是比较热闹，前来朝拜祈福的人们满脸喜气；廊下的长凳告诉人们可以把这里当作山上的聚会所。

English

In the "Romance of the Three Kingdoms," the Changban Slope passage describes that Cao Cao originally had a precious sword forged by Ou Yezi called Zhanlu, specially entrusted to a sword-carrying officer Xiahou, but it was ultimately seized by Zhao Zilong.

Ou Yezi was a person of Wu in the Spring and Autumn period; invited by King Yunchang of Yue, he forged five famous swords: Zhanlu, Yuchang, Panying, Juque, and Chungou.

Zhanlu Mountain was once the place where Ou Yezi forged swords.Climbing the mountain was to visit Qingliang Temple; climbing requires passing through such a small village — Wushantou.

In the rain, the colorful stone path is somewhat slippery, and the ancient trees in the mist hint that you have entered the sea of clouds of Zhanlu.

The ancient path stretches endlessly, with only endless rain and scenery; I very much want to turn this book into a picture album.

Neither guide nor signposts, the advantage is that no one disturbs, nor does the sun remind of time.Finally arrived.

Though Qingliang Temple perches on the mountain peak, it has Zhanyun Peak to lean against behind, surrounded by greenery on all sides with mountains arching around.

According to historical records, Qingliang Temple was originally Zhanlu Nunnery, first built in 705 (the first year of Shenlong reign, Tang), later destroyed.

In 1099 (the second year of Yuanfu reign, Song), to commemorate County Magistrate Zhou Cai praying for rain on the mountain, a shrine was built on the old site, later destroyed and rebuilt multiple times.

In 1628 (the first year of Chongzhen reign, Ming), it was rebuilt and renamed Zhanlu Chan Monastery; in 1910 (the second year of Xuantong reign, late Qing), after major repairs, it was renamed Qingliang Temple.

Chongzhen and Xuantong — both were late dynasties, but after all they were dynasties.

According to a Ming stele in the temple, the climate here is cool, "wearing warm clothes in hot months" — presumably the temple name takes this meaning.

The mountain-top temple does not have the spacious, flat layout of ordinary temples; from outside it looks more like a residence, but inside there is a different world.

The construction of the courtyard skylight makes the temple's layout and lighting distinctive, and the halls also have several skylights for lighting.

If the courtyard were not completely painted red and cluttered with too many objects, it would be quite simple and ancient; the stone bases of the columns are all very old.

Perhaps because this mountain is too high and coming up once is not easy, the temple has instead been relatively well preserved, so later reinforcements and new installations are not too elaborate.

Though the mountain is empty of people, the temple is still quite lively; people coming to worship and pray have joyful faces; the long benches under the corridors tell people they can treat this as a gathering place on the mountain.

推荐级别：★★★

中峰寺

No.125
Zhongfeng Temple
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：南平松溪县旧县乡
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
晚期木结构环境和布局闽浙边境有名寺庙唐景福元年始建清康熙五十年重建规划四面环山如抱
中文 Chinese

中峰寺是闽浙边境地区有名的寺庙。坐落于旧县乡境内武当山麓。寺庙四面环山如抱，雾竹叠翠，远望如宝莲盛开，盘桓中古村静寂。自古以来，当地乡人就有金鸡应化、九龙吐水等许多的传说。史料记载，中峰寺始建于唐景福元年（892年）。

现存的规模是清康熙五十年（1711年）重建时规划的，其中修复的大雄宝殿应属于当时旧作，可惜略显单薄、热烈和拼凑。至于其他几座殿堂，就是近年所造的了。

English

Zhongfeng Temple is a famous temple in the Fujian-Zhejiang border region.It is located at the foot of Wudang Mountain in Jiuxian Township.

The temple is surrounded by mountains on all sides like an embrace, with misty bamboo and layered greenery; from afar it looks like a precious lotus in full bloom, and wandering among it the ancient village is silent.

Since ancient times, local villagers have had many legends such as the Golden Chicken's manifestation and the Nine Dragons Spitting Water.

Historical records show that Zhongfeng Temple was first built in 892 (the first year of Jingfu reign, Tang).

The existing scale was planned during the reconstruction in 1711 (the 50th year of Kangxi reign, Qing); the restored Mahavira Hall should belong to the original work of that time, unfortunately appearing somewhat thin, overly vibrant, and patchwork.

As for the other several halls, they were built in recent years.

推荐级别：★★★

交龙桥

No.126
Jiaolong Bridge
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：南平政和县澄源乡大梨溪村
类型：桥梁·木拱桥
特征标签 Highlights
木拱桥结构桥村关系古道线索大梨溪桥清道光十五年重建重檐歇山顶抬梁式
中文 Chinese

从寿宁奔往政和县的路上，进入深山，便美不胜收了。"政和天空"一语，说的是天空，也是心境，还是希望。交龙桥位于政和县澄源乡大梨溪村，所以也叫大梨溪桥。一路总是沿着一条大溪前行。如果电子导航不能直达大梨溪村，就先到一个叫"新康"的公路边小村，附近有个岔路写着"象鼻亭"，延此岔路走到底就是大梨溪村。本来附近十几公里有个赤溪村，那里有个赤溪桥。

我走到这个流着小瀑布的涵洞前止步了，外面有牌子说是塌方禁止入内。犹豫了一下，折返了。交龙桥属于小型桥，其建制和附近的三仙桥、七仙桥、院林桥等近似。桥长29米，宽4.7米，拱跨13.3米。

桥屋伴随桥拱作优美的弧线，中间用重檐歇山顶，抬梁式结构。虽然略显残破，但风韵犹存，可以想象盛时的样子多么优雅。此桥始建年代不详，重建于清道光十五年（1835年）。

廊屋内部的题记不仅提供了重建年代信息，更说明政和县正堂也曾捐俸。

English

On the road from Shouning to Zhenghe County, entering the deep mountains, the beauty becomes endless.The phrase "Zhenghe Sky" speaks of the sky, also of the state of mind, and also of hope.

Jiaolong Bridge is located in Dalixi Village, Chengyuan Township, Zhenghe County, so it is also called Dalixi Bridge.Along the way one always follows a large stream.

If electronic navigation cannot reach Dalixi Village directly, first go to a small roadside village called "Xinkang," near which there is a fork road marked "Xiangbi Pavilion"; following this fork to the end leads to Dalixi Village.

Originally there was a Chixi Village over ten kilometers away, with a Chixi Bridge there.

I stopped before this culvert with a small waterfall flowing through it; outside there was a sign saying landslide, no entry.After hesitating a moment, I turned back.

Jiaolong Bridge is a small bridge, its construction similar to the nearby Sanxian Bridge, Qixian Bridge, and Yuanlin Bridge.The bridge is 29 meters long, 4.

7 meters wide, with an arch span of 13.3 meters.

The bridge house follows the bridge arch in a graceful arc, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof in the middle and a beam-lifting structure.

Though somewhat dilapidated, its charm remains, and one can imagine how elegant it was in its prime.

The bridge's founding date is unknown; it was rebuilt in 1835 (the 15th year of Daoguang reign, Qing).

The inscriptions inside the covered hall not only provide information on the reconstruction date, but also show that the county magistrate of Zhenghe County also donated his salary.

推荐级别：★★★★

英节庙

No.127
Yingjie Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：南平政和县杨源乡杨源村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
庙宇格局环境和布局戏曲文化北宋崇宁年间始建康熙元年大殿道光三十年戏台
中文 Chinese

位于政和县南部的杨源乡杨源村，虽然地处有些偏僻，但非常的干净规整，明显经过精心的管理。村中有条小河流过，名叫鲤鱼溪。中午过后是孩子们上学的时间，村里村外到处是小孩子和家长；村中有妈祖庙里的泥偶，也多是妈妈带着小孩的形象。

一路走来，眼前风光尽被一座豪华的廊桥所掩，看到英节庙了，在那里，不悲也不喜。这是一座紧凑的院落，二层的房连着戏台和大殿，始建于北宋崇宁年间（1102—1106年），元、明时期均有修建。

现存建筑中，大殿为康熙元年（1662年）所建，戏台为道光三十年（1850年）重建。英节庙是用来纪念历史人物张谨的。唐乾符年间（874—879年），黄巢农民军入闽，唐王朝以张谨为福建招讨使，率官兵数万与黄巢起义军激战。

张谨战死，葬于铁山。后在张谨身亡地夏山修建张谨庙，北宋崇宁年间追谥昭烈，赐张谨庙为"英节大观"，并增建县城、杨源等三处英节庙。张谨后裔在杨源定居繁衍，此地多数人姓张。每年村中二月初九，八月初六有两次祭祖活动，因此杨源英节庙会祭祖味道十分浓厚。

英节庙戏台上演的是四平戏——一个珍贵的戏曲品种，一个流行在当地的古老曲种，本是随着当初人们的迁徙由中原地区带来，戏曲的发音也曾经用的是中原古音。四平戏在当地盛极一时，但现在逐渐式微。戏台照壁上保存着珍贵的戏神壁画，被载入《中国戏曲志》。我们有幸见到了四平戏剧团的张老师，他深爱着自己的戏曲事业，也深爱着宁静的乡村生活。

台柱上两幅楹联写道，"三五人可做千军万马，六七步如行四海九州"，"常将旧事比新事，聊把今人做古人"。戏曲的写真，人生的常理。

English

Yangyuan Village in Yangyuan Township, southern Zhenghe County, though somewhat remote, is very clean and orderly, clearly under careful management.

A small river flows through the village, called Carp Stream.

After noon is the time for children to go to school; inside and outside the village there are children and parents everywhere; in the village there are clay figurines in the Mazu Temple, mostly depicting mothers with young children.

Along the way, the scenery before my eyes was entirely overshadowed by a luxurious covered bridge; then I saw Yingjie Temple, where there is neither sorrow nor joy.

This is a compact courtyard, with two-story rooms connecting to the stage and the main hall, first built during the Chongning reign of the Northern Song (1102–1106), with constructions in both the Yuan and Ming periods.

Among the existing buildings, the main hall was built in 1662 (the first year of Kangxi reign), and the stage was rebuilt in 1850 (the 30th year of Daoguang reign).

Yingjie Temple was built to commemorate the historical figure Zhang Jin.

During the Qianfu reign of the Tang (874–879), Huang Chao's peasant army entered Fujian; the Tang dynasty appointed Zhang Jin as the Fujian Recruitment and Pacification Commissioner, leading tens of thousands of official troops in fierce battle with Huang Chao's rebel army.

Zhang Jin died in battle and was buried in Tieshan.

Later, at Xiashan where Zhang Jin died, a Zhang Jin Temple was built; during the Chongning reign of the Northern Song, he was posthumously honored as Zhaolie, and the Zhang Jin Temple was granted the name "Yingjie Daguan," with three additional Yingjie Temples built in the county seat, Yangyuan, and elsewhere.

Zhang Jin's descendants settled and multiplied in Yangyuan, and most people here are surnamed Zhang.

Every year the village holds two ancestor-worship activities on the ninth day of the second lunar month and the sixth day of the eighth lunar month, so the Yangyuan Yingjie Temple fair has a very strong ancestor-worship flavor.

Performed on the Yingjie Temple stage is Siping Opera — a precious opera genre, an ancient tune popular locally, originally brought from the Central Plains region with the migration of people at that time; the pronunciation of the opera also once used the ancient Central Plains pronunciation.

Siping Opera was once extremely popular locally, but is now gradually declining.Precious opera-deity murals are preserved on the stage's back wall, recorded in the "Annals of Chinese Opera.

" We were fortunate to meet Teacher Zhang of the Siping Opera Troupe, who deeply loves his opera career and also deeply loves the quiet rural life.

Two couplets on the stage pillars read: "Three or five people can play a thousand troops and ten thousand horses; six or seven steps are like traveling the four seas and nine provinces," and "Often compare old affairs with new affairs; let us treat modern people as ancient people.

" The realism of opera, the common sense of life.

推荐级别：★★★

镇龟塔

No.128
Zhengui Tower
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：南平政和县澄源乡澄源村
类型：宗教建筑·石结构
特征标签 Highlights
石塔形制比例尺度风景环境明隆庆六年建七级浮屠石构实心塔六角形平面
中文 Chinese

进入政和县境内的澄源乡，在路边看到了这个新版的廊桥，而且是纯木结构的，外形潇洒大方，顶部弧线流畅自然，顶部做了三个小阁楼，中间加重檐桥亭，不知道纯池镇的院林桥年轻时是不是这个样子。仿佛是为了演示一下廊桥的功能，此时突然下起雨来，人们纷纷到桥中躲避。

不经意回头就是镇龟塔了，古朴，典雅，就这么默默地立在新廊桥对面公路边的菜地里。镇龟塔建于明隆庆六年（1572年），是个七级浮屠，石构实心塔，平面呈六角形，体量不是很大，葫芦形塔刹，通高5.2米。塔座为须弥座造型，束腰处及上袱凿有力士像、仰莲纹饰和文字铭刻。

塔身每层高60.63厘米，塔座以上四层，每层每面雕有佛像，浮雕精美，手法古朴飘逸，人物表情栩栩如生，寥寥数笔竟勾勒出悲天悯人之像。不幸文物保护碑刻标志倒在地上断成两截，竟分辨不出此文属于省保还是县保，我们暂且自定省保罢。澄源村附近文物古迹甚多，此地必然也是人文荟萃之地，走了没多远公路边又见到一座古刹。

古刹位于公路边的田间，不知道名字，只见到大殿匾额上写有"梧桐宝殿"，梁柱上写有"大明嘉靖年仍旧重建"，看来又是一千年古寺，明代依旧式重建的。从重檐翘角复杂的木结构可见大殿内部之一斑。可惜天晚了，雨中叩门无人应答。

附近就是佛子山景区，傍晚山中无人，车行山中，无穷美景从窗边眼前掠过，这是对家人遥远的担心的慰藉。

English

Entering Chengyuan Township within Zhenghe County, by the roadside I saw this new version of a covered bridge, and it is of pure timber structure, with a handsome and generous appearance, smooth and natural top arc, with three small pavilions on top and a double-eave bridge pavilion in the middle — I wonder if Yuanlin Bridge in Chunchi Town looked like this when young.

As if to demonstrate the function of a covered bridge, it suddenly started raining at this moment, and people rushed to take shelter in the bridge.

Casually turning around, there was Zhengui Tower — simple, elegant, just standing silently in the vegetable field by the highway opposite the new covered bridge.

Zhengui Tower was built in 1572 (the sixth year of Longqing reign, Ming), a seven-story pagoda (七级浮屠), a solid stone tower with a hexagonal plan, not very large in volume, with a gourd-shaped finial and a total height of 5.

2 meters.The tower base is in the xumi pedestal style, with the waist and upper part chiseled with strongman figures, upward-lotus patterns, and text inscriptions.Each layer of the tower body is 60.

63 centimeters high; the four layers above the base have Buddha statues carved on each face, with exquisite reliefs, simple and elegant technique, and lifelike character expressions — with just a few strokes, they actually delineate compassionate figures.

Unfortunately, the cultural heritage protection stele marker lies on the ground broken in two, and one cannot even tell whether this site belongs to provincial or county protection; we shall tentatively designate it as provincial protection.

There are many cultural relics and historic sites near Chengyuan Village, so this place must also be a gathering place of culture; not far along the highway, another ancient temple was seen.

The ancient temple is located in the fields by the highway, its name unknown; only the main hall plaque reads "Wutong Baodian" (Paulownia Treasure Hall), and the beams and columns read "Rebuilt in the Jiajing year of the Great Ming following the old style" — it seems to be another thousand-year-old ancient temple, rebuilt in the Ming following the old style.

From the complex timber structure of the double eaves and upturned corners, one can glimpse the interior of the main hall.

Unfortunately it was getting late, and knocking on the door in the rain got no answer.

Nearby is the Fozishan (Buddha Child Mountain) scenic area; in the evening the mountains are empty of people, driving through the mountains, endless beauty flashes past the window and before the eyes — this is consolation for the distant worry of family.

推荐级别：★★★

莆田市 Putian City

22 处

大宗伯第

No.129
Mansion of Minister of Rituals
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：莆田市城厢区长寿街庙前路
类型：家教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
斗拱拆换下来的老构件明万历二十年建礼部尚书陈经邦府第百廿间大厝抬梁与穿斗结合
中文 Chinese

大宗伯第在庙前路（俗称铁树里），是明代礼部尚书陈经邦的府第，建成于明万历二十年（1592年）。

系按明制，前后七进，核心是五开间三厅六房，以大厅为主轴线左右对称布置，加上门房，护厝，共有大小房间一百多间，号称"百廿间大厝"，是明代一品官典型的府第豪宅。

整个大厝的梁宇架采用抬梁与穿斗相结合方式，体现出明代建筑的大方简约之美。现今虽然是大杂院，所幸房子的外观没有发生太大改变，不失为目前莆田地区保存最完整的明代宅第建筑。

陈经邦（1537—1616年），字公望，嘉靖四十四年（1565年）进士，授翰林院编修，神宗在东宫时，曾被选任讲读官，神宗临朝后，备受宠顾，官职连升至礼部尚书。万历十三年（1585年）因与宰相意见不合，疏请罢归，遂开始筹划建造宅第，至1592年方全部完成。

这里还有御赐的匾额为证，"启沃亲臣"四个字道出大宗伯的生平，即不但是皇帝的老师，而且关系亲近。从书法的角度来看，神宗的字写得极好，也该归于老师启沃之功。万历皇帝一度被妖魔化，说他不理朝政，大办特务机关云云。实际上万历皇帝在位时间较长，文化经济有一定的发展，只不过他和当朝的文官关系不好，所以懒理朝政，但又派东厂、西厂去监督牵制他们，所以那些文官恨极了，史书上把他描写得很不堪。

其实东厂西厂虽然残暴，但更多是针对当时腐败的官僚系统。万历皇帝本人是性情中人，据说定陵的地宫竣工，他曾亲自躺进棺木中体验并大呼"合身"，还在地宫中宴请群臣，其潇洒的唯物主义精神是否也是受眼前这位老师的熏陶？院中的石基竟是用御赐的石碑铺就，自然是子孙们倦勤了；台基石缝间长出顽强的小草，台基之上可爱的小童车，希望新生命的勃勃生机可以唤醒厚重的过去。

前门当年帝师的后人们在悠闲地享受下午时光，不像待唤醒和救助的样子，会不会对大杂院也偶尔赞一声"合身"？

English

Dazongbo Di (Mansion of the Grand Master of Rituals) is on Miaoqian Road (commonly called Tieshuli), the residence of Chen Jingbang, Minister of Rites in the Ming Dynasty, completed in 1592 (the 20th year of Wanli reign, Ming).

Built according to Ming regulations, it has seven courtyards front to back; the core is five bays, three halls, and six rooms, symmetrically arranged left and right with the main hall as the central axis, plus gatehouses and side wings (hucuo), totaling over one hundred rooms of various sizes, known as the "120-room Great Mansion" — a typical first-rank official's mansion of the Ming.

The beam frame of the entire mansion uses a combination of beam-lifting (tailiang) and column-and-tie (chuandou) methods, embodying the generous and minimalist beauty of Ming architecture.

Although it is now a mixed-use courtyard (dazayuan), fortunately the exterior of the house has not changed much, and it remains the most completely preserved Ming Dynasty residential building in the Putian area.

Chen Jingbang (1537–1616), courtesy name Gongwang, became a jinshi in 1565 (the 44th year of Jiajing reign), was appointed Hanlin Academy compiler, and when Shenzong was in the Eastern Palace, he was selected as a lecturer; after Shenzong ascended the throne, he was highly favored and promoted successively to Minister of Rites.

In 1585 (the 13th year of Wanli reign), due to disagreement with the Grand Secretary, he petitioned to retire and began planning the residence, which was only fully completed in 1592.

There is also an imperially bestowed plaque as evidence; the four characters "Qiwo Qinchen" (Enlightened and Trusted Minister) reveal Dazongbo's life — not only was he the emperor's teacher, but also closely related.

From a calligraphic perspective, Shenzong's handwriting is excellent, which should also be attributed to the teacher's enlightenment.

Emperor Wanli was once demonized, said to ignore government affairs and run secret police agencies.

In fact, Wanli reigned for a long time, with certain cultural and economic development; it was just that he had poor relations with the civil officials of his court, so he was lazy in governing, but sent the Eastern and Western Depots to supervise and contain them, which made those civil officials hate him deeply, and history books describe him very poorly.

In fact, although the Eastern and Western Depots were brutal, they were more aimed at the corrupt bureaucratic system of the time.

Emperor Wanli himself was a person of temperament; it is said that when the underground palace of Dingling was completed, he personally lay in the coffin to experience it and exclaimed "fits well," and even bantered with ministers in the underground palace — was his dashing materialistic spirit also influenced by this teacher before him?

The stone bases in the courtyard were actually paved with imperially bestowed stone tablets, naturally because descendants grew tired of diligence; stubborn grass grows in the cracks of the platform stone, and a cute little stroller on the platform hopes the vigorous vitality of new life can awaken the heavy past.

The descendants of the former imperial teacher at the front gate are leisurely enjoying the afternoon, not looking like they need awakening or rescue — might they occasionally praise the mixed courtyard with a "fits well"?

中文 Chinese

莆田市区之西北的东岩山，即东山，古称乌石山，又名麟山。数字控的人们把"东山晓旭"归入为莆田二十四景之一。但是如果没有山中的报恩寺，闽北闽西大山里的"晓旭胜景"不逊于此者估计不下万计。

东岩报恩教寺，俗称东山报恩寺，创建于宋淳化元年（990年），元、明代屡有重修。明万历三十二年（1604年）请赐藏经。

现存寺院建筑为1988年修复，改山门修建为天王殿，另建石牌坊式山门。或许是有塔镇兹的缘故，新的建筑并不唐突，红色的油漆也显得比较沉稳，没有随着致富的脚步快乐地舞蹈。

大殿中还保留一些古老的瓜楞石柱，但真正的魂灵是大雄宝殿后的报恩寺塔，又称东岩山石塔。建塔日期可以追溯到宋淳化元年（990年），明代局部依宋制重修。塔是典型的石构仿木楼阁式，平面八角形，三层。

塔身四面开拱券式门，塔门两侧雕金刚力士，情态皆生动；塔基采用典型的早期须弥座形式，周遭束腰的壶门中浮雕狮子；塔檐口隐刻出筒板瓦，檐下层层半混轮廓的出挑象征斗拱。塔内空间并不局促，内壁砌有...

English

Dongyan Mountain, northwest of Putian city center, also known as Dongshan, anciently called Wushi Mountain, also named Linshan.

Numerically-minded people classify "Dongshan Dawn" as one of Putian's Twenty-Four Scenes.

But without the Baoen Temple in the mountain, there are probably no fewer than ten thousand "dawn scenic spots" in the great mountains of northern and western Fujian that are no less impressive.

Dongyan Baoen Temple, commonly called Dongshan Baoen Temple, was founded in 990 (the first year of Chunhua reign, Song), with repeated restorations in the Yuan and Ming.

In 1604 (the 32nd year of Wanli reign, Ming), it requested and received an imperial grant of the Buddhist canon.

The existing temple buildings were restored in 1988, with the mountain gate rebuilt as the Heavenly King Hall and an additional stone-paifang-style mountain gate.

Perhaps because a pagoda guards this place, the new buildings are not obtrusive, and the red paint appears relatively steady, not dancing joyfully with the pace of getting rich.

Some ancient melon-shaped (gualeng) stone columns remain in the main hall, but the true soul is the Baoen Temple Pagoda behind the Mahavira Hall, also called Dongyanshan Stone Pagoda.

The pagoda's construction date can be traced back to 990 (the first year of Chunhua reign, Song), with partial restoration following Song regulations in the Ming.

The pagoda is a typical stone imitation-timber multi-story style, octagonal in plan, with three stories.

The pagoda body has arched doors on four sides, with Vajra warriors (Jingang Lishi) carved on both sides of the doors, all vivid in expression; the pagoda base uses a typical early xumi pedestal form, with lions in relief in the hupumen (niche doors) of the surrounding waist; the pagoda eaves have hidden carvings of cylindrical and flat tiles, and under the eaves, layered semi-circular projecting contours symbolize bracket sets.

The interior space of the pagoda is not cramped, with the inner walls built of...

谯楼

Watchtower

城市格局气氛小型天安门二层大城楼下层九间上层九间屋顶厦两头三段
中文 Chinese

出了大宗伯第，徜徉于莆田市中心的老街巷。莆田的历史悠久，自古商业发达，在现代化的高楼大厦之间仍然掩盖不住旧日的市井繁华之气。那股气质就是繁华紧张的商场中随处可见的灵魂的闲暇。"听谯楼，打罢了，二更鼓响……"市中心保存基本完好的古谯楼，样子有点像小型的天安门。二层的大城楼，下层一排有九间，上层算上周围廊也有九间；屋顶厦两头，一排分成三段，增加轮廓线的变化，避免了单调感。

硕大的城台只有当心一洞券道，早已不是人们穿行的通路。一眼望去，就是摊点，再远就是快餐店，一种奇特的穿越时空的对视。券洞边没有生意，百无聊赖的摊主自顾自摆弄着手机，是一副全国人民都有的模样。四顾之下，谯楼东南侧就是修葺一新的文峰天后宫和三代祠。依然属于那种被热烈的商业烘托着的热烈的仿古口味。随便停放的车辆是在现实的挤压下对父母说教的"选择性忽视"。

English

Leaving Dazongbo Di, one wanders through the old streets and alleys in central Putian.

Putian has a long history and has been commercially developed since ancient times; between modern high-rise buildings, the old bustling market atmosphere still cannot be concealed.

That quality is the leisure of the soul visible everywhere in the bustling and tense marketplace."Listening to the watchtower, the second watch drum has sounded...

" The ancient watchtower, basically well-preserved in the city center, looks a bit like a miniature Tiananmen.

It is a two-story great gate tower; the lower level has a row of nine bays, and the upper level, including the surrounding corridor, also has nine bays; the roof has two gable ends (xia liangtou), with a row divided into three sections, increasing the variation of the silhouette and avoiding monotony.

The massive gate platform has only one arched passage in the center, long no longer a path for people to pass through.

At a glance, there are stalls, and further away are fast-food restaurants — a strange time-traveling gaze.

There is no business by the archway, and the bored stall owner fiddles with his phone by himself, a look shared by people all over the country.

Looking around, southeast of the watchtower are the newly renovated Wenfeng Tianhou Palace and Sandai Ancestral Hall.

Still belonging to that enthusiastic antique-imitating flavor set off by enthusiastic commerce.Casually parked vehicles are a "selective neglect" of parental teachings under the pressure of reality.

兴化府城隍庙

No.132
City God Temple in Xinghua Prefecture
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：宋—明
地址：莆田市荔城区西北端元妙观西
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
寺院格局石结构古塔明洪武三年初建弘治二年正殿万历十九年仪门天启四年后殿
中文 Chinese

可以想象不远的几年后，政府将把庙前路、大宗伯第这一区域整治得古色古香，兴化府城隍庙面前的一切将相当堂皇，我们的车子也不能方便地停靠在马路边的树荫下了——虽然今天还不是。此刻兴化府城隍庙新建的大门仿佛一位穿了古装的姑娘站在穿便装的警察或保安中间。

兴化府城隍庙在明洪武三年（1370年）初建，后代屡有扩建，正殿为弘治二年（1489年）始建，仪门系万历十九年（1591年）建，后殿建于天启四年（1624年）。

此后历代直至光绪年间，先后经历多次维修工程。20世纪五六十年代间，整个庙宇改作他用。至20世纪90年代，仅存受损的仪门及较完整的正、后殿。近年重新募资修复，并新建大门。

现存建筑自中轴线由南向北，依次为：屏墙、外石埕、大门、前内埕及甬道、仪门、戏台、后内埕及甬道、月台（正殿丹墀）、正殿、后殿。其中，仪门、正殿和后殿为明代建筑遗存，系历史价值最高者。

正殿是城隍庙的主体建筑，建于弘治二年（1489年），面阔五间，进深四间，重檐歇山顶。

后殿建于天启四年（1624年），原奉祀明代敕封淑德夫人（即陈文龙母亲，陈瓒的宗嫂），故又称为"夫人妈殿"。

English

One can imagine that in a few years, the government will renovate the Miaoqian Road and Dazongbo Di area into an antique style, and everything in front of Xinghua Prefecture City God Temple will be quite grand; our car will no longer be able to conveniently park under the shade of trees by the roadside — though today is not yet that day.

At this moment, the newly built gate of Xinghua Prefecture City God Temple is like a girl in ancient costume standing among police or security guards in casual clothes.

Xinghua Prefecture City God Temple was first built in 1370 (the third year of Hongwu reign, Ming), with repeated expansions by later generations; the main hall was first built in 1489 (the second year of Hongzhi reign), the ceremonial gate (yimen) was built in 1591 (the 19th year of Wanli reign), and the rear hall was built in 1624 (the fourth year of Tianqi reign).

Thereafter, through successive dynasties until the Guangxu reign, it underwent multiple repair projects.During the 1950s and 1960s, the entire temple was converted to other uses.

By the 1990s, only the damaged ceremonial gate and the relatively complete main and rear halls remained.In recent years, funds were raised again for restoration, and a new gate was built.

The existing buildings, along the central axis from south to north, are依次: screen wall, outer stone courtyard, gate, front inner courtyard and passage, ceremonial gate, stage, rear inner courtyard and passage, moon platform (main hall's red stone platform), main hall, rear hall.

Among them, the ceremonial gate, main hall, and rear hall are Ming Dynasty architectural remains, of the highest historical value.

The main hall is the main building of the City God Temple, built in 1489 (the second year of Hongzhi reign), five bays wide and four deep, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof.

The rear hall was built in 1624 (the fourth year of Tianqi reign), originally enshrining the Ming-imperially-conferred Lady Shude (i.e.

, Chen Wenlong's mother, Chen Zan's clan sister-in-law), hence also called the "Lady Mom Hall."

中文 Chinese

不知是元妙观保佑了现在的砺青中学，还是砺青中学已经成为元妙观的靠山，身处闹市，院子规整的布置还是围出一方静谧之地，可以凭此想象当初地处城郊，临水而建的盛时景象。

元妙观始建于唐贞观二年（628年），北宋大中祥符八年（1015年）重建，改名为"天庆观"，元代称"玄妙观"，至清代康熙年间为避皇帝讳又改称"元妙观"。

观内现存建筑有山门、三清殿及东、西岳殿各一座。正门虽设而长关，木结构古朴，或可追溯到明代；进入拜谒，要走或东或西的旁门；东偏院保存着古碑刻和管理用房，西院辟为文化馆，...

English

I wonder whether Yuanmiao Temple blesses the current Liqing Middle School, or whether Liqing Middle School has become the backer of Yuanmiao Temple; located in the busy city, the orderly layout of the courtyard still encloses a quiet place, from which one can imagine the prosperous scene when it was originally located on the city outskirts, built by the water.

Yuanmiao Temple was first built in 628 (the second year of Zhenguan reign, Tang), rebuilt in 1015 (the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu reign, Northern Song), and renamed "Tianqing Temple"; in the Yuan it was called "Xuanmiao Temple," and in the Qing Kangxi reign, to avoid the emperor's name taboo, it was renamed "Yuanmiao Temple.

" The existing buildings in the temple include the mountain gate, Sanqing Hall, and one each of the Eastern and Western Peak Halls.

Although the main gate is set, it is long closed; the timber structure is simple and ancient, perhaps traceable to the Ming; to enter and worship, one must take the side gate either east or west; the eastern side courtyard preserves ancient stele carvings and management rooms, and the western courtyard is converted into a cultural center, .

..
