正顺庙

No.151
Zhengshun Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明市梅列区列西街道中心沙溪河畔
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
寺院格局早期建筑痕迹南宋绍定六年为祀奉谢佑将军而建三明市区始建最早保存最完好木结构道教建筑广惠将军显烈尊王宋孝宗赐正顺庙额
中文 Chinese

三明正顺庙最早是南宋绍定六年（1233年）为祀奉北宋邑人谢佑将军而建，堪称三明市区始建年代最早、保存最完好的一座木结构道教建筑。

谢佑有着不凡的道教渊源，羽化升仙后，朝廷敕封他为"广惠将军显烈尊王"，南宋淳熙十六年（1189年），宋孝宗赐"正顺庙"额。庙的大门是1984年新建的。"鲤园"的名字来自列西地区鲤鱼一样的地段形状，而庙址又恰恰在鱼嘴的地方。

山门的做法还是继承了当地晚清繁复的建制，这里带翅膀的仙女赫然在目，是有趣的主题。

正顺庙宇为单檐悬山顶式，六架椽屋分心用三柱，斗拱结构和屋架保留完整，经过元、明、清时期多次重修。

柱基、台阶之中定有始建时的遗物，代表性的是素面覆盆式石柱础；而木结构部分则历代做法特征杂陈，保存丰富的历史信息，带有早期痕迹的是几根古朴的梭柱。院中留下来古老石作的痕迹满目皆是。地上所铺的石材最为新奇有趣，重复使用了大量石栏板、云拱赑顶，莫非是宋代的遗物？

English

Sanming Zhengshun Temple was最早 built in 1233 (the sixth year of Shaoding reign, Southern Song) to enshrine General Xie You, a local of the Northern Song, and can be called the earliest-founded and best-preserved timber-structure Taoist building in downtown Sanming.

Xie You had an extraordinary Taoist origin; after his ascension as an immortal, the court conferred on him the title "General Guanghui, King of Manifest Heroism"; in 1189 (the 16th year of Chunxi reign, Southern Song), Emperor Xiaozong of Song bestowed the plaque "Zhengshun Temple.

" The temple's gate was newly built in 1984.The name "Liyuan" (Carp Garden) comes from the carp-shaped terrain of the Liexi area, and the temple site is precisely at the "fish mouth.

" The construction of the mountain gate still inherits the complex local late-Qing style; here, winged fairies are clearly visible, an interesting theme.

Zhengshun Temple has a single-eave overhanging gable roof, with a six-rafter hall using three columns in the central-bay arrangement (fenxin yong sanzhu); the bracket-set structure and roof frame are completely preserved, having undergone multiple restorations in the Yuan, Ming, and Qing periods.

Among the column bases and steps there must be relics from the founding period; representative are the plain-surface inverted-basin stone column bases; while the timber structure part has mixed features of successive dynasties' methods, preserving rich historical information, and the ones with early traces are several simple ancient spindle columns (suozhu).

The traces of ancient stonework left in the courtyard are everywhere.

The stone paving on the ground is the most novel and interesting, reusing a large number of stone railings and cloud-bracket bixi tops — could they be Song Dynasty relics?

推荐级别：★★★

安贞堡

No.152
Anzhen Fort
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：永安市槐南乡洋头村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
民居格局结构工艺装饰做法池贯城清光绪十一年池占瑞建历时十四年占地约1万平方米
中文 Chinese

安贞堡位于永安市槐南乡洋头村，村头这样可爱的民居映入眼帘。要知道，"西华片"这里，现有老屋数百幢，安贞堡不过是其中最壮观的一幢。远远看去，安贞堡安卧于山脚下，面对一片开阔田地，显得气度雍容。堡的正面水塘中广植荷花，添得几分仙气。荷塘边有一告示牌，先说明这池荷花是清流引进的优良品种，栽种如何不容易，为了保持景观，请不要采摘。

如果实在喜欢得不行未经许可采摘了，每朵荷花或莲蓬需交"种植费"10元……说得有理有据，十分客气，又不失原则。即使你被罚了，大家依然不失体面。未进安贞堡，先领略到其后人的有理有节的古风，令我辈习惯了"严禁"、"罚款"、"后果自负"等上邦用语的人不禁疑惑：这里的人是中国人吗？

安贞堡又名"池贯城"，由当地乡绅池占瑞建于清朝光绪十一年（公元1885年），历时十四年完工。该堡占地面积约1万平方米，规模罕见。

规模虽大，但其"原理"却十分简单，主体建筑的内核就是一个四四方方的"四合院"，只两进院落，左右加厢房、加护厝，铺陈很开，外面就是城堡围墙，将核心建筑包裹起来。不过四合院内部是二层，而且雕梁画栋，做足了文章。最大的特色是建筑随地势逐次升高，屋顶层层叠叠，韵律十足，令人赞叹于古人的审美。跨进堡门感觉凉爽，透着一股温润之气。

早年的水井里面的水还是满满的，不知是否令人的用心；而花样百出的小木作、木...

English

Anzhen Fort is located in Yangtou Village, Huainan Township, Yong'an City; such lovely residences greet the eye at the village head.

You should know that in the "Xihua Pian" area here, there are now hundreds of old houses, and Anzhen Fort is merely the most spectacular one among them.

Seen from afar, Anzhen Fort rests peacefully at the foot of the mountain, facing a stretch of open fields, appearing dignified and graceful.

In the pond in front of the fort, lotus flowers are widely planted, adding a touch of celestial charm.

By the lotus pond there is a notice board, first explaining that these lotuses are a fine variety introduced from Qingliu, how difficult they are to plant, and asking people not to pick them to maintain the scenery.

If one really cannot help but pick without permission, each lotus flower or seedpod requires a "planting fee" of 10 yuan...It is reasoned and well-founded, very polite, yet without losing principle.

Even if you are fined, everyone still maintains dignity.

Before entering Anzhen Fort, one first experiences the reasonable and restrained ancient style of its descendants, making those of us accustomed to superior phrases like "strictly forbidden," "fine," and "at your own risk" wonder: are the people here Chinese?

Anzhen Fort, also known as "Chiguan City," was built by local gentry Chi Zhanrui in 1885 (the 11th year of Guangxu reign, Qing), taking fourteen years to complete.

The fort covers about 10,000 square meters, a rare scale.

Though large in scale, its "principle" is very simple: the core of the main building is a square "siheyuan" (courtyard house), with only two courtyards, side rooms on the left and right, plus protective wings (hucuo), spread out widely; outside is the castle wall, wrapping the core building.

However, the interior of the siheyuan is two stories, with carved beams and painted rafters, fully elaborated.

The greatest feature is that the building rises successively with the terrain, with roofs layered upon layered, full of rhythm, making one admire the aesthetics of the ancients.

Stepping through the fort gate feels cool, with a moist and gentle aura.The water in the early well is still full, unknown whether it is due to human care; and the varied small timber work, wood...

推荐级别：★★★★★

贡川城墙·会清桥

No.153
City Wall of Gongchuan and Huiqing Bridge
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：三明永安市贡川镇延爽村观成村
类型：古城·桥梁
特征标签 Highlights
古城遗迹桥梁结构明嘉靖四十一年建贡堡明代造城运动原长约2千米高7米东门攀龙门
中文 Chinese

沿着205国道从三明市去永安市，途中就是贡川城墙了。今人的道路应当是利用了古人的道里，而贡川城东南二面环水，西北二面负山，和会清桥相伴，一起度过了好几百年。

贡川城墙，古称"贡堡"，建于明嘉靖四十一年（1562年），当属明代"造城运动"的一部分。城墙原长约2千米，高7米左右，城楼无存，原有七个门，现存的有五个，而只有东门攀龙门尚堪使用。

城墙也破坏逾半，仅存900米，仅攀龙门至会清桥段尚可观。墙基的材料主要是随手可以取到的材料——鹅卵石、花岗石和丹霞石，上部用青砖包砌，城砖规格大而统一，定制烧造，可见许多砖上印有"贡堡"、"贡川"字样，一些还附有还烧制工匠的名字。城墙脚下设有"马道"，供城门关闭时过往路人行走。

不过现存状况令人担忧，砖砌体上杂草众生，破坏有加重的迹象，散落墙砖随意堆放，尽可取去自用，居民生活用品杂陈，路边道路也被辟为农贸市场，已经找不到当年藏书十万册的书院遗风了。或许是经常使用的缘故，城堡外会清桥风姿依旧。虽然如今已有新桥承担主要交通功能，但来往的行人依然愿意漫步老桥廊屋，躲避酷暑和风雨。

会清桥建于明代天启二年（1622年），横跨胡贡溪之上，连接贡川堡与巫峡头，前方即是沙溪，两溪一浑一清，汇合之处泾渭分明，胡贡溪"以浊会清"，因此得名。

桥长41米、宽7米，桥面高于水面8米余，用石材砌筑成拱券，两墩三孔，桥身建廊屋，自成清秀的姿态。

桥屋十一间，抬梁式结构；桥两端有门楼，中部是升起的桥亭，桥屋门楼的屋檐之下还可见到泥塑和彩绘，门楼四面坡屋顶，飞檐翘角，如翚斯飞；屋檐下有两翼伸展的风雨档板；桥中间神龛内供奉着玄武大帝。

English

Along National Highway 205 from Sanming to Yong'an, along the way is the Gongchuan City Wall.

Today's roads should have utilized the ancient roads; Gongchuan City is surrounded by water on the southeast two sides and backed by mountains on the northwest two sides, accompanied by Huiqing Bridge, having spent several hundred years together.

Gongchuan City Wall, anciently called "Gong Fort," was built in 1562 (the 41st year of Jiajing reign, Ming), and should be part of the Ming Dynasty "city-building movement.

" The wall was originally about 2 kilometers long and about 7 meters high; the gate towers no longer exist, of the original seven gates, five remain, and only the east gate Panlong Gate is still usable.

The wall is also over half destroyed, with only 900 meters remaining, and only the section from Panlong Gate to Huiqing Bridge is still worth seeing.

The wall base materials are mainly materials readily available — cobblestones, granite, and Danxia stone; the upper part is faced with blue bricks, with city bricks large and uniform in specification, custom-fired; many bricks can be seen printed with the characters "Gong Fort" and "Gongchuan," and some also bear the names of the firing craftsmen.

At the foot of the wall there is a "horse road" for passersby to walk when the city gates are closed.

However, the current condition is worrying: weeds grow on the brick masonry, with signs of worsening damage; scattered wall bricks are piled up arbitrarily, available for anyone to take for personal use; residents' daily necessities are scattered about; the roadside has also been turned into a farmers' market, and the legacy of the academy that once stored 100,000 books can no longer be found.

Perhaps because of frequent use, Huiqing Bridge outside the castle still retains its graceful appearance.

Although a new bridge now承担 the main traffic function, passing pedestrians still willingly stroll on the old bridge's covered hall to escape the heat and rain.

Huiqing Bridge was built in 1622 (the second year of Tianqi reign, Ming), spanning the Hugong Stream, connecting Gongchuan Fort and Wuxiatou; ahead is the Shaxi River, with the two streams one muddy and one clear, their confluence distinctly separate; Hugong Stream "meets the clear with the muddy," hence the name.

The bridge is 41 meters long and 7 meters wide, with the deck over 8 meters above the water; it is built of stone into arches, with two piers and three openings, and a covered hall on the bridge body, forming a graceful posture of its own.

The bridge hall has eleven bays with beam-lifting structure; there are gate towers at both ends of the bridge, and a raised bridge pavilion in the middle; under the eaves of the bridge hall gate towers, clay sculptures and painted decorations can still be seen; the gate towers have four-sided sloped roofs with flying eaves and upturned corners, "like a pheasant in flight"; under the eaves there are two-wing extending wind-and-rain boards; in the shrine in the middle of the bridge, the Great Emperor Xuanwu is enshrined.

推荐级别：★★★

会清堡·庭园

No.154
Huiqing Fort and Courtyard
级别：文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明永安市西洋镇福庄村
类型：民居·园林
特征标签 Highlights
民居格局书院园林咸丰三年邢作屏带领族人防御红巾之乱建成闽中数十座土堡中唯一现存庭园实例堡轮廓前方正后弯曲弓形三合土夯筑堡墙回廊一周射孔
中文 Chinese

土堡是邢作屏带领族人防御"红巾"之乱于咸丰三年（1853年）建成的。

土堡是防御性的，但是一旦有了喘息，还是要读书，要突破防御的藩篱，所以会清堡有自己的园子，而它也是闽中数十座土堡中唯一的现存实例了。会清堡方位并不对南北，主入口居于一侧，对东南方向。

堡的轮廓前半方正而后半弯曲呈弓形，堡墙三合土夯筑，其上回廊一周，对外开射孔；堡内院落三进，第二进的燕诒堂为核心的厅堂，前后天井，层层抬高。书院是在堡垒之外的，自己有自己的中轴线，与堡垒的轴线垂直。

书院主厅前有水池，跨池建桥，结合月台分割水面；池塘两翼更建水阁，阁周设廊，简明布局间空间已经动静有秩了，配合栏杆、隔扇，冰裂纹、水波纹、万字纹、海棠纹，方寸之间百态具备。

English

The earth fort was built by Xing Zuoping leading his clan to defend against the "Red Scarf" rebellion, completed in 1853 (the third year of Xianfeng reign).

The earth fort was defensive, but once there was a respite, one still had to study, to break through the barriers of defense, so Huiqing Fort has its own garden, and it is also the only surviving example among dozens of earth forts in central Fujian.

Huiqing Fort's orientation is not aligned north-south; the main entrance is on one side, facing southeast.

The fort's outline is square in the front half and curved in a bow shape in the rear half; the fort wall is rammed with sanhetu (three-part earth), with a surrounding corridor on top and arrow slits opening outward; inside the fort there are three courtyards, with the second courtyard's Yanyi Hall as the core hall, with front and rear skylights, raised layer by layer.

The academy is outside the fortress, with its own central axis, perpendicular to the fortress's axis.

In front of the academy's main hall there is a water pool, with a bridge spanning the pool, combined with a moon platform to divide the water surface; on both wings of the pond, water pavilions are further built, with corridors around the pavilions; in the concise layout, the space already has order between movement and stillness,配合 railings, lattice partitions, ice-crack patterns, water-wave patterns, wan-character patterns, and crabapple patterns — all forms are present within a small space.

推荐级别：★★★

会龙桥

No.155
Huilong Bridge
级别：无
年代：清—当代
地址：三明市清流县长校镇江坊村
类型：桥梁·木桥
特征标签 Highlights
木桥结构屋顶设计明末始建特大洪水毁20世纪60年代依原样重建桥长20米宽5米高4米穿斗式木架构
中文 Chinese

回想起在宁德地区寻访木拱廊桥的旅程，廊桥情结还是令人难以割舍。

除了廊桥的审美、工艺吸引人外，其中有个很务实的原因，就是肯修建廊桥并能保存至今的村落一定是个急公好义，人文荟萃之地，周边多半还有很多其他的人文景观，可以作为古建筑考察的一个线索，往往能有意外收获。这次要寻访的会龙桥距连城有百米之遥。很奇怪这一地区的景色总与脑海中的"南方"沾不上边，其天空的高远、阳光的炽烈总让人想起西藏。

会龙桥在田野中，旁边有会龙寺；田野中一片寂静，只有不断的鸟叫虫鸣；暗红色的桥身，黑色的屋顶，在绿色的映衬下，竟给人以寺庙的感觉。会龙桥始建于明末，后来毁于一场特大洪水，村民集资于20世纪60年代依照原样重建。

桥长20米，宽5米，高4米，桥屋穿斗式木架构，桥的一端依山坡，另一端垫有缓坡，当年古道的石阶隐约可见。桥架一墩两孔等跨，中间的桥墩依照老式做法成船形，减少洪水对桥身的冲击。

桥架为横木直排，不是木拱结构，此做法适用跨度较小，桥体长的话中间要有桥墩作为过渡支撑，无法横跨深沟大涧；优点是承重能力强，因此桥上部建筑多规模较大。廊屋内有神龛；廊屋的风雨板半开，既可遮风挡雨又注重采光，并有座椅供人休息。会龙桥的又一可爱处是这一连三个并排的歇山顶，造型优美、工艺精湛不说，边角装饰处竟施以琉璃构件，平添几分富贵气息。

联想此桥重建于"破四旧"的20世纪60年代，当地文化的执拗真是颇令人不解。兀自站立桥头，看那一派田园风光；偶有"仙人"从桥上过，原是去打农药。一笑过后，平淡处只是愿在桥里坐着，不忍离去。

English

Recalling the journey of searching for timber-arch covered bridges in the Ningde area, the covered-bridge complex is still hard to let go of.

Besides the aesthetic and craftsmanship appeal of covered bridges, there is a very practical reason: villages willing to build covered bridges and able to preserve them to this day must be places of public spirit and cultural richness, with many other cultural landscapes nearby, which can serve as a clue for ancient architecture investigation, often yielding unexpected gains.

The Huilong Bridge to be visited this time is about a hundred meters from Liancheng.

Strangely, the scenery of this region never seems to match the "South" in one's mind; its lofty sky and blazing sunlight always remind one of Tibet.

Huilong Bridge is in the fields, with Huilong Temple beside it; the fields are silent, with only constant bird calls and insect chirps; the dark red bridge body and black roof, against the green backdrop, actually give the feeling of a temple.

Huilong Bridge was first built in the late Ming, later destroyed by an extraordinary flood; villagers raised funds to rebuild it according to the original style in the 1960s.

The bridge is 20 meters long, 5 meters wide, and 4 meters high, with a column-and-tie timber frame for the bridge hall; one end of the bridge leans against a hillside, and the other end is padded with a gentle slope, with the stone steps of the ancient road faintly visible.

The bridge frame has one pier and two equal-span openings; the middle pier is made boat-shaped according to the old method, reducing the impact of floods on the bridge body.

The bridge frame is of horizontal timber arranged in straight rows, not a timber-arch structure; this method is suitable for smaller spans — if the bridge body is long, a pier is needed in the middle as transitional support, unable to span deep gullies and ravines; its advantage is strong load-bearing capacity, so the upper buildings of the bridge are often larger in scale.

There is a shrine inside the covered hall; the wind-and-rain boards of the covered hall are half-open, both shielding from wind and rain and emphasizing lighting, with seats for people to rest.

Another lovely feature of Huilong Bridge is this row of three side-by-side hip-and-gable roofs; not to mention their beautiful shape and exquisite craftsmanship, the corner decorations are actually applied with glazed components, adding a touch of wealth and nobility.

Recalling that this bridge was rebuilt in the 1960s, the era of "destroying the four olds," the stubbornness of local culture is truly puzzling.

Standing alone at the bridgehead, watching that idyllic scenery; occasionally an "immortal" passes over the bridge, turns out to be going to spray pesticide.

After a smile, in the ordinary place, one just wishes to sit inside the bridge, unable to bear to leave.

推荐级别：★★★

赖坊民居建筑群

No.156
Vernacular Dwellings in Laifang
级别：中国历史文化名村
年代：清
地址：三明清流县赖坊乡赖武、赖安村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
民居格局结构工艺装饰做法唐乾符元年赖姓徙居汀州古田南宋咸淳二年一郎公九郎公卜居水东三十余代
中文 Chinese

《清流县志》记载，清流赖姓来自颍川，徙居汀州古路上杭县古田的时间是唐乾符元年（874年），孙辈始迁居清流赖安、赖武。

《赖氏族谱》又说，赖坊赖氏肇基者为一郎公和其弟九郎公，于南宋咸淳二年（1266年）寻猪而至，卜居水东，播衍耕殖，世代相传至今已有三十余代。而这里密布的民居则均建于清中期以后，至今未进行过大规模的维修，基本保持原貌。

最有代表性的，要数彩映庚宅、翰林第、棠棣竞秀宅、来青宅、攸叙宅、迎薰宅等六座。头一座彩映庚，在赖武村西南部，是赖其章在清光绪十八年（1892年）建造的。东边依山，宅院面西，轴线转折，从砖雕门楼进入院坪，左转向北才面对上下两厅，南侧还有一列横屋。大门前的双狮、门上砖雕古朴精美；院内埕上卵石铺墁颇具匠心；正堂屋架素雅中亦不失精工雕刻。

再一座翰林第，位于赖武村中部偏东，建于清咸丰年间。同样面西而设，两进合院带左右护厝，格局对称规整。门内出了翰林，所以大门才敢写"翰林第"门额；屋内板墙上，至今保留有较多的科举捷报，与今天使用的农具相映成趣...

English

The "Qingliu County Annals" record that the Lai surname in Qingliu came from Yingchuan, and the time they moved to Gutian in Shanghang County on the ancient Tingzhou road was 874 (the first year of Qianfu reign, Tang); their grandchildren began to move to Lai'an and Laiwu in Qingliu.

The "Lai Clan Genealogy" also says that the founders of the Lai clan in Laifang were Lord Yilang and his younger brother Lord Jiulang, who came following pigs in 1266 (the second year of Xianchun reign, Southern Song), chose to live by the water east, multiplied and farmed, and have been passed down for over thirty generations to this day.

The densely distributed dwellings here were all built after the mid-Qing, and have not undergone large-scale repairs to this day, basically maintaining their original appearance.

The most representative are six residences: Caiyinggeng Residence, Hanlin Di (Hanlin Mansion), Tangdi Jingxiu Residence, Laiqing Residence, Youxu Residence, and Yingxun Residence.

The first one, Caiyinggeng, is in the southwestern part of Laiwu Village, built by Lai Qizhang in 1892 (the 18th year of Guangxu reign, Qing).

With the east side against the mountain, the residence faces west, with a turning axis; entering the courtyard through the brick-carved gate tower, turning left northward one faces the upper and lower halls, and there is a row of horizontal rooms on the south side.

The double lions in front of the main gate and the brick carvings on the gate are simple and exquisite; the cobblestone paving in the courtyard is quite ingenious; the main hall's roof frame, though plain, does not lack exquisite carving.

Another one, Hanlin Di, is located slightly east of the center of Laiwu Village, built during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing.

Also facing west, it is a two-courtyard compound with left and right protective wings (hucuo), with a symmetrical and regular layout.

Since a Hanlin (academician) came out of the gate, the main gate dared to bear the "Hanlin Di" inscription; on the wooden walls inside the house, many imperial examination success notices are still preserved today, forming an interesting contrast with the farm tools used today.

..

推荐级别：★★★

豫章书院

No.157
Yuzhang Academy
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明市宁化县小溪边131号
类型：礼制建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
书院与宗族的关系晚期木结构北有大槐树南有石壁村宁化石壁客家移民中转站江西豫章罗氏汉惠帝罗珠守九江郡手植豫章树南宋创建传播朱程之学
中文 Chinese

听说过"北有大槐树，南有石壁村"吧？那是福建宁化的石壁。宁化位于江西入闽处平坦狭长的通道上，武夷山脉是它的屏障，且河流汇凑交通便利，是唐代黄巢之乱以后客家移民的中转站，造就了石壁的声名。今天的石壁镇和豫章书院在泉南高速上是挨着的两个出口，在客家罗氏移民的历史上则关系更要紧密。

豫章书院源于江西豫章罗氏，汉惠帝时大农令罗珠守九江郡，筑新城时手植豫章树，遂豫章之名，罗氏此后以豫章为堂号。

豫章书院创建于南宋时期，是传播朱程之学的基地；明万历年间因禁而辍；清初恢复，清中叶鼎盛，且发扬拓展，形成江西、黔东、广东、福建为主体的全国性书院体系。

福建的豫章书院起源于清中期。清雍正十三年（1725年）罗家罗登标中举，历任周宁、政和及江西等地训导、教谕，乾隆三十年致仕还乡，在祖祠内招收弟子开馆讲学，挂牌"豫章书院"。

而这个罗氏宗祠，是石壁客家罗氏唯一之总祠，也是世界客家唯一之总祠。

书院用地——小河边131号的罗氏宗祠始建于明永乐壬辰（公元1412年），比紫禁城还要古老；先后经过七次整修，自清同治三年大加修固后，最近的一次全面修饰是在1986年。

此后，宁化豫章书院兼作为开县始祖令纪公之纪念祠堂。书院坐北朝南，面积紧凑，仅一院。

临街有前埕和围墙，门口八字排开，重檐歇山屋顶高耸，琉璃瓦面，檐下如意斗拱密布，四角轻盈翘起；山门之内是一个长方形天井，两侧是厢房廊接；面前正殿三间，硬山式屋顶，简洁明亮，气氛肃穆。

额悬"敦睦堂"匾，正中设龛，自汉代罗珠公起，至25世罗令纪公神位依序列座，各支族系祖宗神位按顺序排列其下，左昭右穆，北高南低。

English

Have you heard of "In the north there is the Great Scholar Tree, in the south there is Shibi Village"?That is Shibi in Ninghua, Fujian.

Ninghua is located on a flat and narrow passage from Jiangxi into Fujian, with the Wuyi Mountains as its barrier, and where rivers converge with convenient transportation; it was a transit station for Hakka immigrants after the Huang Chao Rebellion in the Tang, creating the fame of Shibi.

Today's Shibi Town and Yuzhang Academy are two adjacent exits on the Quannan Expressway, and in the history of Hakka Luo clan immigration their relationship is even closer.

Yuzhang Academy originated from the Yuzhang Luo clan of Jiangxi; during the reign of Emperor Hui of Han, the Grand Minister of Agriculture Luo Zhu guarded Jiujiang Commandery, and when building the new city he personally planted a yuzhang (camphor) tree, hence the name Yuzhang, and the Luo clan thereafter used Yuzhang as their hall name.

Yuzhang Academy was founded during the Southern Song period as a base for spreading Zhu-Cheng Neo-Confucianism; it was discontinued due to prohibition during the Wanli reign of the Ming; restored in the early Qing, it reached its peak in the mid-Qing, and was further developed and expanded, forming a nationwide academy system with Jiangxi, eastern Guizhou, Guangdong, and Fujian as the main bodies.

Fujian's Yuzhang Academy originated in the mid-Qing.

In 1725 (the 13th year of Yongzheng reign, Qing), Luo Dengbiao of the Luo family passed the provincial examination, serving successively as instructor and education official in Zhouning, Zhenghe, and Jiangxi; in 1765 (the 30th year of Qianlong reign) he retired and returned home, recruiting disciples and opening a school in the ancestral hall, hanging the sign "Yuzhang Academy.

" And this Luo Clan Ancestral Hall is the only general ancestral hall of the Shibi Hakka Luo clan, and also the only general ancestral hall of world Hakkas.

The academy's site — the Luo Clan Ancestral Hall at No.

131 Xiaoxibian — was first built in 1412 (the Renchen year of Yongle reign, Ming), even older than the Forbidden City; it has undergone seven repairs successively, and after major reinforcement in the third year of Tongzhi reign of Qing, the most recent comprehensive renovation was in 1986.

Thereafter, Ninghua Yuzhang Academy also served as the memorial ancestral hall of the county's founding ancestor Lord Lingji.

The academy faces south from the north, with a compact area of only one courtyard.

Facing the street there is a front courtyard and wall, with the gate spread in a八字 shape; the double-eave hip-and-gable roof soars high, with glazed tile surface, densely packed ruyi bracket sets under the eaves, and four corners lightly upturned; inside the mountain gate is a rectangular skylight, with side rooms and corridors on both sides; facing it is the main hall of three bays, with a gable roof, simple and bright, with a solemn atmosphere.

The plaque "Dunmu Tang" (Hall of Honoring Harmony) hangs above; in the center is a shrine, with the spirit tablets from Han Dynasty Lord Luo Zhu to the 25th generation Lord Luo Lingji arranged in sequence, with the ancestral spirit tablets of each branch clan arranged below in order, left zhao and right mu, north high and south low.

推荐级别：★★

七叶衍祥坊

No.158
Qiye Yanxiang Archway
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：三明建宁县溪源乡上坪村
类型：礼制建筑·石结构
特征标签 Highlights
结构支撑关系装饰与结构的关系家门雍睦七叶共居七代同堂乾隆下旨上见祖父下见曾孙玄孙者具结呈报奖赏五世同堂已值得称道立牌坊旌表或追溯秦始皇
中文 Chinese

所谓"家门雍睦，七叶共居"，七代同堂，那简直太难得了。所以乾隆下旨各地如有上见祖、父、下见曾孙、玄孙者，可具结呈报，经核实后给予奖赏，不仅家庭完聚、乐享天伦，对于社会的稳定也是莫大的贡献。五世同堂已经非常值得称道的了。立牌坊旌表，或可追溯到秦始皇；能够完整保留下来的"七叶衍祥坊"则是屈指可数的。

建宁的七叶衍祥坊是一座典型的四柱三间五楼式石牌坊，四柱前后二侧有抱鼓形夹柱石，造型简洁大方，并不像漳州石牌坊那样，为了追求深远出挑的檐口而增加过多的立柱。牌坊坐北朝南，总宽6.98米，总高8.76米。左右五楼分上下三层，并不完全呼应四根立柱的位置。

顶楼内收立在最上边的通额之上，又分成三小间，当心左右为龙凤柱，柱间立"圣旨"碑；侧楼一外一内分别与立柱交界。明间额枋之间嵌置"七叶衍祥"匾；字碑及匾额的二侧，又各有一块字碑，记述有关事迹以及建坊经过等。

English

The so-called "family harmony, seven generations living together" — seven generations under one roof — is simply extraordinarily rare.

Therefore, the Qianlong Emperor decreed that if anywhere there were those who could see grandparents and parents above, and great-grandchildren and great-great-grandchildren below, they could submit a report, and after verification be given rewards; not only would the family be united and enjoy family happiness, but it would also be a great contribution to social stability.

Five generations under one roof is already very praiseworthy.

Erecting archways to commend virtue may be traced back to Qin Shi Huang; the "Qiye Yanxiang Archways" (Seven Generations Prosperity Archways) that have been completely preserved are few and far between.

Jianning's Qiye Yanxiang Archway is a typical four-column, three-bay, five-story stone archway, with drum-shaped column-holding stones on the front and rear sides of the four columns, with a simple and generous shape, unlike Zhangzhou stone archways which add too many columns in pursuit of deeply projecting eaves.

The archway faces south from the north, with a total width of 6.98 meters and total height of 8.76 meters.

The left and right five stories are divided into upper and lower three layers, not completely corresponding to the positions of the four columns.

The top story is set back and stands on the uppermost crossbeam, further divided into three small bays; in the center, left and right are dragon-phoenix columns, with an "Imperial Decree" stele between the columns; the side stories, one outer and one inner, respectively meet the columns.

Between the main bay's lintels, a "Qiye Yanxiang" plaque is embedded; on both sides of the character stele and plaque, there is another character stele each, recording related deeds and the process of building the archway.

推荐级别：★★★

甘露岩寺

No.159
Ganlu Rock Temple
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：南宋—清
地址：泰宁大金湖景区西岸
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
寺院格局早期建筑痕迹晚期木结构宋绍兴十六年1146年建850多年岩穴高80多米深30米上宽30多米下宽10多米倒三角形一柱插地不假片瓦
中文 Chinese

山水之乐无疑是考察古建筑的绝佳馈赠。要去甘露岩寺，就要先游览大金湖的丹霞地貌。弃舟登岸，跨过石桥，遇见石经幢，就到了南方悬空寺——甘露岩寺。甘露岩寺老屋始建于宋绍兴十六年（1146年），距今已有850多年。寺院依托的岩穴高80多米，深30米，上宽约有30多米，下宽10多米，呈倒三角形。

营造者把这地理上的劣势变为建筑上的优势，一柱插地，不假片瓦，用一根巨柱撑起了四幢重楼叠阁——上殿、蜃楼阁、观音阁、南安阁四部分组成，斗拱层叠，巧夺天工。一柱擎天固然难得，利用岩石横向架设平台也需要高超的技艺，不过闽中擅长此技者当不在少数，想想木拱廊桥。

人们说这个大柱已经通神，抱一下会梦想成真。建筑总体新近装修过，木结构是否也大动了手脚不得而知。想起傅熹年、王贵祥等先生的研究，当年的甘露庵在专家们开始深入研究之前就毁掉了。

尽管如此，透过1959年《文物》上刊登的素材，学者们还是可以清晰地看出日本"大佛样"和福建地区华林寺、元妙观三清殿和甘露庵之间的继承关系。12世纪时日本名僧重源法师三度入闽考察，当时他在大金湖的心境会是什么样的呢？

环顾周边，人类的杰作之外，大自然的杰作似乎更令人赞叹——山崖之上，草木渲染，似乎将本地山间的无数民居一股脑地呈现出来了。照相之时，身边走过一群游客。突然其中一位用文化人的京腔，像是对我说又像是自言自语道："福建人就是聪明，瞧这木结构做得多好。

"在此听到乡音异常亲切，我也就搭腔："是呀，哪怕是新活儿也这么好……"那位老兄回头看了我一眼："毕竟他那个文化积淀在那儿呢……"说罢转身随团而去。因为有这方山水，当然还有文化积淀。

English

The joy of mountains and waters is undoubtedly an excellent gift for investigating ancient architecture.To go to Ganlu Rock Temple, one must first tour the Danxia landform of Dajin Lake.

Abandoning the boat and going ashore, crossing a stone bridge, encountering a stone pillar (jingchuang), one arrives at the southern hanging temple — Ganlu Rock Temple.

The old building of Ganlu Rock Temple was first built in 1146 (the 16th year of Shaoxing reign, Southern Song), over 850 years ago.

The rock cave the temple relies on is over 80 meters high, 30 meters deep, about 30 meters wide at the top and over 10 meters wide at the bottom, in an inverted triangle shape.

The builders turned this geographical disadvantage into an architectural advantage: one column inserted into the ground, without a single tile, using one giant column to support four multi-story pavilions — composed of the Upper Hall, Shenlou Pavilion, Guanyin Pavilion, and Nan'an Pavilion, with layered bracket sets, a marvel of craftsmanship.

A single column supporting the sky is certainly rare, and using rock to horizontally erect platforms also requires superb skill; however, there are quite a few people in central Fujian skilled at this — think of timber-arch covered bridges.

People say this giant column has become divine, and hugging it will make dreams come true.

The building has been newly renovated overall, and whether the timber structure was also greatly altered is unknown.Recalling the research of Mr.Fu Xinian, Mr.

Wang Guixiang, and others, the original Ganlu Nunnery was destroyed before experts began in-depth research.

Nevertheless, through the materials published in "Wenwu" (Cultural Relics) in 1959, scholars can still clearly see the inheritance relationship between the Japanese "Daibutsuyo" (Great Buddha style) and the Fujian region's Hualin Temple, Yuanmiao Temple Sanqing Hall, and Ganlu Nunnery.

In the 12th century, the famous Japanese monk Chogen made three trips to Fujian for investigation; what would his state of mind have been at Dajin Lake then?

Looking around, beyond human masterpieces, nature's masterpieces seem even more admirable — on the cliffs, vegetation is rendered, as if presenting countless local mountain dwellings all at once.

While taking photos, a group of tourists passed by.

Suddenly one of them, in a cultured Beijing accent, as if speaking to me or to himself, said: "Fujianese are just smart, look how well this timber structure is made.

" Hearing a hometown accent here was exceptionally warm, so I chimed in: "Yes, even the new work is this good..." That fellow glanced back at me: "After all, his cultural accumulation is there...

" Then he turned and left with the group.Because of this landscape, and of course the cultural accumulation.

推荐级别：★★★★

古城

No.160
Taining Ancient City
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：三明市泰宁古城
类型：古城
特征标签 Highlights
古城码头遗迹石作做法明嘉靖三十八年知县熊鹗筹银筑城历时七月八座城门外接官道上建城楼墙头可行人走马总长度2363米
中文 Chinese

泰宁是个古城，有着十分悠久的历史，至今散发迷人魅力，加之天雨留客，一住十天之久。就要离去之际，偶得机缘从另外一个角度领略一下泰宁的韵味。碑刻记载，明嘉靖三十八年（1559年），知县熊鹗筹银筑城，历时七月。城开大小城门八座，外接官道，上建城楼，墙头可行人走马，总长度达2363米。

泰宁临水，城边有一条河，以前这条河对泰宁来说无疑更重要，往来的商业一定很繁忙，现在还保存有古码头。栓船石柱的磨损状况令人想到当初船只上下往来的盛况。城门做得如此之小，似乎比大户人家的院门还要局促，初令人不解。仔细想大概有两重功能，平时收税，战时防卫。从原来的城里一侧看古城墙则台阶垛口一应俱全。正对城墙的是一组宏伟的牌楼，对影成三人，原来这才是泰宁古城的城门遗址。

据说这样的大城门原来有四座，目前仅剩下这不完整的一座了。巨大的石料，精心的雕刻，又让人联想起附近的顺昌县的宝峰寺；牌楼上面不遗余力的精雕细刻，一定是在歌颂什么，同时也在炫耀什么。现在这一广场白天略显荒芜，晚上是人们的娱乐场所，很多人在这里跳交谊舞。离开城门不远，用鲁迅的话说，"蹩进这样的小巷"。小巷中对外开放的人家，雕刻玲珑的古老水槽特别抢眼，今天依旧使用的旧物到...

English

Taining is an ancient city with a very long history, still exuding charming appeal to this day; coupled with rain keeping guests, one stayed for ten days.

As one was about to leave, one happened to get a chance to appreciate Taining's charm from another angle.

Stone inscriptions record that in 1559 (the 38th year of Jiajing reign, Ming), County Magistrate Xiong E raised silver to build the city, taking seven months.

The city had eight city gates of various sizes, connecting to official roads outside, with gate towers built above, and the wall tops could be walked on by people and horses, with a total length of 2363 meters.

Taining is by water, with a river by the city; in the past this river was undoubtedly more important to Taining, and the commerce coming and going must have been very busy; ancient docks are still preserved today.

The wear on the ship-tying stone columns makes one think of the grand scene of ships coming and going in those days.

The city gates are made so small, seeming even more cramped than the gate of a wealthy family, which is puzzling at first.

Thinking carefully, they probably had two functions: collecting taxes in peacetime and defense in wartime.

Looking at the ancient city wall from the original inside-city side, steps and crenellations are all present.

Directly facing the wall is a group of grand archways, forming a trio with their shadows; it turns out this is the actual gate site of Taining Ancient City.

It is said there were originally four such large gates, and currently only this incomplete one remains.

The giant stone materials and careful carvings remind one of the nearby Baofeng Temple in Shunchang County; the painstaking fine carvings on the archways must be praising something, and at the same time showing off something.

This square now appears somewhat desolate during the day, but at night it is a place of entertainment for people, with many dancing ballroom dance here.

Not far from the city gate, in Lu Xun's words, "sneaking into such an alley.

" In the alley, among the households open to the public, the exquisitely carved ancient water trough is particularly eye-catching, and the old objects still in use today...

推荐级别：★★★

李家岩寺

No.161
Lijia Rock Temple
级别：无
年代：当代
地址：泰宁县李家岩景区
类型：宗教·自然风光
特征标签 Highlights
风光原名天台岩禅寺泰宁县城到寨下大峡谷途中巨大岩石矗立于山谷之中横向石缝明代兵部尚书李春烨曾在此读书成名唐代始建修葺一新
中文 Chinese

李家岩寺原名天台岩禅寺，坐落于泰宁县城到寨下大峡谷的途中。一座巨大的岩石矗立于山谷之中，横向有一石缝，李家岩寺便建于石缝中，从山下隐约可见。若论禅寺以山得名，则叫作天台岩寺是再恰当不过，因为眼前这块巨石确实形如天台一般。后因尚书第的主人明代的兵部尚书李春烨曾在此读书而成名，寺庙遂被当地人称为李家岩寺，久而成例，当初的天台岩寺反而没人这么叫了。

李家岩寺据说最早建于唐代，不过现在的寺庙看去修葺一新，已经难觅古寺的蛛丝马迹，不变的是当年的那番光景。禅寺位于石缝中，有不少出家人在此修行。禅寺内香烟缭绕，有僧人打坐，有很多佛学的书籍发放，一派祥和的佛家气氛。

从山下沿一条古旧的石阶往上500米，有一条悬挂于绝壁之上的岩槽走廊，岩槽开口朝外，外围筑上了铁、木两层栏杆，以方便行走；其尽头就是天台岩寺。进入岩寺之前，先穿过一条半米宽的石凿小道，面前石门书写一楹联"具怀逸兴壮思飞，可上九天揽明月"，横批"吞吐天地"。此为"雪洞"，即昔日李春烨读书的石屋，现为小佛堂。

与雪洞相连的建筑就是天台岩寺，中为佛殿，左为辅房，右为禅房，简朴无华，与幽僻的岩穴气韵相通。是不是只有人的作品才叫作建筑？这要看你是不是有对环境的敏锐感知。梁思成先生所谓的"体形环境"，就是审度、鉴赏和批判你所在的大环境到你触摸的小装饰。李家岩的环境，用千年的风雨当刻刀，雕琢之后再等待绿色的浸染，你或者触摸得到，但你的心胸装得下吗？

English

Lijia Rock Temple was originally named Tiantai Rock Chan Temple, located on the way from Taining County town to the Zaixia Grand Canyon.

A giant rock stands in the valley, with a horizontal rock fissure; Lijia Rock Temple was built in the rock fissure, faintly visible from below the mountain.

If discussing the Chan temple being named after the mountain, calling it Tiantai Rock Temple could not be more appropriate, because the giant rock before one's eyes indeed resembles a heavenly platform.

Later, because the master of the Mansion of the Minister, Ming Dynasty Minister of War Li Chunye, once studied here and became famous, the temple was called Lijia Rock Temple by locals; over time this became the convention, and the original Tiantai Rock Temple name is no longer used.

Lijia Rock Temple is said to have been first built in the Tang Dynasty, but the current temple looks newly renovated, and it is already difficult to find any traces of the ancient temple; what remains unchanged is the scene of those days.

The Chan temple is located in the rock fissure, with many monastics practicing here.

Inside the Chan temple, incense smoke curls, monks meditate, and many Buddhist books are distributed — a peaceful Buddhist atmosphere.

From below the mountain, along an ancient stone step path up 500 meters, there is a rock-slot corridor hanging on the precipice; the rock slot opens outward, with two layers of iron and wood railings built on the outside for convenient walking; at its end is Tiantai Rock Temple.

Before entering the rock temple, one first passes through a half-meter-wide stone-chiseled path; in front, the stone gate bears a couplet: "With lofty aspirations and bold thoughts soaring, one can reach the ninth heaven to grasp the bright moon," with the horizontal inscription "Swallowing and Spitting Heaven and Earth.

" This is the "Snow Cave," the stone house where Li Chunye once studied, now a small Buddhist hall.

The building connected to the Snow Cave is Tiantai Rock Temple, with the Buddha hall in the center, auxiliary rooms on the left, and meditation rooms on the right — simple and unadorned, in harmony with the secluded rock cave's aura.

Is it only human works that are called architecture?It depends on whether you have a keen perception of the environment.What Mr.

Liang Sicheng called the "physical environment" is to assess, appreciate, and critique from the large environment you are in to the small decorations you touch.

The environment of Lijia Rock, using a thousand years of wind and rain as a carving knife, after carving then waiting for the green to permeate — you may be able to touch it, but can your heart contain it?

推荐级别：★★

尚书第

No.162
Mansion of Minister
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：明
地址：三明泰宁市中心杉城镇尚书街
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
民居格局结构工艺装饰做法明天启年间兵部尚书李春烨大器晚成46岁中进士十年二品大员隐退泰宁古城以尚书第建筑群为中心
中文 Chinese

在闽西北的山区小城泰宁有一座尚书第，其规模宏大，工艺考究，保存完好，成了这座小城的标志性建筑。历史上这位尚书并不是家喻户晓，他是明朝天启年间的兵部尚书李春烨。据说他大器晚成，46岁才中进士，但十年之间做到二品大员便隐退了，因此人们对他的宦海沉浮和财富积累有很多猜测。

泰宁古城以尚书第建筑群为中心，李氏宗祠地位最崇，周边古街两旁商铺林立，老房子也有不少，古镇当初的氛围依旧。从尚书第大门开始就是一派官气，其规模和气派与我们参观过的当地民居殊为不同。举步而入，这里给人的感觉与其说是一处府第，不如说是半条胡同，而且是全部由青砖和花岗岩打造的极其奢华的胡同。

庭院布置得非常素雅，与现代人有关的是，这里未见大红灯笼、大红对联和大红条幅。上述诸多大红曾困扰余一路，终于忍不住在武夷山的下梅大夫第向导游女孩提起，建议将灯笼等改成其他。黄色是皇家专用的颜色，或云可以改成白色，导游小姐面露惊慌，连连摆手说不可以不可以……服从于大家的说法便了。

闽地由于盛产木材，所以很多大宅都是高大敞亮，设计上有南方建筑的审美情趣，而感觉上又不像江南建筑那般小巧玲珑；院中的地面都是花岗岩，屋内地面则施以青砖；门窗上大量的木雕，其雕工以气派见长，而不是一味追求繁复的花样，与民间富家大户的风格是有差别的；门楣上的砖雕和仿木构建，怎么大家都要和宝峰寺一试高下？

总之，整个尚书第的各个部分给人的感觉是用料巨大、做工精美。可能泰宁本身的地理人文环境成就并保存了尚书第，在当初的建造过程中不但提供了物质的可能，在日后的岁月变迁中又因其地处偏僻人口稀少，远离政治旋涡而得以完整保存。午后的阳光在院中留下长长的阴影和宁静的气氛，人的功过是非喜怒哀乐随着时光逝去。就像人们评价尚书本人的功过，终无定论，最后说"无论怎样，他为当地人民留下了这座宏伟的尚书第"。

"无论怎样"几个字非常之好，不知这几个字作为我们的是非标准和行为准则有多久了。

English

In the mountainous small city of Taining in northwestern Fujian, there is a Mansion of the Minister (Shangshu Di), with grand scale, exquisite craftsmanship, and well-preserved condition, becoming the landmark building of this small city.

Historically, this minister was not a household name; he was Li Chunye, Minister of War during the Tianqi reign of the Ming Dynasty.

It is said that he was a late bloomer, only passing the jinshi examination at age 46, but within ten years reached the rank of second-rank official and then retired; therefore people have many speculations about his ups and downs in officialdom and wealth accumulation.

Taining Ancient City centers on the Shangshu Di building complex, with the Li Clan Ancestral Hall holding the highest status; surrounding ancient streets are lined with shops on both sides, and there are quite a few old houses, with the original atmosphere of the ancient town still intact.

From the gate of Shangshu Di onward, there is an air of officialdom; its scale and imposing manner are quite different from the local residences we have visited.

Stepping inside, the feeling here is less like a mansion than half a hutong — and an extremely luxurious hutong made entirely of blue bricks and granite.

The courtyards are arranged very elegantly; related to modern people, there are no big red lanterns, big red couplets, or big red banners here.

The aforementioned many red things had troubled me all the way, and I finally could not help mentioning it to the tour guide girl at Xiamei Dafu Di in Wuyi Mountain, suggesting changing the lanterns to something else.

Yellow is a color exclusively for the imperial family, or some say it could be changed to white; the tour guide girl looked alarmed, repeatedly waving her hands saying no, no...

Just go along with what everyone says.

Because Fujian is rich in timber, many large mansions are tall and bright, with the aesthetic taste of southern architecture in design, yet not feeling as delicate and small as Jiangnan architecture; the courtyard floors are all granite, while indoor floors are paved with blue bricks; the large amount of wood carving on doors and windows is characterized by imposing style rather than blindly pursuing intricate patterns, differing from the style of wealthy folk families; the brick carvings and imitation-timber structures on the lintels — why does everyone want to compete with Baofeng Temple?

In short, every part of the entire Shangshu Di gives the impression of massive materials and exquisite workmanship.

Perhaps Taining's own geographical and cultural environment created and preserved Shangshu Di; in the original construction process it not only provided material possibilities, but in the subsequent changes of years, because of its remote location and sparse population, far from political turmoil, it was completely preserved.

The afternoon sunlight leaves long shadows and a tranquil atmosphere in the courtyard; people's merits and demerits, right and wrong, joys and sorrows pass with time.

Just as people evaluate the merits and demerits of the Minister himself, ultimately without a definitive conclusion, finally saying "no matter what, he left this magnificent Shangshu Di for the local people.

" The words "no matter what" are very good; I wonder how long these words have served as our standard of right and wrong and code of conduct.

推荐级别：★★★★

良地建筑群

No.163
Building Complex in Liangdi
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明将乐县万全乡良地村
类型：礼制·宗教·公共建筑
特征标签 Highlights
乡土建筑群概念的理由结构工艺装饰做法闽西北客家建村始祖不凡借山地错落砌筑台地吊脚立柱房屋外观朴实简洁内部雕栏画栋
中文 Chinese

世外桃源的人也会追随欲望的脚步，良地村也不能免俗，村子里的年轻人外出打工，老人成了村中一切事物的主力。年轻人要回乡的吧？一路上沿溪上溯，渐高渐窄的道路夹在古木翠竹之间，溪水淙淙，而豁然开朗的平畴，就是老家了。到底为什么走呢？闽西北客家建村始祖是不凡的。

因借了山地的错落，或砌筑台地，或吊脚立柱；也按捺住了炫耀的念头，房屋外观朴实简洁，而内部雕栏画栋，没有给环境添一丝不协。这里的建筑不只是住宅，而是一套典型的"乡土建筑群"。值得大书一下的包括文武庙、梁氏宗祠、绪延厝、月山公屋、冠群谷仓、水尾木廊桥六处。

文武庙在村子南口，清乾隆二十六年（1761年）建，原来只是文昌阁，后来又增祀关公，文武双全了。庙的主体只一进小院，朝向顺着进村道路，进入则须拐进前坪兜个圈子。

中轴线上的房子都极富特色：门楼是牌楼式的，如意斗拱精美繁复，屋顶高挑；拜亭几乎占满了院子，结构简明，朴素大方；主殿两层，孔子居主位在上而关老爷在楼下，是村子的标志。梁氏宗祠是当地居民生活的核心，又名裕启堂，在文武庙之北。

祠堂入口朝东，对着主路，在左右更各建门楼，庄严地宣示着自己的领地，也占有了主路的一段。祠堂主座一进，院落中再无堵塞，以便族人在此公议、祭祀。祠堂前山南墙嵌置有清嘉庆十四年（1809）合乡公立之"禁约碑"，前坪有弧形吊脚楼倒座、仓房等设施。绪延厝是一座典型的住宅，位于村西北面坡地上。

宅子朝向东南，开门在左前方，左侧有花厅水池，右侧是两列横屋；左侧是石砌墙脚，右侧则前廊外挑，成吊脚楼，柱子立于低处山崖上，是因地制宜的典型。月山公屋，是乾嘉时期名人月山公梁迄的房子，在村头出口处，朝向东南。原来此屋占地广大，解放初期左侧两列横屋已被改建，现存建筑由右前侧门道、一进院的主座、右后侧书房、左后侧藏书阁等组成。良地村拥有大量谷仓，村东北侧溪流西岸的冠群谷仓便是代表。

冠群谷仓是一组八座单层仓房，前有院坪，内部储藏空间架空。良地村南头入村处，先能看到水尾木廊桥。这是一座单孔的伸臂梁木桥，上建廊屋。

桥面阔11间，宽22.4米，进深用4柱抬梁，深3.84米，桥面距水面高约5米，桥屋高4.27米。

桥体古朴，桥屋体型变化丰富，屋顶错落；桥内设六个神位；桥侧与集灵宫相连；桥头与古驿道相接。顾名思义，水尾桥在风水上是村子关锁水尾的建筑。

English

People in a paradise on earth will also follow the footsteps of desire; Liangdi Village is no exception.

The young people in the village go out to work, and the elderly become the main force for everything in the village.The young people should return home, right?

Along the way upstream along the stream, the gradually higher and narrower road is sandwiched between ancient trees and green bamboo, with the stream gurgling, and the suddenly open flat fields are home.

Why leave after all?The founders of Hakka villages in northwestern Fujian were extraordinary.

By taking advantage of the mountain terrain's irregularity, they either built terraces or used stilt columns; they also restrained the urge to show off, with simple and unadorned house exteriors while the interiors had carved railings and painted beams, adding not a trace of disharmony to the environment.

The buildings here are not just residences, but a typical set of "vernacular building complex.

" Worth writing about in detail are six places: the Wenwu Temple (Civil-Military Temple), Liang Clan Ancestral Hall, Xuyan Residence, Yueshan Public House, Guanqun Granary, and Shuiwei Timber Covered Bridge.

The Wenwu Temple is at the south entrance of the village, built in 1761 (the 26th year of Qianlong reign, Qing); originally it was only a Wenchang Pavilion, later adding the worship of Guan Gong, thus having both civil and military virtues.

The main body of the temple is only one small courtyard, oriented along the road into the village; entering requires turning into the front courtyard and making a circle.

The houses on the central axis are all highly distinctive: the gate tower is paifang-style, with exquisite and intricate ruyi bracket sets and a high-pitched roof; the worship pavilion almost fills the courtyard, with simple structure and plain generosity; the main hall is two stories, with Confucius in the main position upstairs and Lord Guan downstairs — a symbol of the village.

The Liang Clan Ancestral Hall is the core of local residents' lives, also known as Yuqi Hall, north of the Wenwu Temple.

The ancestral hall entrance faces east, toward the main road, with gate towers built on both the left and right, solemnly proclaiming its territory and also occupying a section of the main road.

The ancestral hall's main seat is one courtyard, with no blockage in the courtyard, so that clan members can hold public discussions and sacrifices here.

On the south wall in front of the ancestral hall mountain, a "Prohibition Stele" jointly erected by the whole township in 1809 (the 14th year of Jiaqing reign, Qing) is embedded; the front courtyard has facilities such as an arc-shaped stilt building facing backward and granaries.

推荐级别：★★★★★

中文 Chinese

在全国闻名的沙县，有一个大水湾村，村中坐落着一座古宅，叫陈氏大厝，当地人称其为"孝子坊"。"孝子坊"始建于清乾隆年间，主人是"儒学正堂"陈宗诰，后来道光皇帝钦赐"孝子"二字，大概是讲究儒学的人在孝道上也是足以为人表率。进入不大的正门，里面是一块开阔的广场。正值农历七月十五中元节，老人赶来祖屋祭祖。

古宅内部由并列三进二天井的院落组成，虽然年代久远，略显破败，但给人感觉气魄宏大，非一般民居可比。大厅内部高大恢宏，梁架厚重，...

English

In the nationally famous Shaxian County, there is a Dachshuiwan Village, in which sits an ancient mansion called the Chen Family Mansion, locally known as the "Filial Son Archway.

" The "Filial Son Archway" was first built during the Qianlong reign of the Qing; its master was Chen Zonggao, the "Official of Confucian Learning," and later the Daoguang Emperor imperially bestowed the two characters "Filial Son" — probably because someone who values Confucian learning is also exemplary in filial piety.

Entering the not-large main gate, inside is an open square.

It was the Zhongyuan Festival (Ghost Festival) on the 15th day of the seventh lunar month, and elderly people came to the ancestral house to worship ancestors.

The interior of the ancient mansion consists of three parallel courtyards with two skylights; although old and slightly dilapidated, it gives a feeling of grandeur, incomparable to ordinary residences.

The interior of the main hall is tall and magnificent, with heavy beam frames, ...

水美堡

No.165
Shuimei Fort
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明沙县水美村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
土堡与土楼的不同乡村生活三座相距不远土堡清道光后始建一大两小相互呼应同一家族最大土堡位于村口保存最完整堡后土楼围墙掩映花木中
中文 Chinese

沙县的水美村有三座相距不远的土堡，始建于清道光之后，一大两小相互呼应，属于同一家族。最大的土堡位于村口，保存也最完整。堡后身的土楼和围墙掩映在花木之中，似乎与当初剑拔弩张的岁月已经完全没有关系。

堡的外面紧邻的民居，构成小巷，巷中堆满日常劳作之物，一派温馨的景象；堡的正门，悬字"奠厥攸居"，同治元年立，东门悬"磐安"石匾，图的就是安定。进入堡内幽暗的门洞，忽然下起雨来，有女主人跑出来，见有外人在此，遂用普通话高喊"下雨了"，冲出堡外去收东西。进入门内是轩敞的大厅和大块的空地，有种豁然开朗的感觉。再里边的庭院虽不算十分宏大，也是十分精致规整。

南方的庭院就是为雨准备的，此时的雨淅淅沥沥落在院中，不由坐在廊下细听雨声。有年头的长凳，大食堂时期的遗物吧？老人就是从那个时代走来的吧？歇一歇，反思一下。堡内的厅堂相连，往复沟通，外人进来容易迷失，正惊讶于厅堂之构造为何如此相似，相似到同一位置摆放同一把竹椅，后来才发现这个院子刚才来过。在堡内穿梭，没有其他的游人，偶尔传来屋内人们的零星话语，或是灶间做饭的声音，饭菜的香气随之在堡内弥漫。

向村中走去，一大块稻田的两边有两个比较小的土堡遥遥相对，像是兄弟二人。其中的一座正面的堡墙已经塌了，不过里面的房屋保存尚好。今天是中元节，屋内的父子二人在准备祭品，儿子似乎执意要什么东西，不依不饶的，父亲在不断开导之，也是其乐融融。

狗儿见有生人来，跑出来大叫，后来发现我既不怕它，也不讨厌它，又表现得十分友好，我走到哪里始终跟随左右，小动物的感情也很丰富。内部的小空间同大同小异了，不同的是时间和心情。

English

Shuimei Village in Shaxian County has three earth forts not far apart, first built after the Daoguang reign of the Qing; one large and two small echo each other, belonging to the same family.

The largest earth fort is located at the village entrance and is also the best preserved.

The earth building and wall behind the fort are shaded by flowers and trees, seeming to have completely no relation to the originally tense and confrontational years.

The residences immediately outside the fort form alleys, piled with daily labor objects, a warm scene; the main gate of the fort bears the inscription "Establishing Their Dwelling," erected in the first year of Tongzhi reign, and the east gate bears a stone plaque "Rock-Solid Peace," aiming for stability.

Entering the dark gate tunnel inside the fort, it suddenly started raining; a hostess ran out, seeing outsiders here, then shouted in Mandarin "it's raining," and rushed out of the fort to collect things.

Inside the gate is a spacious hall and large open ground, with a feeling of sudden openness.The courtyard further inside, though not very grand, is also very exquisite and regular.

Southern courtyards are prepared for rain; at this moment the rain patters down in the courtyard, and one cannot help but sit under the corridor listening carefully to the sound of rain.

An aged long bench, a relic from the big canteen era?The elderly must have come from that era?Rest a while, reflect.

The halls inside the fort are connected, communicating back and forth; outsiders can easily get lost, just wondering why the hall structures are so similar — similar to the same bamboo chair placed in the same position — only later realizing this courtyard was visited before.

Wandering inside the fort, there are no other tourists; occasionally scattered words from people inside, or the sound of cooking in the kitchen, with the aroma of food filling the fort.

Walking toward the village, on both sides of a large rice paddy, two relatively small earth forts face each other from afar, like two brothers.

The front wall of one of them has already collapsed, but the houses inside are still well preserved.

Today is the Zhongyuan Festival; the father and son inside are preparing sacrificial offerings, the son seems insistent on something, refusing to let go, and the father keeps guiding him — also a scene of harmony.

The dog, seeing a stranger, ran out barking; later finding that I neither feared it nor disliked it, it became very friendly, always following me wherever I went — the emotions of small animals are also very rich.

The small spaces inside are more or less the same; what differs is time and mood.

推荐级别：★★★

大腹圳

No.166
Dafuzhen Ancient Vernacular Dwellings
级别：县级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明市尤溪县梅仙镇上洋村
类型：宗教建筑·木结构
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木作与装饰乡村生活又名大福圳清同治九年始建光绪十三年完成占地七千余平方米
中文 Chinese

大腹圳又名大福圳，一大片端庄的古建筑静卧于省道边的村口。这里的古宅始建于清同治九年，清光绪十三年完成，占地面积七千余平方米，当初的主人据说是经营木材生意的富商。古宅是由并排相连的四处院落组成，几处院门相互错落，并不排成直线，最旁边的一处院落规模较大，门口的位置也突出一些。

从大门向里面望去，古宅的细节之处已是难免破败，但格局宛然，特别是保存完好的石作，透露出一股雍容之气。从堂屋回望，是一块平整的田地；堂屋的屋顶上寄居了成群的麻雀，扑啦啦扇动翅膀飞来飞去，这样一幅景象也许是当初辉煌一时的主人所想不到的。尤溪处于福建西部，已经渐近比较偏远的山区，所以这里的宅院也兼具"堡"的性质，外形坚固而内部则四通八达。

古宅的规模很大，通过这种长长的走廊相通；这里也让人联想起连江地区的郑氏三落厝，结构庞大，狭小的空间内，景致非凡；建筑细节处的做工也很讲究，精致的木雕、石刻、彩绘随处可见。不过这些上佳的工艺在福建地区的大宅中已经是司空见惯。寂寞空旷古宅中，不时传来人说话的声音和做饭烧菜的声音，但又似乎不知道人在哪里。

在这样的廊椅上闲坐，凉爽的穿堂风吹来一扫暑热。忽闻人声由远及近，原来是这里的主人一家四口，两个小孩子好奇地看着我，女主人则非常热情地招呼"老板在这里参观呀，要不要进来喝点水"云云，其举止得体，热情好礼，甚有大家之风。笔者客气谢过，说话间一家人又消失在古宅中，一切仍归寂静。不过古宅的少东家今天非常高兴，表演了一套拳法，自报家门虚岁9岁，马上上二年级。

孩子，他们手里是古宅的未来，他们已经能够感受生活的艰辛。风起云涌，暴雨就要来了。孩子，闻到树木的味道了吗？你们祖上经营木材，多么懂得木材处理的诀窍啊，老木屋多漂亮啊……

English

Dafuzhen, also known as Dafuzhen, is a large expanse of dignified ancient buildings quietly lying at the village entrance by the provincial road.

The ancient mansion here was first built in the ninth year of Tongzhi reign of the Qing and completed in the 13th year of Guangxu reign, covering over 7,000 square meters; the original owner is said to have been a wealthy merchant in the timber business.

The ancient mansion consists of four side-by-side connected courtyards, with several gateways staggered against each other, not arranged in a straight line; the courtyard at the far side is larger in scale, with its gate position also more prominent.

Looking inward from the main gate, the details of the ancient mansion are inevitably dilapidated, but the layout remains intact, especially the well-preserved stonework, revealing an air of grace and dignity.

Looking back from the main hall, there is a flat field; on the roof of the main hall, flocks of sparrows have taken up residence, fluttering their wings and flying about — such a scene perhaps was unimaginable to the originally glorious owner.

Youxi is in western Fujian, already approaching the more remote mountainous areas, so the residences here also have the nature of a "fort," with a solid exterior and四通八达 interior.

The ancient mansion is very large, connected through such long corridors; this also reminds one of the Zheng Clan's Three-Layer Residence in Lianjiang area, with a massive structure and extraordinary scenery within narrow spaces; the workmanship at architectural details is also exquisite, with fine wood carvings, stone carvings, and painted decorations everywhere.

However, such excellent craftsmanship is already commonplace in the large mansions of Fujian.

In the lonely and empty ancient mansion, from time to time come the sounds of people talking and cooking, but it seems unknown where the people are.

Sitting idly on such a corridor chair, the cool cross-breeze blows away the summer heat.

Suddenly hearing voices approaching from far to near, it turned out to be the owner's family of four here; the two children looked at me curiously, while the hostess very warmly greeted "Boss, are you visiting here, would you like to come in for some water" and so on; her demeanor was appropriate, warm and courteous, quite with the air of a great family.

The author politely thanked, and as we spoke the family disappeared into the ancient mansion again, everything returning to silence.

However, the young master of the ancient mansion was very happy today, performing a set of boxing techniques, introducing himself as 9 years old by nominal age, about to enter second grade.

Children, what they hold in their hands is the future of the ancient mansion; they can already feel the hardships of life.Winds rise and clouds gather, a heavy storm is coming.

Children, can you smell the wood?Your ancestors dealt in timber, how well they understood the tricks of timber treatment, how beautiful the old wooden house is...

推荐级别：★★★

聚奎堡

No.167
Jukui Fort
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明市尤溪县中仙乡西华村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
古宅格局木、石作与装饰清代曾出现十名贡生三华地区东华西华华阳乡绅陈经正主人新修西华陈氏支谱
中文 Chinese

以防御为目的的大宅叫作堡也罢，堂也罢，并无实质差别。聚奎堡的名字来源于当地清代曾出现过十名贡生。尤溪中仙乡的东华、西华、华阳被称为三华地区，这里的乡绅陈经正就是此堡的主人。好在有《新修西华陈氏支谱》，里面记载了陈氏发迹的年代大致在乾隆年间。

陈经正在清乾隆年间（1736—1795年）营建了此宅，虽说他较有名的房屋就有龙德堂、新安堂和聚奎堂，所谓"狡兔三窟"，但属聚奎堂规模最大，占地面积6552平方米，建筑面积3000平方米。

道光二年（1822年），他出资翻盖年久衰颓的岭兜祖庙，谋划家族久安大计；道光十二年（1832年）复修大宅；太平天国之乱期间，始筑围墙为堡。聚奎堡整体上坐西朝东，门户严密。堡内有大小房间200余间、水井5个、藏物窑2个、射击孔60个、瞭望台3个、瞭望窗80个，具备抵御土匪和日常生活的双重功能。

走进大厅，一眼就可以看见依然高悬着的道光和光绪年间的"文魁"、"璧水声光"等5块匾额。堡中建筑多为两层，转折迂回，不自知间便迷失了方向，方知当时居民众多房屋充塞。据说，聚奎堡在民国的时候曾经抵抗了多次匪患，然终为土匪所据。不过，陈氏的子孙倒是十分坦然："如果不是土匪抢了聚奎堡，我们这些人可都成了地主，'文革'中或许就难逃劫难了……"

English

Large mansions built for defensive purposes, whether called fort (bao) or hall (tang), have no essential difference.

The name Jukui Fort originates from the fact that ten gongsheng (tribute students) once appeared locally in the Qing Dynasty.

Donghua, Xihua, and Huayang in Zhongxian Township of Youxi are called the Sanhua (Three Hua) region, and the local gentry Chen Jingzheng was the owner of this fort.

Fortunately, there is the "Newly Compiled Genealogy of the Chen Clan of Xihua," which records that the Chen clan's rise to prosperity was roughly during the Qianlong reign.

Chen Jingzheng built this residence during the Qianlong reign of the Qing (1736–1795); although his more famous houses included Longde Hall, Xin'an Hall, and Jukui Hall — the so-called "cunning rabbit has three burrows" — Jukui Hall was the largest in scale, covering 6,552 square meters with a building area of 3,000 square meters.

In 1822 (the second year of Daoguang reign), he funded the rebuilding of the dilapidated Lingdou Ancestral Temple, planning for the long-term security of the clan; in 1832 (the 12th year of Daoguang reign), he restored the large mansion; during the Taiping Rebellion, he began building walls to make it a fort.

Jukui Fort overall faces east from the west, with严密 gateways.

Inside the fort there are over 200 rooms of various sizes, 5 wells, 2 storage cellars, 60 shooting holes, 3 observation platforms, and 80 observation windows,具备 the dual functions of resisting bandits and daily life.

Entering the main hall, one can immediately see the five plaques from the Daoguang and Guangxu reigns still hanging high, such as "Wen Kui" (Literary Champion) and "Bi Shui Sheng Guang" (Jade Water Sound and Light).

The buildings in the fort are mostly two stories, with twists and turns; one unknowingly loses direction, only then realizing how many residents there were and how packed the houses were.

It is said that Jukui Fort resisted multiple bandit raids during the Republican period, but was eventually occupied by bandits.

However, the Chen descendants are quite calm: "If the bandits hadn't seized Jukui Fort, we would all have become landlords, and perhaps we wouldn't have escaped disaster during the Cultural Revolution.

.."

推荐级别：★★★

茂荆堡

No.168
Maojing Fort
级别：省级文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明市尤溪县台溪乡盖竹村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
土堡布局防御设施排水系统结构和装饰寻访途中人烟稀少树木繁茂亚热带植物大观园盖竹村盛产毛竹
中文 Chinese

寻访茂荆堡的途中，一路之上人烟稀少、树木繁茂，仿佛游走于亚热带植物的大观园。不时有黑瓦屋顶的老宅点缀其间，给一片碧绿的山景增色不少。茂荆堡所在的盖竹村很好找，跟着导航走就是了。村庄位于一条小河的两旁，有很多老民居，也有一些新房子。不过茂荆堡坐落于村子后面的山坡上，且平时是锁着的，有专人看管，因此到村头一定要打听一下。

这里的村民像闽西、闽北其他地方的村民一样都是非常淳朴热情的。有幸找到了茂荆堡的第五代传人和管理负责人陈先生。和他的祖先一样，陈先生现在的主业是乡间大夫。几分矜持加上几分高兴，陈先生知道我是特地来参观茂荆堡的，就像身藏宝贝而遇到远道而来寻访的人一样笑了。在他的热情带领下，茂荆堡逐渐露出了庐山真面目。

当我最终站在它的面前，还是不禁呆住了。据陈先生说他祖上是远近闻名的医生，但医生特别是过去的医生发不了大财，好在他的祖先兼具商业头脑。顾名思义，盖竹村一带盛产毛竹，可惜过去只会用土法制造烧纸钱用的纸张，形同浪费。其祖上将本地的毛竹或毛竹制品运到尤溪县城去，再将县城的商品转卖到当地，因而积累了大量财富。

正值清代同光年间，当地匪患较多，遂在村后的山上修建了规模宏大的茂荆堡，于1882年即清光绪八年竣工。建筑就像被赋予了生长的能力，和当地的风土环境息息相关，茂荆堡的营造可谓颇不负眼前这一番景色。大门很小，紧接着是高高的台阶，其紧凑严密与外面的景色形成强烈反差，很有些城堡的样子。

要再转过两个弯才能上到堡的正厅。虽然是壁垒森严，廊柱之间还是少不得雕梁画栋。从主人的视角望去，忽然意识到茂荆堡在坚固安全之外，应该还是有几分自矜和夸耀的成分。或者郎中先生使用了中医的理论，讲究固本，自己身体健壮、免疫力强，任你各种病毒来袭，我自不惧。不过自强过分容易变成自误，茂荆堡规模宏大，远近闻名，弄得十里八方的豪杰都想来一试身手，也够陈老一呛。这就是阴阳消长，物极必反，按西洋的词汇叫辩证法。

茂荆堡依山而建，其内部落差较大，比较险峻，建设必须注重细节之处：四处都有瞭望口，围墙内联设通道，供家丁巡逻之用，叫马道；雨水和生活污水的排放都是有讲究的；临窗而设的长椅，可以坐在上面休息聊天，不过整天...

English

On the way to visit Maojing Fort, along the road there were few people and lush trees, as if wandering in a grand garden of subtropical plants.

From time to time, old houses with black tile roofs dotted the landscape, adding much to the green mountain scenery.

Gaizhu Village, where Maojing Fort is located, is easy to find — just follow the navigation.The village is located on both sides of a small river, with many old residences and some new houses.

However, Maojing Fort sits on the hillside behind the village, and is usually locked with a dedicated caretaker, so one must definitely ask around at the village entrance.

The villagers here, like those in other parts of western and northern Fujian, are very simple and warm-hearted.I was fortunate to find Mr.

Chen, the fifth-generation descendant and management负责人 of Maojing Fort.Like his ancestors, Mr.Chen's main occupation now is a village doctor.With a touch of reserve and a touch of joy, Mr.

Chen, knowing I had come specially to visit Maojing Fort, smiled like someone hiding a treasure who meets a visitor from afar.

Under his enthusiastic guidance, Maojing Fort gradually revealed its true face.When I finally stood before it, I couldn't help but be stunned.According to Mr.

Chen, his ancestors were well-known doctors nearby, but doctors — especially doctors of the past — could not make great fortunes; fortunately, his ancestors also had a business mind.

As the name suggests, the Gaizhu Village area abounds in moso bamboo; unfortunately, in the past they only used indigenous methods to make paper for burning spirit money, which was tantamount to waste.

His ancestors transported local moso bamboo or bamboo products to Youxi County town, then resold county-town commodities locally, thus accumulating great wealth.

During the Tongzhi-Guangxu period of the Qing, there were many bandit problems locally, so they built the massive Maojing Fort on the mountain behind the village, completed in 1882 — the eighth year of Guangxu reign of the Qing.

The building seems endowed with the ability to grow, closely related to the local environment and customs; the construction of Maojing Fort can be said to live up to the scenery before one's eyes.

The main gate is very small, immediately followed by high steps; its compactness and tightness form a strong contrast with the scenery outside, quite like a castle.

One must turn two more corners to reach the main hall of the fort.

Although it is heavily fortified, between the corridors and columns there is no lack of carved beams and painted rafters.

Looking from the owner's perspective, one suddenly realizes that beyond solidity and security, Maojing Fort should still have some elements of self-praise and showing off.

Or perhaps the doctor used the theory of traditional Chinese medicine, emphasizing strengthening the foundation — with a robust body and strong immunity, no matter what viruses come, I fear nothing.

However, excessive self-strengthening can easily become self-defeating; Maojing Fort is massive and famous far and wide, making heroes from miles around want to test their skills, which was quite a handful for old Mr.

Chen.This is the waxing and waning of yin and yang, things reverse when they reach the extreme — in Western terms, dialectics.

Maojing Fort was built against the mountain, with a large internal drop and relatively steep terrain; construction had to pay attention to details: there are observation openings everywhere, and connected passages inside the walls for family guards to patrol, called horse roads (madao); the drainage of rainwater and domestic sewage is all carefully designed; long benches by the windows allow one to sit and rest and chat, though all day.

..

普通民居

No.169
Regular Vernacular Dwellings
级别：无
年代：明—清
地址：三明尤溪村落

特征标签 Highlights
民居格局结构工艺装饰做法探访古建筑途中被普通民居吸引楼堂庙宇豪门大宅是高雅牡丹荷花水仙普通民居是山间田中的野百合顽强生命力
中文 Chinese

在探访古建筑的途中，惊叹于那些楼堂庙宇、豪门大宅之余，往往被那些一闪即逝的普通民居所吸引。如果说前者是花园中高雅的牡丹、荷花、水仙，那么后者就是散落在山间田中的野百合，以顽强的生命力展示着另一种美。而且因为这些民居的就地取材，因地制宜，往往更能反映当地的建筑文化和风土人情。我们珍视的只有文物保护单位吗？第一个例子是彩洋村。厚丰村郑氏大厝西面的山中有一个彩洋水库，旁边坐落着安逸的小村庄。

坐在老房子的台基上水库的景色近在眼前。第二个实例是经通村，就在大腹圳古宅所不远的经通村，有很多古老的民居，或者说就是以前的村落，现在已经废弃了。不过从其个体和群体的规模还能想象当初村子的兴旺。不过现在的村子也很兴旺，只是故事已经发生在人们都搬去的新房子里了。还有桂峰村。桂峰村的古民居在当地也是很有名气，山地里夯土建筑和石作工艺非常出色，到处是厚重的石阶，常见这种门前的半圆形石基。

村中大姓蔡氏家庙规模宏大；废弃的书院中，仍然可见当初的设施，可以嗅到当初的气氛。经笔者探访，其实老房子大多地基完整，而且里面高大宽敞，冬暖夏凉，但还是难以摆脱被闲置甚至拆除的命运。其实我们抛弃的不是老房子，而是要追求塑造一种新的价值体系，可谁能对乡亲们说清楚那是什么呢？

English

In the course of visiting ancient buildings, while marveling at those halls, temples, and grand mansions, one is often attracted by those fleeting ordinary vernacular dwellings.

If the former are the elegant peonies, lotuses, and narcissus in a garden, then the latter are the wild lilies scattered in the mountains and fields, displaying another kind of beauty with tenacious vitality.

And because these dwellings use local materials and adapt to local conditions, they often better reflect the local architectural culture and customs.

Do we only cherish cultural heritage protection units?The first example is Caiyang Village.

In the mountains west of the Zheng Clan Mansion in Houfeng Village, there is a Caiyang Reservoir, next to which sits a cozy small village.

Sitting on the foundation of an old house, the reservoir scenery is right before one's eyes.

The second example is Jingtong Village, not far from the Dafuzhen ancient mansion; there are many ancient dwellings, or rather former villages, now abandoned.

However, from the scale of individuals and groups, one can still imagine the prosperity of the village in those days.

But the current village is also prosperous, except that the stories now happen in the new houses where people have moved.There is also Guifeng Village.

The ancient dwellings of Guifeng Village are also quite famous locally; the rammed-earth architecture and stone craftsmanship in the mountains are excellent, with heavy stone steps everywhere, and this kind of semicircular stone foundation in front of doors is common.

The large surname in the village, the Cai Clan Ancestral Temple, is massive in scale; in the abandoned academy, the original facilities can still be seen, and one can smell the atmosphere of those days.

After the author's visits, in fact most old houses have complete foundations, and the interiors are tall and spacious, warm in winter and cool in summer, but they still cannot escape the fate of being left idle or even demolished.

In fact, what we are abandoning is not the old houses, but the pursuit of shaping a new value system — but who can explain clearly to the villagers what that is?

推荐级别：★★★★★

中文 Chinese

尤溪地处闽地西部山区，这里比较偏僻，若逢乱世则匪盗盛行，因此这里的大户人家在营建大宅的时候就比较注重防御功能，其特点是规模巨大，可容上百人阖族而居，同时有比较高大严密的围墙，形成一种独特的建筑形式。不过将这种形制的大宅称为"土堡"，低估了生活，似乎有点不伦不类。

书京村有相邻的两座土堡——瑞庆堡和光裕堡，属于同一家族，可以称为父子堡，分别兴建于清代道光和咸丰年间。位于下面山谷间平地上的子堡瑞庆堡，大门外旗杆座上主人姓名和咸丰纪年清晰可见。大门前一片寂静，堡的主人一...

English

Youxi is located in the western mountainous area of Fujian, relatively remote; in troubled times bandits and robbers prevailed, so the wealthy families here paid more attention to defensive functions when building large mansions.

Their characteristic is massive scale, capable of accommodating over a hundred people of the whole clan living together, while having relatively tall and tight enclosure walls, forming a unique architectural form.

However, calling this type of large mansion an "earthen fort" (tubao) underestimates the life within, seeming somewhat inappropriate.

In Shujing Village there are two adjacent earthen forts — Ruiqing Fort and Guangyu Fort — belonging to the same clan, which can be called father-and-son forts, built respectively during the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns of the Qing.

The son's fort, Ruiqing Fort, located on flat ground in the valley below, has the owner's name and the Xianfeng reign year clearly visible on the flagpole base outside the main gate.

In front of the main gate is一片 silence, and the fort's owner...

玉井坊郑氏大厝

No.171
Yujingfang Zheng's Family Mansion
级别：全国重点文物保护单位
年代：清
地址：三明市尤溪县西滨镇厚丰村
类型：民居
特征标签 Highlights
建筑组合和多层建筑设计大木结构木雕、石雕、彩画装饰深藏苍翠中尤溪县西滨镇西部山中厚丰村构筑奢华郑氏大厝也叫郑孔时公大厝乾隆四十五年1780年始建历时十余年完成
中文 Chinese

深藏在一片苍翠中，尤溪县西滨镇西部山中的厚丰村原本默默无闻，让它出名的是村中的一座构筑奢华的郑氏大厝，也叫（郑）孔时公大厝。大厝始建于乾隆四十五年（1780年），历时十余年完成，道光年间增建护厝数间，并进行了维修，后亦有增容维护之举。

大厝平面呈方形圆角，通面阔45米，通进深50米，建筑最高处三层，至高点13米，平实无华大门丝毫也不会给整体的巍峨壮观减色半分。很有幸在大厝的大门口遇到了郑氏大厝的管理者季先生，一位和善的老者，如果60岁算老的话。

他当时正在忙于竖立"国宝碑"，因为郑氏大厝作为最新一批国家级文保单位已经获批了，季先生掩饰不住的高兴。看我远道而来，季先生热情地进行讲解，他对大厝的里里外外可说是如数家珍。很奇怪他虽自称是一普通农人，但他的普通话讲得很好，而且条理清楚，时不时让我感觉是一位大学里常见的操着南方口音的老师。建筑为歇山顶控制全局，坐北朝南。

主体建筑由正厝、横厝和左右壁舍所组成。平面由一横厝、二壁舍、二厢房、三厅堂及九个过水亭连接，构成一个建筑整体。里面近祖堂、远祖堂、后楼、后花园，...

English

Deeply hidden in a sea of green, Houfeng Village in the western mountains of Xibin Town, Youxi County, was originally unknown; what made it famous was a luxuriously constructed Zheng Clan Mansion in the village, also called (Zheng) Kongshi Gong Mansion.

The mansion was first built in the 45th year of Qianlong reign (1780), taking over ten years to complete; during the Daoguang reign, several side wings (hucuo) were added and repairs were carried out, with later expansions and maintenance as well.

The mansion plan is square with rounded corners, with a total width of 45 meters and total depth of 50 meters; the highest point of the building is three stories, reaching 13 meters at the apex.

The plain and unadorned main gate in no way detracts from the overall majestic grandeur.I was fortunate to meet Mr.

Ji, the manager of the Zheng Mansion, at the main gate — a kind elderly gentleman, if 60 counts as old.

He was busy erecting the "National Treasure Stele," because the Zheng Mansion had just been approved as the latest batch of national-level cultural heritage protection units, and Mr.

Ji could not hide his joy.Seeing me come from afar, Mr.Ji enthusiastically gave explanations; he knew the mansion inside and out like the back of his hand.

Strangely, although he called himself an ordinary farmer, his Mandarin was very good and well-organized, from time to time making me feel like a common university teacher with a southern accent.

The building uses a hip-and-gable roof (xieshan ding) to control the overall composition, facing south.

The main building consists of the central residence (zhengcuo), side residences (hengcuo), and left and right wall houses (bishe).

The plan is connected by one side residence, two wall houses, two wing rooms, three halls, and nine water-passing pavilions (guoshui ting), forming an architectural whole.

Inside there are the near ancestral hall, far ancestral hall, rear building, and rear garden...
